18096363515306860.summary: A woman in a modern white kitchen introduces a recipe for panjeeri laddoo, a traditional South Asian sweet. She explains she has loved it since childhood and that her mother-in-law made it generously after her son was born, noting its reputed benefits for bone health, immunity, digestion, and postpartum recovery, and that it is enjoyed in winter with chai or milk. Laid out on the counter are numerous ingredients in bowls: ghee, jaggery syrup, makhana (fox nuts), mixed nuts (almonds, walnuts, pistachios, cashews), sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, sooji, besan, coconut, raisins, and gond. She proceeds step-by-step: dissolving jaggery in water to make a syrup, then roasting each ingredient separately in ghee on low heat—raisins, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, gond, sooji/besan mixture, mixed nuts, shredded coconut, and finally makhana—to prevent burning. All roasted components are combined in a large glass bowl, cooled, then pulsed in a food processor to a coarse consistency. She pours the warm jaggery syrup over the mixture, stirs thoroughly, and then hand-rolls the warm mass into round laddoos, placing them on a gold tray. The video ends with her holding a finished laddoo, taking a bite, and expressing enjoyment, presenting the final batch of approximately 25 laddoos.

17993333604049739.summary: A woman in a red-and-white striped shirt prepares a black sesame latte in a bright kitchen setting. The video opens with close-ups of a pink ceramic mug filled with a frothy grey drink topped with black sesame seeds, overlaid with text reading 'FEED HER FIRST' and 'Welcome to feed her first.' She explains via voiceover that this is simple nourishment for the postpartum month, created by a chef who understands how mothers often forget themselves while caring for a baby. She demonstrates making the drink: pouring milk into a metal frothing pitcher, adding Clearspring Organic Black Tahini, and mixing in a dark syrup (likely date or maple). The mixture is frothed, poured into the pink mug, and topped with more black sesame seeds. On-screen text highlights that black sesame is rich in iron, zinc, and healthy fats, and is perfect for postpartum recovery. The woman tastes the drink, expressing enjoyment. The tone is nurturing, educational, and focused on maternal self-care, with the creator promising the full recipe in the caption.

18063959687688894.summary: This social media video presents a health tip from the perspective of an expert for women in their third trimester of pregnancy and those who are postpartum or breastfeeding. The creator, a woman in a kitchen, is demonstrating the preparation of a remedy intended to maximize iron absorption. She carefully pours a red liquid from a saucepan through a funnel into a glass carafe. This visual action directly illustrates the concept she is verbally explaining in the audio. Her calm and informative tone aims to establish trust with her audience. The overall purpose is educational, providing practical advice on nutrition during a critical phase of motherhood.

17867429825947412.summary: The video follows a couple as they attempt to recreate a recipe for fried green onions that they saw on a social media platform. The video begins with them watching the recipe video, where a hand is shown cutting green onions. They then transition to their own kitchen, where they gather the ingredients, including flour, spices, and beer. The man measures the ingredients into a bowl while the woman assists. They then proceed to coat the green onions in the batter and fry them. Finally, they sit down to eat the finished product, dipping the fried green onions in truffle butter. They both express their enjoyment of the dish, indicating that the recipe was a success. The overall tone of the video is positive and informative, with the creators sharing their experience of trying a new recipe.

18021869069894508.summary: This is a short-form cooking video by creator @shishisimple demonstrating a simple recipe for fresh herb rice. The video opens with close-ups of finished rice mixed with green ingredients, overlaid with text "This changed my rice forever" and "Better than Chipotle rice." The creator adds shelled edamame to hot steamed rice in a black pot, then chops fresh cilantro and scallions on a wooden board. She squeezes lime (or lemon) juice over the mixture, sprinkles salt, and drizzles olive oil. On-screen text labels each ingredient in English and Chinese. She mixes everything together with a white spatula, describing the result as "Fresh, zesty, addictive." The rice is then molded into a bowl and served on a blue-patterned plate alongside ground meat, sliced cucumber, tomato, and avocado. The creator, wearing a striped shirt and brown apron, holds up the plate, eats the rice with chopsticks, and smiles. Text encourages viewers to save the recipe. The video has a bright, cheerful instrumental soundtrack and is presented as an easy, healthy summer dish inspired by @plantbasedrd, suitable for cilantro lovers with arugula offered as an alternative.

18028712588909488.summary:
The video opens with a close-up of a finished microwave cake being served in a bowl with custard poured over it. The creator, a young man with a mustache wearing a white t-shirt, explains via voiceover that this simple microwave cake 'genuinely changed my life' and helped him win the Cake Week technical challenge on the Great British Bake Off. He credits learning the recipe from his mum, calling it the first recipe he memorized and a source of pure nostalgia.

The video cuts to clips from the Bake Off tent showing judges and contestants, then returns to the kitchen where the man and his blonde mother prepare the cake together. Following the classic 'equal weights' method, they crack eggs into a glass bowl on a scale, then add the same weight of flour, butter, and sugar, plus vanilla extract. They mix everything in the bowl without creaming, pour in honey, and microwave it. While it cooks, they prepare a quick custard sauce on the stove.

After microwaving, they serve the sponge in a bowl, top it with jam and custard, and taste it together with exaggerated enjoyment. The creator frames the recipe as the start of a new series called 'Foods From My Life,' suggesting it represents where his love of baking began. The overall tone is affectionate, nostalgic, and encouraging, aimed at home bakers.

17850106815564338.summary: This is a step-by-step cooking tutorial presented by a woman in a kitchen with a green wall backdrop. The video demonstrates how to prepare a layered, savory rice dish, likely a type of Indian 'poha' or 'upma'. The process begins with chopping fresh vegetables like onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers. Next, a sauce is made by toasting spices like cumin seeds and dried chilies, then blending them into a paste. The final dish is assembled by layering cooked rice, puffed rice, the chopped vegetables, and the prepared sauce in a clear container, creating a colorful and appetizing meal. The host presents the finished dish, emphasizing its appeal and convenience for meal prepping.

18091495088660876.summary: The video is a POV-style cooking demonstration set in a home kitchen with a wooden cutting board. On-screen text reads 'POV: you've waited all year for this.' The creator prepares smoky fig bruschetta: whole fresh figs are sliced in half, then cooked in a pan with honey, minced garlic, red pepper flakes, and fresh rosemary until caramelized and bubbling. A sprig of rosemary is briefly torched over the pan for smoke. Separately, Lifeway Farmer Cheese is placed in a bowl, mixed with lemon zest and black pepper. The finished dish is assembled by spreading the whipped cheese on a plate, topping with the hot honey figs and their sauce, and sprinkling chopped pistachios. For serving, the mixture is piled onto toasted baguette slices topped with prosciutto. The creator, a man with tattoos wearing a striped shirt, holds the plate and takes a bite, expressing enjoyment. The tone is enthusiastic and instructional, promoting the seasonal fall recipe.

18146387797604301.summary: A creator demonstrates making 'Whipped Ricotta Toast with garlic confit, lemon pesto, & honey.' The video opens with close-ups of the finished toast on a black plate, topped with piped whipped ricotta, spooned yellow garlic confit, and drizzled honey. The creator, a woman with long dark hair wearing a black knit top, holds the toast and takes bites while describing it as 'outrageously good' and something she 'cannot stop thinking about.' Flashback shots show the preparation: peeled garlic cloves placed in a pink Staub pot, covered with oil and rosemary sprigs to make confit; ricotta scooped into a small blender cup with olive oil and salt, then blended into a smooth whipped texture; toasted sourdough rubbed with confit garlic and olive oil, then topped with the whipped ricotta, lemon pesto, and honey. On-screen text reinforces the recipe name and steps. The overall tone is upbeat, appetizing, and promotional of the flavor combination.

18035502020899937.summary: A woman in a home kitchen presents her 'Bites on Bites' series featuring raspberry pistachio smash dates. She holds up the finished treat — a flattened date topped with green pistachio butter, red raspberry jam, and dark chocolate — and explains this is a weekly-prep snack. The video then shows the step-by-step process: taking Medjool dates from a container, removing the pits, placing them on parchment paper and smashing them flat with the bottom of a glass jar. She spreads a thick layer of pistachio butter onto each smashed date, then spoons homemade raspberry chia jam over the top. Next, she stirs melted chocolate in a bowl and spoons it over the jam layer, finishing with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. Returning to camera, she tastes the bite, makes an 'OK' hand gesture, and describes how the flavors pair perfectly together. The tone is friendly, instructional, and enthusiastic, aimed at sharing an easy, sweet snack recipe.

18040873955838725.summary: A woman in a home kitchen begins her morning at 6:00 am with a brief prayer gesture before cooking. On-screen text describes the activity as 'Prayer, Lunchbox and protein Goodness.' She prepares a flatbread by combining Rajgara (amaranth) flour with mashed boiled sweet potato, cottage cheese, chopped cilantro, ajwain, cumin powder, black pepper, salt, wheat flour, and sesame seeds. After adding water and kneading a soft dough, she lets it rest for 15-20 minutes, then portions, rolls out, and cooks the paratha on a hot tawa over a gas flame, applying oil or ghee. The finished bread is described as 'High protein, Iron, Calcium rich Softest parantha.' She folds it and packs it into a stainless steel lunchbox alongside red grapes, yogurt, and pumpkin seeds. The video ends with her smiling and performing a namaste, with text encouraging viewers to follow for more healthy recipes.

18080840567526815.summary: The video is a short, visually pleasing cooking clip with on-screen text stating, 'That packet of carrots in my fridge was staring at me for a week. So I made this.' It shows the process of making pickled carrots in a clear glass jar. A person's hands add sliced orange carrots, whole garlic cloves, and green chilies into the jar, followed by a spoonful of salt and a pour of amber-colored liquid (likely vinegar) and then water. The contents are stirred with a wooden utensil, and the jar is sealed with a glass lid. The setting is bright with sunlight casting leaf shadows, and includes decorative elements like white lilies and a lit candle in the background. The watermark '@thesoulfulplates' is visible throughout. The audio is a gentle solo piano instrumental with no speech.

18172845739456297.summary: The video is a short, visually-focused cooking clip set to gentle piano music, with the recurring on-screen text 'Me at least once a week' suggesting it's a favorite comfort food. It opens with a close-up of a finished grilled cheese sandwich on a white plate with red trim, being cut in half to reveal a dramatic cheese pull. The process then rewinds to show preparation: thinly sliced shallots are sautéed in butter in a pan, seasoned with spices, salt, and a touch of sugar and water to caramelize them. Assembly takes place in the same pan: one slice of bread is topped with shredded cheese and caramelized onions, while another slice is spread with green pesto, topped with more onions and fresh mozzarella slices. The sandwich is pressed and grilled until the bread is golden-brown and crispy. The video concludes by returning to the plated sandwich, pulling it apart again to emphasize the melted, stretchy cheese and savory filling. The overall tone is cozy, appetizing, and satisfying.

18120176459319372.summary: A person prepares jalapeño cream cheese pinwheels in a kitchen with a white countertop and blue tile backsplash. Starting with a sheet of puff pastry on a wooden board, they spread Philadelphia cream cheese over it, then layer sliced Mezzetta tamed jalapeño peppers and shredded cheese. The pastry is rolled tightly, sliced into rounds, and placed on a parchment-lined baking sheet. An egg wash is brushed on top before baking. After baking, the pinwheels are golden brown with melted cheese and visible jalapeños. The creator finishes them by drizzling Mike's Hot Honey over each one, then breaks one open to show the gooey interior. On-screen text throughout reads 'pov: you're a little snackie before dinner every night type of girl.' The tone is casual, appetizing, and focused on an easy appetizer recipe.

18128469355875831.summary: A young man in a red-and-blue checkered shirt and backward cap sits at a restaurant table and explains his method for making 'real aglio e olio.' He states that the dish should finish without leaving a puddle of oil on the plate. The video cuts between him talking and close-up kitchen shots: cold olive oil poured into a pan, minced garlic added to infuse flavor, then chili flakes, cooked slowly to avoid bitterness. Half-cooked pasta is transferred from boiling water into the pan, where about 70% of the cooking finishes by tossing it in the garlic-chili oil so it absorbs the flavors. A splash of starchy pasta water is added to create a smooth, creamy sauce rather than an oily pool. The finished pasta is plated, topped with chopped parsley and grated cheese. He invites viewers to try the dish at Ameretti Artisan's Kitchen, noting they will find a big difference. The tone is instructional and promotional.

18095405213239654.summary: A woman in a modern home kitchen presents her favorite weeknight dinner: miso salmon. She opens by stating the dish cooks in under 15 minutes and makes great leftovers. While preparing the marinade in a glass measuring cup, she adds miso paste, then pours in sesame oil, mirin, and soy sauce, explaining that keeping these pantry staples made cooking less intimidating. She grates fresh ginger into the mixture and stirs it together. Holding a toddler, she pours the marinade over raw salmon fillets in a glass dish. The video shows rice being rinsed, then the salmon placed on a foil-lined tray going into a countertop oven set to broil at 450°F for 10-15 minutes until caramelized and crispy. Finished fillets are shown plated over white rice with broccolini, and also served to the toddler mixed with rice. She notes the dish is easy to serve over rice or salad, and that her husband, toddler, and she all love it.

18118557853767103.summary: A woman with short dark hair wearing a navy blue knit cardigan stands in a bright home kitchen and prepares a simple meal described as 'chili crisp eggs over hot buttered rice.' She begins by cracking two brown eggs into a white bowl. She then transfers steaming white rice into a larger floral-patterned bowl, adds a pat of butter, and stirs it in. Next, she heats oil in a stainless steel pan, pours in the two eggs, and fries them sunny-side-up until the whites set while keeping the yolks runny, seasoning with black pepper. She slides the fried eggs onto the buttered rice. For toppings, she shaves thin pieces of Parmesan cheese over the eggs, spoons on red chili crisp from a jar labeled 'Fly By Jing,' sprinkles chopped green scallions, and drizzles soy sauce. Close-up shots show the finished bowl with vibrant orange yolks, melted cheese, and chili oil. She then eats the dish with a fork, chews, and smiles at the camera before waving goodbye. The audio narration frames the dish as an easy, comforting 'go-to simple girl dinner' and 'the ultimate expression of self-love when you want to make yourself something lovely with little to no effort.' The tone is calm, warm, and instructional.

18072985289756962.summary: A woman wearing pink striped pajamas and glasses presents a step-by-step tutorial for making homemade cultured butter. The video opens with her enjoying a breakfast of soft-boiled eggs, fresh figs, sourdough toast with butter, and a latte made with an espresso machine. She explains that she has been eating the same breakfast daily and recently discovered how to make cultured butter. The process shown includes pouring heavy cream into a glass bowl, adding a spoonful of yogurt or kefir as a starter culture, mixing gently, covering with a kitchen towel, and letting it ferment at room temperature for 24 to 48 hours until thick and scoopable. She then whips the cultured cream with an electric hand mixer until it separates into solid butter and liquid buttermilk, which she saves. The butter is transferred to a bowl of ice water, kneaded by hand to wash out remaining buttermilk, then placed in a separate bowl where salt is added and mixed in. She shapes the finished butter into a log, wraps it in parchment paper, and stores it. The video concludes with her slicing the fresh butter onto toast, assembling her breakfast plate again, and drinking her coffee, emphasizing the satisfaction of making something from scratch.

18086487293636537.summary: A female creator, identified as Kelly Scott (@kellyscleankitchen), demonstrates how to make a classic French lemon butter sauce called beurre au citron. Speaking directly to camera in a home kitchen with green tile backsplash, she explains the technique while preparing asparagus. She starts by blanching purple and green asparagus spears in boiling water, then finishes them in a pan with butter and salt over medium heat. After adding fresh lemon juice and bringing it to a bubble, she removes the asparagus to reserve it. With the heat off, she whisks in several tablespoons of cold butter piece by piece, explaining that the cold butter emulsifies with the lemon juice to create a thick, creamy sauce without cream. She seasons with salt, stirs in fresh herbs like dill or parsley, and then spoons the finished yellow, herb-flecked sauce generously over the plated asparagus. The tone is educational and enthusiastic, emphasizing how easy the sauce is to elevate fish, vegetables, or other ingredients. On-screen text and captions promote her newsletter and recipe website.

18123830731841952.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video demonstrating how to make a seasonal appetizer described as a 'showstopper' — a whipped goat cheese and cream cheese dip topped with a sweet-savory pistachio and dried cherry mixture. The creator begins by whipping together blocks of cream cheese and goat cheese in a glass bowl using a KitchenAid hand mixer, then adds honey and blends until smooth before spreading the mixture into a serving bowl. Separately, on a stovetop, she melts butter, then adds brown sugar and more honey, whisking until combined. She then stirs in chopped pistachios and dried cherries, cooking them briefly in the buttery glaze. The hot topping is poured over the whipped cheese base, followed by fresh orange zest grated on top. The finished dip is shown being served with crackers and pretzels on a wooden board, with a hand scooping some onto a cracker to display the texture. The tone is instructional and inviting, focused entirely on food preparation.

18632498812054543.summary: A man wearing a black 'DAVILA'S' t-shirt stands in a commercial kitchen and presents a blueberry burrata dish. He explains it is not on the restaurant menu but a recipe he is sharing for viewers to make at home. The video shows him preparing a blueberry compote by combining fresh blueberries, brown sugar, honey, chopped shallots, fresh thyme, and red pepper flakes in a pan, then cooking it down. He plates fresh burrata cheese, spoons the cooked blueberry mixture over it, and garnishes with crushed pistachios, torn basil leaves, and grated lemon zest, finishing with a drizzle of olive oil. Toasted focaccia bread is served alongside. He demonstrates eating the dish by topping a piece of focaccia with the burrata and blueberries, encouraging viewers to try it themselves. The tone is instructional and friendly.

18132897259741249.summary: A woman in a home kitchen prepares a holiday onion dip. The video opens with her slicing a white onion on a wooden board, with text overlay reading 'me every holiday' and crying emojis, referencing the common experience of tearing up while chopping onions. She then transfers the sliced onions to a hot pan and sautés them until deeply caramelized and browned. In a white serving dish, she combines Hellmann's mayonnaise and Oikos Pro plain Greek yogurt, adds the cooked onions, pours in Worcestershire sauce, and thoroughly mixes everything into a creamy dip. She finishes by sprinkling chopped green onions on top as garnish. The tone is casual, relatable, and instructional, typical of social media food content.

18101211488302338.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates how to make her personal version of chili oil udon noodles. She begins by finely chopping garlic, ginger, cilantro, and spring onions, then prepares a sauce in a small bowl combining soy sauce, black rice vinegar, mirin (or honey), and Japanese sake or Chinese cooking wine, plus chili oil which she tastes and finds very spicy. She cooks the aromatics in a wok with oil, adds tomato paste and chili powder to create a red oil, pours in the sauce, then tosses in pre-cooked udon noodles to absorb the flavor. She finishes with a squeeze of lemon or lime juice and the fresh herbs. After plating, she eats the noodles with chopsticks, expressing enjoyment and noting they are also good cold from the fridge. A fluffy gray cat named Bean briefly interrupts her while she is preparing the chili oil. The tone is casual, instructional, and enthusiastic.

18145238710600807.summary: A person demonstrates how to make a homemade lemon basil vinaigrette in a kitchen setting. The video opens with a close-up of a finished green dressing in a glass jar, then shows the preparation process: olive oil is poured into a measuring cup, followed by mustard, vinegar, grated cheese, garlic, and fresh basil leaves. An immersion blender (Breville brand) is used to emulsify the ingredients into a creamy green sauce, which is then poured back into the jar. On-screen text and voiceover explain that restaurant salads taste better because they don't use bottled dressing, and promote this quick recipe as a simple alternative. The creator, a man wearing a dark jacket over a white shirt and a New York Yankees cap, encourages viewers to check his page for more recipes and to follow him. The overall tone is friendly, instructional, and food-focused.

18116030504078484.summary: A woman with long dark hair wearing a black ribbed tank top stands indoors holding a white plate of orange-colored stir-fried food, which she eats with chopsticks. On-screen text and her speech deliver an 'annual reminder' to 'put down the non-fat Greek yogurt bowl,' stating that other protein sources exist besides eggs and Greek yogurt. She explains she hasn't had eggs or Greek yogurt for breakfast in a very long time, identifies the dish as rehydrated bean curd cheese stir-fried with peanut Laoganma chili crisp, and notes she is eating it at 7 o'clock in the morning. She emphasizes that other people's popular diets should not dictate personal food preferences, arguing that if you don't eat what you like you won't stick with it and therefore won't achieve desired outcomes. The video ends with her encouraging viewers to 'enjoy your bakery cheats.' A small inset image briefly shows a close-up of the dish being lifted with chopsticks.

18129743437757714.summary: A woman demonstrates her budget-friendly dinner routine, explaining that she and her husband spend $50 per week on food. The video opens with a close-up of finished fried rice, then shows her preparing the base meal in a rice cooker: adding uncooked white rice and water, breaking in a block of S&B Golden Curry mix, then adding frozen mixed vegetables and crumbled tofu. She closes the lid, presses start, and later stirs the cooked mixture. On-screen text reinforces her message that they eat this Japanese curry rice with umami taste for color and protein, and that she can eat on $50 a week because she uses 'meal formulas, not recipes.' The video ends with her smiling while eating the dish with chopsticks and directing viewers to a link in her bio for more details. The tone is instructional, friendly, and practical, focused on affordable home cooking.

17883587742689038.summary: The video is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating how to make 'Hoisin Chicken but Make it Fried Rice.' It opens with a close-up of the finished dish being served from a wok into a black bowl, showing fried rice mixed with chicken pieces, scrambled egg, and chopped green onions. The process then rewinds to show the cooking steps: diced raw chicken is added to a hot oiled wok and stir-fried until cooked, then removed. Beaten egg is poured in and scrambled, followed by chopped green onions and garlic. A large portion of cooked white rice is added and broken up and mixed with the egg. The cooked chicken is returned to the wok, and a dark hoisin-based sauce is poured over everything. All ingredients are vigorously stir-fried together until evenly coated and browned. Finally, fresh sliced green onions are sprinkled on top as garnish. On-screen text reads 'HOISIN CHICKEN BUT MAKE IT FRIED RICE' and later 'Recipe in caption.' The audio consists of sizzling and stirring sounds with no spoken dialogue. The tone is clean, instructional, and focused on the satisfying visual of the cooking process.

18177119125447854.summary: A woman with long braided hair, wearing a white halter top and dark skirt, presents a 'super easy salad recipe for healthy skin & hair' in a bright indoor home setting. She begins by tasting the finished salad from a flower-shaped bowl, reacting with exaggerated enjoyment. She then demonstrates preparation: slicing a cucumber on a wooden board, adding chopped red onion ('kanda/pyaz'), minced garlic, and pumpkin seeds. She dresses the salad with olive oil and soy sauce, mixing it before eating again and praising the result. Throughout, she speaks directly to camera in an energetic, conversational tone, claiming the dish is good for skin and hair and joking that even someone who can't cook can feel like a chef. The visual focus remains on her upper body and the food preparation process.

18112842362602521.summary: A woman with long brown hair wearing a blue blouse demonstrates how to make a high-protein bean bowl in under five minutes. The video opens with her eating from a white bowl while on-screen text states '18g of protein 10g of fiber in 5 minutes' and 'Forget the protein powder, the hot girls are out here eating BEANS.' She retrieves a bag of frozen peas and edamame from a freezer, pours them into a bowl, and covers them with hot water to defrost. After straining the water in a sink, she returns to the counter and drizzles the beans with soy sauce, rice vinegar, and chili sesame oil. Close-ups show the glossy seasoned beans being mixed. On-screen text explains the dish is satisfying on its own or can be turned into a complete meal by adding salmon or tuna and rice. She smiles and eats the finished bowl outdoors in sunlight. The overall tone is casual, upbeat, and focused on quick healthy eating.

18184857907423268.summary: A woman named Megan, wearing a red apron and hair rollers, presents a quick recipe for '15-minute scallion tofu.' The video opens with shots of the finished dish—golden-brown tofu cubes coated in a dark sauce with wilted green onions. She introduces the ingredients, holding up large green onions (which she jokingly calls 'gronions'). The tutorial proceeds step-by-step: she slices the green onions, mixes a sauce in a small bowl with light and dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, water, salt and pepper, then prepares firm tofu by breaking it into large chunks and patting it dry. She pan-fries the tofu in oil until golden brown on both sides, pushes it aside to sauté the white parts of the onion, pours in the sauce to let the tofu absorb flavor, and finally adds the green tops just until wilted. She plates the dish and tastes it, concluding the demonstration. The tone is casual, friendly, and instructional.

18017470097731290.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial posted by creator Jeeca (@thefoodietakesflight) demonstrating how to make steamed silken tofu with ginger scallion sauce. The video opens with the finished dish in a white bowl inside a bamboo steamer, then shows the creator explaining why she prefers silken tofu for its texture. She removes a block of silken tofu from packaging, places it in a bowl, scores it into a grid pattern without cutting through, and steams it for about five minutes. After steaming, she drains the excess liquid released by the tofu. While the tofu steams, she sautés chopped green onion and ginger in oil, transfers them to a bowl, and mixes in seasonings including Chinese black vinegar, soy sauce, and other ingredients to create the sauce. She pours the hot sauce over the steamed tofu, then tops it with chili oil, sesame seeds, and additional fresh green onions. The final dish is served over white rice, and the creator is shown tasting it. The tone is warm, instructional, and focused on an easy Asian home-cooking recipe.

17979760032098978.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make a healthy, four-ingredient dessert using Okinawan purple sweet potato. The creator shows the process from start to finish: slicing and dicing the raw purple sweet potato, steaming the cubes in a bamboo steamer, mashing them, then mixing with white flour and a liquid to form a dough. Wearing gloves, they roll the mixture into small round balls, place them on a tray, and cook them in an air fryer until warm, puffy, and chewy. The finished balls are transferred to a bowl, drizzled with agave or honey, and sprinkled with sesame seeds. On-screen text emphasizes that the dessert is plant-based, refined-sugar-free, and gluten-free, inspired by Taiwanese deep-fried sweet potato balls but made without oil for easy cleanup. The tone is instructional and wholesome, focusing on the texture and appeal of the final product.

17967055626129552.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make high-protein cottage cheese biscuits topped with melted cheddar and jalapeño slices. The video opens with close-ups of the finished golden-brown bakes being pulled apart to show a soft interior, then shows her taking a bite and reacting positively. The recipe process is shown step-by-step: cracking an egg into a bowl, adding cottage cheese, whisking, mixing in shredded cheddar and chopped jalapeño, incorporating flour, scooping dough onto a parchment-lined tray, topping with more cheese and a jalapeño ring, and baking. A brief moment shows her giving a small dish of cheese to a corgi dog, captioned "pay cheese tax." On-screen text reinforces the recipe name and key points like "no yeast" and "30 minutes." The audio narration explains that cottage cheese adds protein without affecting taste, resulting in soft, fluffy biscuits ready in 30 minutes.

18018040571714373.summary: The video is a top-down cooking demonstration of making 'crispy smash burger tacos.' It begins with the finished product displayed on a wire rack, then shows the process in reverse order: hands fold a cooked tortilla topped with melted cheddar, creamy sauce, and lettuce into a taco shape and break it open to reveal the crispy interior. The preparation sequence shows four small flour tortillas laid on parchment paper, each topped with a ball of raw ground beef that is spread thinly across the surface and seasoned with salt. Oil is poured into a hot stainless steel pan, and the meat-side-down tortillas are placed in the pan to cook until browned and crispy. Slices of cheddar cheese are added to melt over the meat. The cooked patties are transferred to a cooling rack, where a creamy orange sauce is spooned on, followed by fresh lettuce. The text 'crispy smash burger tacos' appears throughout. The tone is clean, instructional, and focused on the satisfying visual and auditory texture of the food.

17966625549158235.summary: The video is a short-form cooking demonstration presented from a first-person point of view, with on-screen text reading 'pov: you're obsessed with crispy salmon.' A person prepares a dish by placing a seasoned raw salmon fillet onto a round, translucent rice paper wrapper on a wooden cutting board. They sprinkle crumbled white cheese (appearing to be feta) over the salmon, then fold the rice paper around it to form a tight roll. The roll is then pressed into a plate of crushed golden-brown cereal or breadcrumbs to coat it completely. The coated roll is placed into a black Tefal air fryer basket. After cooking, the finished product is shown plated alongside roasted sweet potato chunks and steamed broccolini. A creamy yellow sauce is drizzled over the crispy salmon roll, and a bite is taken to reveal the flaky pink salmon and melted cheese inside. The video has a clean, aesthetic food-content style with soft lighting and no spoken dialogue, focusing entirely on the visual process of creating the meal.

18129181345668421.summary: A young man presents 'dinners you'll actually make episode 5' — caramelized onion and garlic spaghetti. The video opens with close-ups of the finished creamy pasta in a pan, garnished with herbs, while on-screen text calls it easy and his favorite dinner. He then demonstrates the recipe: adding olive oil and butter to a pan, cooking sliced onions low and slow until deeply golden, then adding minced garlic, a spice blend (paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, Italian seasoning, salt), and a spoonful of chili crisp. He explains the 'secret ingredient' is a splash of soy sauce for umami, followed by cream or coconut milk and grated Parmesan cheese, before tossing in cooked spaghetti and parsley. Interspersed, he holds up his phone to show how viewers can save the Instagram Reel to his app, Osta, which converts social-media recipes into written ingredient lists and directions, emphasizing it is 100% free. The tone is upbeat, instructional, and promotional, set in a home kitchen with candles and fresh ingredients visible.

18109654343040508.summary:
A woman presents her 11-year-perfected tomato soup recipe, promising to teach it in under 60 seconds. The video opens with the finished dish—a creamy orange soup in a dark speckled bowl drizzled with olive oil, served alongside a toasted grilled cheese sandwich which she dips and eats.

She then walks through the preparation: placing halved large tomatoes and cherry/candy tomatoes on a foil-lined sheet pan, adding chopped red bell pepper and onion, coating everything with Italian seasoning, black pepper, and olive oil, and roasting at 350°F for about an hour until wrinkled and caramelized. She notes she lets it cool overnight.

The next day, she transfers the roasted vegetables to a blender, squeezes in the softened roasted garlic from its head, adds one cup of chicken or vegetable stock and one cup of water, and blends until smooth. Instead of heavy cream or oat milk, she stirs in Thai coconut milk while heating the soup in a pot, explaining it makes the soup velvety and improves with reheating. She serves the hot soup back into the bowl, finishes with another olive oil drizzle, and concludes that viewers have now learned the recipe.

18011552840928557.summary: This is a bright, sunlit cooking video focused on making a 'fig & caramelized onion grilled cheese' sandwich, as indicated by on-screen text throughout. The video shows a person's hands with blue nail polish preparing the sandwich on a black-and-white checkered wooden board. The process includes slicing fresh figs, grating cheese onto a pink dish, spreading a brown paste (likely caramelized onion) and an orange jam onto thick slices of bread, layering shredded cheese, caramelized red onions, sliced figs, fresh thyme leaves, and additional cheese slices, then drizzling honey over the top before closing the sandwich. The assembled sandwich is then grilled in a pan on a gas stove, pressed with another pan, flipped to achieve a golden-brown crust, and finally cut in half to reveal the melted cheese and fig filling. The video concludes with shots of the finished sandwich being held up and pulled apart to show the gooey interior, garnished with more figs and thyme. The audio consists of gentle instrumental background music with no spoken dialogue.

18102467153309496.summary: A woman in a floral-patterned kurta demonstrates how to make lauki (bottle gourd) paneer muthiya, described as a simple and super healthy dish suitable for fasting (vrat). The video opens with her steaming elongated dumplings in a traditional brass pot. She then shows the preparation process: grating lauki, squeezing out excess water using a cloth, grating paneer, and mixing it with flour, chopped green chilies, ginger, cilantro, and spices in a brass thali. She kneads the mixture into a dough, shapes it into small logs, and steams them. After steaming, she cuts the logs into pieces and stir-fries them in a pan with oil, cumin seeds, green chilies, and curry leaves until lightly golden. The finished muthiya are plated on a banana leaf-lined terracotta plate with a side of green chutney, which she dips and tastes with evident enjoyment. The audio features her speaking in Hindi and English explaining the recipe, accompanied by traditional Indian folk music in the background.

18440478235132309.summary: A man with a beard and tattoos prepares a pasta dish in a kitchen setting. The video opens with close-ups of creamy pasta being lifted from a pan, accompanied by on-screen text explaining an Italian saying: 'Never let the farmer know how well cheese and pears go.' He introduces his twist on a Roman classic, 'Cacio e Pere' (cheese and pears). He shows two pears, dices them on a wooden board, then sautés the pieces in olive oil in a copper pan on a portable burner, seasoning with salt and pepper before setting them aside. He prepares the sauce base by mixing grated Pecorino Romano cheese with black pepper and hot pasta water in a small glass bowl until it forms a paste. He cooks large tube pasta (paccheri) in boiling water, then transfers it to the pan with more pasta water and black pepper. He adds the caramelized pears back to the pan, followed by the Pecorino paste, and tosses everything together over heat until the sauce becomes creamy and coats the pasta. The final shots show the finished dish plated and ready to eat.

18210049489342953.summary: A blonde woman in a black long-sleeve top and blue jeans demonstrates Episode Two of her '7 Days of Easy Fall Dump Dinners' series in a bright modern kitchen. The video opens with her pouring a liquid into a finished baked casserole and stirring the creamy orange-colored dish containing chicken, orzo pasta, and spinach. She then walks through the preparation from scratch: placing diced raw chicken into a white baking dish, adding strips of sun-dried tomato, sprinkling seasoning, and covering everything with uncooked orzo rice. She covers the dish with foil and puts it into a double oven. After baking, she removes the dish, pours in milk or cream and grated cheese, and stirs in fresh spinach until the mixture becomes a thick, creamy bake. Throughout, a voiceover describes the recipe as easy, creamy, cozy, with 38 grams of protein, and encourages viewers to grab the recipe below and follow for more easy fall dinners. The tone is friendly, instructional, and focused on simple one-pan cooking.

18147547492606458.summary: A woman demonstrates her 'most viral recipe of 2026 so far' — small chocolate-coated bites. The video opens on a wooden board with orange slices and pumpkin seeds, then shows finished squares in a brown bowl topped with orange zest. She blends dates, cacao, and other ingredients into a thick paste, spoons it into a blue silicone ice-cube tray, tops with melted chocolate, and sprinkles orange zest. On-screen text explains the bites support iron levels via cacao, pumpkin seeds, and tahini, provide carbs from dates, and satisfy afternoon sweet cravings. She states she always keeps a stash in her freezer because she is 'a chocolate girl through and through.' The tone is warm, instructional, and promotional of a healthy-ish snack, ending with her holding the bowl toward the camera.

18118256075299955.summary: This is Episode 4 of a '5 Ways to Use Greek Yogurt' series by creator Jamie (@eatswithjamie), a registered dietitian based in Texas. The video demonstrates how to make a gluten-free blueberry pastry/strudel. The process begins with cracking an egg into a pan, adding baking powder, whisking, then softening two round rice paper sheets in the mixture and layering them. On a plate, thick Greek yogurt is spread over the center, topped with fresh blueberries (with a tip not to add too many to avoid sogginess) and drizzled with honey. The edges of the rice paper are folded inward to form a square galette. After baking or air frying, the pastry becomes golden and flaky. The final shots show the cooked pastry on parchment paper being sliced open to reveal a vibrant purple-blueberry and yogurt filling. The tone is instructional, clean, and food-focused, presented as a healthy breakfast or snack option.

18192470470392274.summary: A woman with shoulder-length dark hair wearing a white t-shirt and light pants demonstrates how to make air-fryer rice paper shrimp rolls in a bright modern kitchen. On-screen text states she saw the recipe and gives it a '12/10 recommend!!'. She begins by finely chopping green onions into a metal bowl, then empties raw peeled shrimp onto a cutting board and minces them. She combines the shrimp and onions, adds seasonings from bottles, and mixes. She lays out a round rice paper wrapper, spoons the shrimp mixture in a line, spreads it, and tightly rolls it up. Using red scissors, she cuts the long roll into bite-sized pieces, places them in a Ninja air fryer basket, sets the temperature to 400 degrees, and cooks them until golden brown and crispy. She presents the finished rolls on foil, takes a bite, expresses enjoyment, and holds one up to show the texture. She also makes 'shrimp chips' from leftover shrimp mixture, noting they are 'soooo crispy!!', and continues eating while smiling. The video is upbeat, focused on food preparation and tasting, with background pop music.

17968876950176305.summary: The video is a short, sunlit cooking tutorial presented from a first-person perspective. It opens with a close-up of cooked oatmeal being scooped into a white bowl, overlaid with the text 'POV: Your toddler is tired of oatmeal,' establishing the premise that an alternative is needed. The scene then shifts to preparing a new dish in a saucepan. Water is poured in, followed by uncooked rice, which is stirred. Milk is added, then cinnamon is sprinkled on top and mixed in. After the mixture cooks and thickens, pumpkin puree is added, followed by maple syrup and vanilla essence. All ingredients are stirred together until combined into a creamy, orange-colored porridge. The visual style is clean and aesthetic, with an orange checkered cloth and a pumpkin-themed trivet in the background, suggesting a fall theme. The audio consists of cheerful, upbeat instrumental music throughout. No people are fully shown, only hands performing the cooking actions.

18599142022056843.summary: A woman identified as Susanna Bowers (@myglobalpantry) in London demonstrates how to cook salmon to avoid dryness. The video opens with a close-up of flaky cooked salmon over herby rice with lemon. She explains the biggest mistake is cooking fish too hot and too fast. In her kitchen, she salts raw salmon fillets, then heats a pan, adds oil, turns heat down, and places salmon skin-side down. She watches it turn from pink to opaque halfway up, flips it, spoons oil over for 30 seconds, and removes it, noting carryover cooking. She prepares a side: mincing garlic, cutting lemon wedges, mixing yogurt with dill, parsley, and lemon for a sauce, and stirring fresh herbs into warm rice. She tastes the rice, calls the method easy for weeknights, and says she wrote step-by-step instructions in her newsletter so viewers can get perfect salmon at home. She eats the finished dish and asks viewers what food to tackle next after chicken last week and salmon this week. The tone is instructional, calm, and encouraging.

17927834463323006.summary: A woman with long dark hair and red nail polish introduces a recipe for what she calls a 'dangerous dessert' — black sesame butter mochi — which she has made multiple times recently because it satisfies sudden cravings without the time commitment of bread baking. Speaking to the camera while holding a small microphone, she demonstrates the process step-by-step on a wooden countertop. She cracks eggs into a metal bowl on a scale, adds sugar and vanilla, whisks, then incorporates flour by sifting it in. She mixes in black sesame paste until the batter turns gray, strains it to remove lumps, and pours it into a greased muffin tin. For an extra gooey center, she places small white sticky rice balls (tangyuan) into each cup before covering them with more batter. She bakes the mochi in an air fryer, flipping the tin halfway through, and repeats for a second batch. The finished mochi are golden brown with some showing burst centers. She tastes one, breaks it open to reveal the melted rice ball inside, and reacts with enjoyment, saying 'This one's fresh' and laughing that she's 'blessed.' She closes by thanking viewers and saying goodbye.

17910042885282136.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted August 28, 2026 by creator @hana_kailua demonstrating how to make a "healthy Korean pancake made with tofu" instead of flour. The video opens with the finished dish on a blue plate, then shows step-by-step preparation: chopping fresh garlic chives on a marble board, placing a block of silken tofu in a glass bowl, adding potato starch (on-screen text: "No flour! Made with silken tofu"), mashing it into a batter, folding in the chives, and preparing a dipping sauce with sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame seeds, and chili oil. The batter is poured into a hot oiled pan (text: "Make sure the pan is HOT!"), cooked until golden brown and flipped to show a chewy texture (text: "Golden & chewy"). The final shots return to the plated pancake being lifted with chopsticks, with text describing it as "Healthy, easy & delicious!" and "Thank you for watching ❤️". The tone is bright, instructional, and wholesome, set to upbeat instrumental music, with no dialogue.

18113936989694377.summary: In this MasterChef Australia clip from 2026, contestant Poh demonstrates her favorite carb—homemade rice noodles—to fellow contestants. She mixes rice flour, tapioca flour, boiling water, and neutral oil, explaining there is no kneading technique, just binding starches together. The dough is pressed through a ricer straight into boiling water, creating fresh noodles instantly, which impresses the group. Judge Belinda notes how easy it looks. Later, contestant Lucy presents her version: "fakeaway noodles" with Poh's noodles topped with crispy beef and a salty-sweet-sour-spicy sauce garnished with cilantro, chili, peanuts, and spring onion. Judges taste and praise Lucy's execution—the noodles are springy, the beef adds texture, and the sauce balances sweet, salty, and vinegar perfectly. Poh exclaims "Amazing!" and another judge says she "nailed the brief." Lucy reacts with joy and gratitude as contestants applaud. The segment ends with branding for Coles, Channel 10, and MasterChef.

18642728488041228.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make 'apple pie' pastry rings. The on-screen text reads 'Nobody tell apple pie.' A person with manicured nails and rings prepares the dessert: they slice fresh red apples on a wooden board, use a round cutter to remove the core creating apple rings, dip the rings in cinnamon sugar, then wrap thin strips of raw puff pastry around each ring. The assembled pastries are placed on a baking sheet, brushed with egg wash, sprinkled with more cinnamon sugar, and baked until golden brown and flaky. The finished product is plated on a white dish, drizzled with caramel sauce, and served alongside scoops of vanilla ice cream. The setting includes a lit amber candle and a basket of apples in the background, creating a warm, autumnal aesthetic. 17880665484534217.summary: The video is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating the preparation of 'JALAPEÑO POPPER cottage cheese toast.' It opens with a close-up of the finished toast on a wooden board, topped with melted browned cheese, sliced jalapeños, and red pepper flakes. Text identifies the dish. The process is shown step-by-step: diced red onion and chopped jalapeño are placed in a white bowl, followed by shredded cheese and a large scoop of cottage cheese, then mixed together. The mixture is spread onto a slice of rustic bread, topped with additional jalapeño slices, more shredded cheese, and red pepper flakes. After baking, the cheese is melted and golden-brown. The toast is then cut into three strips, with on-screen text encouraging viewers to 'Follow for weekly toast ideas.' The tone is clean, instructional, and focused entirely on food.

18140200696513587.summary: A female creator demonstrates how to make sago (tapioca pearl) pudding as a refreshing summer dessert. She explains cooking tiny tapioca pearls in boiling water for about 15 minutes, then letting them sit until translucent. She presents three variations: a mango version mixing pearls with diced almond agar jelly, mango chunks, strawberries, and a puree of mangoes, whole milk, coconut milk, and honey; an earthy purple sweet potato version using steamed mashed purple sweet potatoes poured over pearls with diced sweet potato and lychee; and a strawberry version combining slow-roasted sugared strawberries with a plain lightly sweetened pudding base. The video shows close-ups of ingredients, cooking steps, assembly in glasses and bowls, and the creator tasting the finished dessert. The tone is calm, instructional, and appetizing, focused on home cooking.

18147961045558332.summary:
This is a cooking tutorial video demonstrating how to make shrimp fried rice, presented with Malayalam voiceover. The video opens with the finished dish being tossed in a black wok, then served onto a banana leaf-lined brass plate where a hand mixes and lifts the rice to show texture.

The process begins with raw peeled shrimp placed in a bowl, seasoned with salt, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and ground pepper, then mixed by hand. Oil is heated in a wok, the marinated shrimp are fried until they turn orange and crispy, then removed with a slotted spoon and set aside.

In the same oil, minced garlic is sautéed, followed by sliced shallots which are fried until golden brown and caramelized. Fresh curry leaves and red chili flakes are added and stirred. Cooked white rice is then added to the wok and mixed thoroughly with the aromatics. The previously fried shrimp are returned to the pan, everything is tossed together, and a final seasoning is sprinkled over the top before a final mix.

The completed shrimp fried rice is plated generously on the banana leaf, showcasing the golden rice, whole shrimp, and green curry leaves. The watermark 'Jaggus' is visible throughout. The tone is instructional and appetizing, focused entirely on food preparation.

17874086739566402.summary: A woman presents a cozy autumn cooking video for 'French onion pasta.' She begins by showing the finished dish in a white bowl — shell pasta in a creamy, savory sauce topped with chopped parsley and black pepper — then takes a bite. The video then walks through the preparation: sliced onions are added to a pan and cooked down until deeply caramelized, followed by minced garlic, a sprinkle of dried herbs, and flour to form a roux. Broth is poured in, then uncooked shell pasta is simmered directly in the liquid. Once tender, cream is added along with shredded cheese, which melts into a thick sauce. The pan is topped with more cheese and grilled until golden and bubbling, then finished with fresh parsley. The setting is homey with plants and candles in the background, and the narration emphasizes the dish as a comforting, flavorful hug-in-a-bowl perfect for cozy season.

17897177178606136.summary: A woman with tattooed arms demonstrates how to make carrot gnocchi using glutinous rice flour. The video opens with the finished dish—small orange ring-shaped noodles tossed in a dark savory sauce with sesame seeds and herbs. She explains she noticed the recipe is basically carrot and glutinous rice flour, which appeals to her love of chewy, soft, stretchy textures. She peels and slices carrots, boils them, then mashes them in a bowl before adding glutinous rice flour by feel rather than measurement. She kneads the dough until it holds together, rolls it into a log, cuts pieces, and shapes each into a small indented disc. For the sauce, she combines grated garlic and ginger, chili powder, MSG, sugar, sesame seeds, hot sesame oil, soy sauce, black vinegar, and chopped coriander. She boils the shaped noodles until they float, drains them, plates them, and pours the sauce over. Tasting with chopsticks, she describes the flavor as 'green' like something healthy, admits she doesn't know if it is healthy and doesn't care, and concludes the texture combined with the sauce is 'a yes for me.' The overall tone is relaxed, conversational, and encouraging, suggesting viewers take their time, enjoy music or wine, and embrace the process.

18107513807028201.summary: The video opens with the creator, an 18-year-old woman wearing a brown t-shirt and denim apron, holding a jar of red juice in a modern white kitchen as on-screen text invites viewers to 'COME SPEND A 12 HR SHIFT WITH ME AS A 18 YEAR OLD PRIVATE CHEF IN ARIZONA.' She then shows her early morning at home: waking at 5:45, taking a mirror selfie in a black DKNY shirt while doing a slick back bun, and reading her Bible at a table. She grabs breakfast and matcha from the fridge, loads supplies into her car in a garage, and drives while eating caramelized banana overnight oats with peanut butter. Arriving at her first client's kitchen, she puts on her apron and presents the homemade watermelon, lime, and mint juice she made the day before. She begins intensive meal prep: mixing lemon blueberry protein muffins in a large green bowl, blending pesto mozzarella egg bites, and chopping cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and cilantro for a marinated chickpea Greek salad. She also prepares cilantro lime rice, P.F. Chang's-style turkey lettuce wraps, and slices cooked steak. After packaging and labeling everything and leaving the kitchen cleaner than she found it, she drives to her second client's house, stopping for coffee first. At the second kitchen she repeats the process, cooking honey garlic chicken with coconut lime rice. The video ends with her removing her apron and signing out. Throughout she narrates calmly, emphasizing organization and starting the day with faith.

18134037766729935.summary: The video is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating a method for preparing oatmeal. A bottle of Lifeway kefir is shown as the creator adds 2 tablespoons of kefir and 1 cup of water to 1 cup of oats, stirring and covering the bowl to soak overnight. The next morning, the soaked oats are shown. In a saucepan, the creator boils 1 cup of water with 1/4 tsp salt and 2 tbs butter, then adds the soaked oats, reduces to a simmer, and cooks for 10 minutes until thickened. The finished oatmeal is labeled 'Perfection.' The video ends with a call to action to send the video to someone making oatmeal wrong and to follow for more gut healthy grain tips. 18335673694279611.summary: The video is a step-by-step cooking tutorial for a creamy spicy tofu noodle bowl. Separately, crumbled tofu is fried in a pan until golden, then mixed with a dark glaze to create a savory topping. Udon noodles are boiled and drained. The final assembly shows the sauce poured over the noodles in a bowl, topped with the glazed tofu crumble, fresh cilantro, sliced green onions, and sesame seeds. The ingredients are mixed together, lifted with chopsticks to show the texture, and then eaten by a man in a kitchen who appears to enjoy the dish.

Water is added, and the mixture is whisked into a smooth purple batter, then cooked and stirred with a spatula until it forms a thick dough. Wearing black gloves, the creator kneads the warm purple dough, stretches it, and rolls it into small bite-sized balls. The video concludes by returning to the plated finished mochi bites. The audio throughout is a background pop song with a female vocalist; no spoken narration is present.

18114353537517723.summary: The video is a short-form cooking demonstration presented by the account @myhome.byheart, with on-screen text stating 'The recipe that got 17M Views.' A pair of hands picks up one pastry and pulls it apart to reveal a melted cheese and chicken filling inside. The video then rewinds to show the preparation: diced raw chicken is added to a hot pan, seasoned with spices, and sautéed with chopped red and green peppers. Next, a square sheet of puff pastry is placed on a wooden board, scored at each corner, filled in the center with the chicken mixture and shredded cheese, and then folded inward to create a four-petaled flower shape. 18047937671811596.summary:

Next, square wonton wrappers are shown; a scoop of filling is placed in the center, the wrapper is moistened at the edges, and folded into a classic four-pointed star-shaped rangoon. 17991654360005654.summary: This is a short-form cooking video titled 'Day 47/365 days of Breakfast' showing the preparation of chocolate banana oats. The video opens with a finished bowl of dark brown baked oats topped with sliced bananas and large chocolate chunks, described by on-screen text and voiceover as tasting like 'chocolate cake for breakfast without the guilt.' The creator then demonstrates the recipe step-by-step in a white bowl: adding rolled oats, chia seeds, a cracked egg, mashed ripe banana, baking powder, peanut butter, cocoa powder, and milk. All ingredients are mixed together into a thick batter. The mixture is then topped with fresh banana slices and more chocolate pieces before being shown ready to eat. The voiceover emphasizes that the dish is rich, chocolatey, naturally sweetened, creamy, high in fiber, and provides sustained energy without a sugar crash, positioning it as an indulgent-tasting but wholesome breakfast option.

17996746350033180.summary: A woman in a white bathrobe presents a quick recipe for congee, described on-screen as 'how i make congee on a time crunch (30g protein, <15 mins)'. Speaking directly to camera, she explains this is the breakfast her Chinese mother has eaten for over 30 years, claiming it has 'made her age backwards.' She notes traditional congee can take an hour, but offers a shortcut for 'busy women.' The video shows her in a modern kitchen placing eggs in a saucepan, pouring hot water from a kettle, turning on a gas burner, and mixing a powdered supplement (appearing to be protein) into a bowl of cooked congee. The finished dish is topped with chopped green onions and a halved soft-boiled egg with a runny yolk. She is later seen eating the meal in a tank top. 18095890412093685.summary: This is Part 4 of a rice cooker recipe series, demonstrating how to make oyakodon, described as a "criminally underrated" Japanese dish that is very popular in Japan. The creator explains the name means "parent-child bowl" because it uses chicken (the parent) and egg (the child). The video shows the full process: uncooked rice is placed in a Tiger rice cooker pot, then sliced onion and raw chicken thigh are combined in a bowl with soy sauce and seasonings, mixed, and poured over the rice. After cooking the rice and chicken together, the lid is opened and beaten eggs are poured on top, then the cooker is closed briefly to set the egg. The finished dish is served in a white bowl, garnished with chopped green onions and sesame seeds, and eaten with chopsticks by a woman with long dark hair wearing a white shirt. The tone is casual, instructional, and friendly, aimed at viewers looking for an easy, lazy-cook method.

18127206334867428.summary: A woman with short dark hair wearing a red-and-white striped long-sleeve shirt prepares a quick dinner in a modern home kitchen, with on-screen text noting 'dinner when I have 18 min of active cooking energy left.' She chops green asparagus on a wooden board, rinses rice in a black rice cooker pot, adds water, pours in a liquid seasoning, and stirs. She places a raw salmon fillet and a large quantity of shimeji mushrooms on top of the rice, then starts the white Cuckoo rice cooker. Separately, she dissolves miso paste in hot water to make soup and garnishes it with chopped green onions. After cooking, she opens the rice cooker, breaks up the cooked salmon, mixes everything together with shredded seaweed, and uses a light-blue triangular mold to form rice balls, wrapping them with sheets of nori. She serves the soup and rice balls on small plates and trays, then sits at a table to eat, tasting the soup and rice with visible enjoyment while interacting briefly with a child off-camera. 18115849960856721.summary: The video opens with a close-up of four finished glass meal-prep containers filled with baked dumplings in an orange-cream sauce, topped with chopped green onion, cilantro, and red chili crunch, with on-screen text reading "BACK TO SCHOOL Meal Prep." She pours canned full-fat coconut milk into four empty glass containers, followed by Trader Joe's Soyaki sauce and Trader Joe's Thai red curry sauce, then stirs each mixture. Chopped bok choy is added to the bottom of each container, and five to six frozen dumplings are layered on top. The containers are covered tightly with aluminum foil and presumably baked. After baking, the cooked dumplings are shown submerged in the bubbling sauce, and she tops each portion with a spoonful of Momofuku chili crunch, sliced green onions, and fresh cilantro. The final shots show the completed meals being sealed with blue and yellow lids for storage. The overall tone is warm, instructional, and practical, aimed at busy parents and teachers looking for easy lunch prep.

18070101596773642.summary: A woman in a red patterned kurta and striped apron presents 'Episode 01' of a breakfast series outdoors then in a modern kitchen. Speaking in Hindi, she explains that the biggest breakfast mistake is having tea or coffee on an empty stomach after the overnight fast, which causes energy crashes and hunger later. To demonstrate a better option, she soaks moong dal overnight, then blends it with chopped bottle gourd (lauki), spices including turmeric, salt, and water into a smooth batter. She pours the batter onto a hot pan, tops it with chopped onions, cilantro, and grated cheese, covers it to cook, and flips it to reveal a golden uttapam. Separately, she roasts tomatoes and garlic, blends them with chili and salt into a chutney. She plates two uttapams with the chutney, stating this protein-rich meal will keep you energized for six hours without sluggishness. She concludes by promoting her plan for tomorrow's breakfast and asks viewers to follow for more episodes.

18112543945957051.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video presenting what the creator calls 'the only Japanese riceball recipe you need' — takikomi gohan (炊き込みご飯), a one-pot seasoned rice dish. The video opens on a Zojirushi rice cooker, then shows the finished mixed rice containing shredded carrots, sliced shiitake mushrooms, edamame, and chicken. The creator explains she grew up with it and that American friends would ask her mom to make extra because it's so good, describing it as filled with Japanese umami and tons of protein and fiber. The tutorial portion shows preparation: slicing shiitake mushrooms and shredding carrots on a wooden board, then adding mirin, cooking sake, and soy sauce to the rice cooker pot, followed by rinsed rice and water to the fill line, dashi granules, bite-sized raw chicken pieces, shredded carrots, shiitake slices, and edamame. The video concludes with the lid being closed to cook, and shots of the creator and another person happily eating the formed riceballs wrapped in plastic wrap and nori. The overall tone is warm, nostalgic, and instructional.

17961009921138349.summary: The video is a short-form cooking demonstration filmed from an overhead perspective at a stovetop. A person uses a Y-shaped peeler to thinly slice a raw potato directly into a non-stick frying pan containing oil, as on-screen text instructs 'Thinly slice a potato with a peeler.' The potato slices accumulate in the pan, then salt is sprinkled over them. After cooking briefly, the potato layer is flipped with a spatula, revealing a golden-brown underside. Two whole eggs are cracked onto the cooked potato, then beaten together with a spatula to spread across the surface. Shredded cheddar cheese is added on top, followed by covering the pan with a glass lid to melt the cheese. Once melted, the entire mixture is folded in half like an omelet, then cut in half with a knife while still in the pan. The final shot shows one half being lifted with a spatula, displaying the layered potato, egg, and cheese interior, with the text 'Enjoy' appearing on screen. The background includes a blue-and-white checkered kettle on the stove. The audio features a French-language song playing throughout.

18095437343381922.summary: The video shows a person preparing and packing a bento lunch for their daughter, credited to @Cookming. The process begins with an empty stainless steel bento box. The creator hydrates rice paper sheets, then makes a small drink by cooking diced white cubes (likely konjac) with brown sugar and water, pouring the mixture into a decorated glass jar and adding milk. Next, they crack two eggs into a tray, whisk them, and pour onto a waffle iron, topping with sliced banana and chocolate chips before closing to cook a sweet waffle, which is cut and placed in the box. They then peel a cucumber, wrap thin strips of cucumber, egg, and salmon in hydrated rice paper to make rolls, and place them in another compartment. A simple dressing is mixed from a canned beverage, lemon juice, and sesame seeds and poured over the rolls, garnished with cherry tomato halves and star-shaped cheese. Finally, fresh strawberries and a round cheese slice are added to the last compartment. The video ends with the fully packed, colorful bento being closed. The tone is quiet, methodical, and aesthetically focused on food presentation.

18107814005268687.summary: A woman wearing a blue knit sweater presents a 'Busy girl dinners with a dietitian' recipe from her home kitchen. She introduces the dish as one of her favorite low-effort meals for when she has zero energy to cook. The video shows the step-by-step preparation: she whisks three eggs with warm water, adds seasonings including what appears to be soy sauce and dashi powder, gently places cubes of soft tofu into the bowl, tops it with raw shrimp, and microwaves it for about three minutes until set. After cooking, she finishes the dish with soy sauce, sesame oil, snipped spring onions, fresh-cut microgreens from an indoor herb garden, and a spoonful of Lao Gan Ma chili crisp. She describes the final meal as warm, comforting, super filling, and protein-rich, ideal for cold evenings. The tone is calm, instructional, and cozy, with close-ups of the food and her eating it.

18472473505116828.summary: A woman who identifies as half Japanese demonstrates how to increase the nutritional value of her daily white rice without sacrificing flavor. Filmed from overhead and medium shots in a modern kitchen, she starts by showing cooked white rice, then moves to a rice cooker pot. She adds Nishiki brand white rice, followed by Kirkland Organic Quinoa for protein, magnesium, and iron. In a separate bowl, she measures black rice for antioxidants, Japanese barley for fiber, and adzuki beans for digestive health, soaks them, then adds the mixture to the pot along with water and a packet of bone broth powder (noted as 10g protein, 5g collagen). After cooking in a Tiger rice cooker, she opens the lid to reveal a multigrain rice blend, fluffs it, and serves it into a bowl. Throughout, on-screen text explains her philosophy: she does not like to villainize white rice as it is a staple of Japanese cuisine, notes that Japanese people are healthy and live long lives, and emphasizes adding to foods she loves to make them nutritionally complete rather than cutting them out.

17900423592378945.summary: The video is a short-form cooking demonstration for a 'dump and bake butter herb chicken & rice' dish. A person's hands prepare the meal in a white rectangular ceramic baking dish on a wooden surface near a window. The process begins by pouring uncooked white rice into the dish, followed by a light-colored liquid (likely broth) from a glass measuring cup. The mixture is stirred with a wooden spatula. Diced raw chicken breast is then added, topped with dried herbs and spices, and stirred again to combine. The dish is covered tightly with aluminum foil and placed in an oven (implied). After baking, the foil is removed to reveal cooked chicken and rice. Shredded white cheese is sprinkled over the top, followed by a generous amount of fresh basil leaves, which are stirred in. More cheese and chopped fresh parsley are added as garnish. The video ends with a close-up spoonful of the finished creamy, herb-filled chicken and rice casserole. The tone is calm, instructional, and homey, with natural daylight and simple kitchen aesthetics.

18219889309328235.summary: A young woman presents a 'POV you don't feel like cooking for dinner' one-pot meal in her home kitchen. She starts by rinsing rice in a Zojirushi Neuro Fuzzy rice cooker pot, then adds Swanson chicken broth, minced garlic, minced ginger, chopped scallions, chicken bouillon powder, a sprinkle of turmeric, two raw chicken thighs, a pinch of salt, and sesame oil. She closes the lid and starts the cooker. While it cooks, she heats oil in a pan and pours it over a bowl of chopped scallions and ginger with salt to make a scallion oil sauce. Once done, she opens the cooker to reveal bright yellow turmeric rice with cooked chicken on top, removes the chicken, slices it on a cutting board, and plates the rice in a white bowl topped with the sliced chicken and generous spoonfuls of the green scallion oil. She holds up the finished dish and tastes it, commenting that the chicken is 'so silky soft.' The tone is calm, practical, and relatable, aimed at an easy lazy-dinner hack.

18071464901774940.summary: This is a short-form cooking video presented as part of a 'Nap time snack prep series.' The visual focuses entirely on hands preparing a savory baked dish. The process begins with cracking two eggs into a metal bowl, then adding shredded green zucchini, shredded yellow cheese, milk from a gold measuring cup, and flour. The ingredients are whisked together into a thick, speckled batter, which is then poured into a parchment-lined loaf pan. More shredded cheese is sprinkled on top before baking. The finished product is shown as a golden-brown loaf, which is lifted from the pan, sliced, and broken open to reveal a soft, cheesy interior. Background items visible include a carton of brown eggs, whole zucchinis, and a bowl of shredded cheese. There is no dialogue, on-screen narration beyond the text overlay, or identifiable people—only hands performing the cooking steps.

18133009759735546.summary: A muscular man in a black tank top stands in a kitchen with wooden cabinets and demonstrates three high-protein ground chicken recipes. He opens by holding a package of ground chicken and asking, 'You think ground chicken is underrated??' First, he makes 'Mediterranean Chicken Poppers': seasons ground chicken with coriander, cumin, and salt, adds parsley, wraps the mixture in rice paper, rolls it, cuts into six pieces, and air fries at 400 degrees for 14 minutes, noting 219 calories and 24g protein. Second, he makes a 'Chicken Smash Taco': seasons ground chicken with cayenne, coriander, cumin, and salt, spreads it on tortillas, air fries at 400 for 8 minutes, then tops with diced tomatoes, cucumber, and salt, totaling 475 calories and 55g protein. Third, he makes 'Jerk Chicken Poppers': mixes ground chicken with jerk seasoning, grated garlic, chopped green onion, pepper, and honey, dips rice paper in beaten egg, adds filling, folds, cuts into six, and air fries at 400 for 10 minutes, for 250 calories and 25g protein. The video ends with him tasting the finished poppers. The presentation is clean, fast-paced, and focused on meal-prep nutrition.

18102354902202181.summary: The video is Episode 13 of 'Undercover Iron,' a cooking series by creator Alice Cadman (@coachcadman), a MSc Nutrition student based in London. Filmed in 2026, it demonstrates how to make black sesame brownie bites designed to support iron intake. The process begins with blending oats, medjool dates, cashews, cacao powder, and black tahini in a Nutribullet, then pressing the mixture into a purple silicone ice-cube tray. Melted dark chocolate is poured over the base, topped with black sesame seeds and flaky sea salt, then chilled until set. The creator explains the bites provide iron from plant sources like dark chocolate, sesame, cashews, and oats, but notes plant compounds can inhibit absorption, so she advises pairing them with vitamin C-rich foods such as kiwi or strawberries. Visually, the video alternates between close-ups of ingredients, the mixing process, and the finished squares in a terracotta bowl, with the creator tasting one at the end. The tone is instructional, upbeat, and health-focused, with no humor, sexual content, or risky behavior.

18108566045579641.summary: This is the launch of a new cooking series called '10-2-20' — dinner for two, under $10, in less than 20 minutes. A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates making a Thai-inspired stir-fry. She starts by chopping green beans into bite-sized pieces, then cooks ground pork (noting chicken is an alternative) in a hot pan for 5-6 minutes. She adds the chopped green beans, minced garlic, and optional sliced Thai red chili, sautéing for 3-4 minutes. She seasons with soy sauce, oyster sauce, and honey, tossing until glossy. Fresh Thai basil is added at the end. Simultaneously, she fries two crispy eggs for extra protein. The finished dish is plated over hot white rice and topped with the fried egg. On-screen text tracks ingredient costs, totaling $7.62 for two servings. The video emphasizes speed, affordability, and flavor, concluding with the creator tasting the meal and expressing enjoyment.

17906556261554915.summary: A woman presents a recipe for 'Brownie Batter Greek Yogurt Cookies' in a bright kitchen setting. The video opens with close-ups of finished dark chocolate cookies stacked on a white plate, topped with flaky sea salt, being cut open with a gold fork to reveal a gooey, melted chocolate center. She holds up a cookie, breaks it in half to show the fudgy interior, and takes a bite, stating 'These are so good.' On-screen text and her narration describe the texture as having 'crispy edges, irresistibly soft centers' and a 'deep, rich chocolate flavor.' The preparation sequence shows ingredients being added to a glass bowl: brown sugar, an egg, Greek yogurt, a creamy nut butter (tahini), vanilla, and cocoa powder, which are mixed into a thick batter. Chocolate chips and chunks are folded in, described as adding 'subtle toasted nuttiness.' The dough is scooped onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, baked in an oven, and then shown fresh from the oven with melted chocolate pockets. She notes she tested the recipe multiple times and found using both chips and chunks gives 'the perfect amount of pockets of melted chocolate in every single bite.' The video concludes with more shots of the cookies being eaten and text directing viewers to details below.

18107170925112501.summary: The video opens with a close-up of the finished dish: sliced honey garlic chicken glazed with chopped garlic and sauce, arranged over white rice in a dark ceramic bowl, with on-screen text reading 'AIR FRYER RECIPES HONEY GARLIC CHICKEN'. A woman with long black hair in a cream shirt holds the bowl, takes a bite with a spoon, and smiles. The tutorial then shows the preparation: raw chicken thigh fillets in a white bowl are seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic powder, soy sauce, and oyster sauce, then mixed by a gloved hand. Separately, minced garlic and butter are placed in a small metal cup and air fried, then mixed with soy sauce and honey to create the glaze. The marinated chicken is dredged in cornstarch with baking powder, placed on parchment in the air fryer basket, and cooked at 190°C for 8 minutes per side until golden and crispy. The cooked chicken is transferred to a plate, generously spooned with the honey garlic sauce, then sliced and served over rice. The tone is instructional and appetizing, focusing on the texture and gloss of the sauce throughout.

17979402428904175.summary: This is a cooking tutorial by creator @tipcynn (Indonesian in Tokyo) demonstrating how to make Honey Miso Chicken for meal prep. The video opens with the finished caramelized chicken in a pan, then walks through the process: cutting raw chicken thighs into bite-size pieces, mixing a marinade in a yellow bowl with white miso, honey, soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, rice vinegar, and water, coating the chicken, and marinating overnight (with note that 30 minutes works same-day). The chicken is then cooked in a hot pan without added oil since thighs render their own fat, stirred until browned, and the sauce is allowed to caramelize around the pieces. The final dish is transferred to a glass meal-prep container. On-screen text and narration provide step-by-step instructions. The tone is instructional, friendly, and focused on healthy, sustainable eating, ending with 'selamat makan!'.

18015654407944665.summary: The video is a short-form food clip showcasing three variations of chicken over rice. It opens on a bowl with grilled sliced chicken, white rice, and cauliflower, as a dark glossy sauce is poured from a small white pitcher; on-screen text reads "if this is your vibe... 😋".
