It cuts to a second bowl with creamy peanut-style sauce ladled over chicken and rice with cucumber slices, captioned "or this... 😏". A third bowl shows poached chicken with a lighter savory sauce sprinkled with sesame seeds and chili flakes, captioned "or this 😊". The final shot shows chicken tenders simmering in a bubbling dark sauce in a pan, with tongs lifting one piece, and text says "then you're in the right place 😊". A male voiceover repeats the same phrasing. The overall tone is casual, appetizing, and promotional for food content.

18114328931005780.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make a vibrant green curry at home, explaining that restaurant food is more exciting because it introduces unexpected flavor combinations. The video opens with close-ups of the finished dish: bright green curry sauce poured over black rice, topped with fried tofu cubes, fresh basil leaves, and sliced red chilies. She then shows the preparation process in her kitchen, chopping an onion, gathering large amounts of fresh spinach and basil, and blending them with liquid into a vivid green puree. She pours the blended mixture into a pan, adds sautéed diced zucchini, squeezes lime juice, and stirs. The final steps show her plating the black rice and assembling the bowl. Throughout, on-screen text reinforces her narration about skipping guesswork by following recipes where someone else has already done the experimenting, encouraging viewers to save the recipe for future dinners.

17957893059236810.summary: A woman in a pink shirt presents 'Eating Simpler Diaries ep12: Zucchini Ragi Button Noodles' in a home kitchen. Inspired by viral carrot button noodles, she demonstrates a wholesome version using zucchini, edamame, and ragi flour. She chops zucchini, boils it with shelled edamame, then blends the cooked vegetables into a smooth green paste. In a bowl, she combines ragi flour and all-purpose flour with salt, adds the vegetable paste, and kneads it into a soft dough. She rolls tiny balls and presses centers to form button shapes, then boils them in the reserved vegetable water. For the sauce, she heats olive oil in a pan, adds red pepper flakes, red chili powder, and dried basil, then stirs in the remaining paste until creamy. She tosses the cooked buttons in the sauce, plates them, and tastes one with chopsticks while speaking to the camera. On-screen text identifies the dish and series. The tone is calm, instructional, and health-focused, highlighting protein from edamame and ragi and fiber from zucchini, edamame, and ragi.

18130625350740791.summary: A woman in a bright kitchen, wearing a white shirt, pink apron, and pink gloves, demonstrates batch-cooking rolled tacos (taquitos/flautas) for freezer storage. The video opens with her packing already-made rolls into a vacuum-seal bag with the text 'future me will thank me.' It then rewinds to show the process starting at 11:20 am: browning ground meat in a white pan, adding spices and sauce, pouring in water, and simmering until 11:27 am. At 11:30 am she tops the meat with shredded cheese. She then takes tortillas labeled 'STAPLE IN MY COURSE,' fills them with the meat mixture at 11:40 am ('coming together'), rolls them tightly, and lines them up on a parchment-lined baking sheet at 12:00 pm. Finally at 12:05 pm she places the tray into the freezer. The tone is practical, organized, and domestic, focused on efficient meal preparation.

18640435696019656.summary: A young woman, who states she is 18 years old and works meal-prepping for people's houses, films herself in a modern kitchen with dark cabinets. She explains she has four different clients and will cook for them that week. She proceeds through several recipes: first making refined-sugar-free raspberry almond protein muffins, which she tops with sliced almonds and tastes; then preparing a peach cobbler from fresh peaches, adding sugar and spices before baking; next making pan-fried dumplings/potstickers, mixing the filling, steaming and crisping them; followed by a meatloaf where she sautés onions, mixes ground meat with breadcrumbs, egg, and seasonings, forms it in a dish, and adds sauce; then cooking seasoned chicken thighs in a skillet; and finally searing and slicing a large piece of steak. Throughout she references her laptop for recipes, uses standard kitchen tools, and presents the finished meals in glass containers. The video is purely culinary, with no controversial content.

18614376961006915.summary: The video is a side-by-side recipe replication of a viral 'HEALTHY FUDGE BROWNIE CHEESECAKE BARS' dessert. A woman demonstrates the original method: mixing almond flour, cocoa powder, maple syrup, and almond milk for the brownie base, pressing it into a pan, freezing, then layering a cheesecake mixture of cream cheese, monk fruit icing sugar, and lemon juice, freezing again, and topping with a chocolate sauce made from cocoa, maple syrup, coconut oil, and almond milk. A male creator in a Bass Pro Shops cap and sleeveless shirt follows along step-by-step in his kitchen, narrating each ingredient and action. After chilling, he tastes the finished bar, calls it 'by far the best dessert item I've ever done,' rates it an 'easy 9.5 out of 10,' notes each bar has about 10g protein, and promotes his updated top 10 viral recipes, asking viewers to comment 'VIRAL.' The tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and promotional, focused entirely on food preparation and tasting.

18016579118916696.summary: A woman with long dark hair and red nail polish demonstrates how to make a high-protein breakfast toast that tastes like cheesecake. In a modern white kitchen, she starts by toasting gluten-free bread, then blends 1/2 cup low-fat cottage cheese with vanilla extract and maple syrup in a food processor until smooth. She prepares toppings including fresh blueberries cooked into a compote with lemon juice and chia seeds, diced walnuts, and thinly chopped mint leaves. She assembles the dish by spreading the whipped cottage cheese mixture on the toast, adding a dollop of blueberry compote, grating lemon zest over it, and finishing with walnuts and mint. She presents the finished toast, takes bites during a taste test, and expresses enjoyment, describing the combination of creamy cottage cheese, sweet blueberries, bright lemon zest, and fresh mint as exceeding expectations.

18107371589216581.summary: A woman in a black t-shirt demonstrates how to make an almond buckwheat banana bread topped with chocolate ganache, presented as part of her series 'Date Me' where she makes desserts sweetened with dates instead of refined sugar. She starts by showing overripe bananas, then mashes them with pitted dates and lemon zest. She whips egg whites separately, combines wet and dry ingredients including almond flour (noted for healthy fats and vitamin E) and buckwheat flour (noted for fiber, magnesium, manganese), folds in whipped egg whites for lift, and chops pure cacao mass to fold into the batter for crunchy chocolate pieces. After baking, she prepares a ganache from melted cacao mass and coconut milk, blends additional dates into a paste, and mixes it into the chocolate. The finished loaf is shown sliced, described as soft, moist, slightly nutty, and chocolatey. She plates a slice with ganache and sea salt, eats it, and emphasizes that the goal is desserts that taste incredible while satisfying cravings and allowing you to 'still love your body back.'

17919782817432509.summary: A woman in a home kitchen presents a series of food hacks for toddlers, centered on a small mint-green waffle maker. Opening with on-screen text 'don't know what to feed your toddler? WAFFLE IT!', she demonstrates pressing different meals into waffle shapes: cheese and broccoli, chicken and rice, spinach batter, mashed beets, banana and oats, french fries, chopped chicken nuggets, sweet potato puree, and even grapes. Each item is shown being placed in the waffle iron and then held up as a finished round waffle. The video ends with her cracking an egg over a bowl of pasta with broccoli, with text reading 'apparently everything is a waffle now...' The overall tone is playful, instructional, and aimed at parents looking for creative ways to serve food to young children.

18111619552980030.summary: A woman in a pink Batman T-shirt stands in a home kitchen holding a large metal container overflowing with raw cauliflower florets, explaining she ordered way too much and needs to use it up. She introduces her plan to make Gobhi 65, but using an air fryer for a healthier twist. The video cuts to a close-up of the finished dish—crispy, reddish-orange cauliflower pieces served on a banana leaf in a white bowl, labeled "Gobhi 65." She then demonstrates the process: transferring the florets to a clear glass bowl, adding a dry batter of flour, cornflour, Kashmiri chili powder, coriander, cumin, salt, sugar, chopped curry leaves, whisked yogurt, a dash of oil, and water. She mixes everything by hand until evenly coated and lets it marinate for ten minutes. Next, she places the florets in a single layer in an air fryer basket without touching, brushes them with oil, and air-fries until super crispy. Separately, she heats oil in a hammered kadai, sautés finely chopped ginger, garlic, halved green chilies, and curry leaves, adds Kashmiri chili powder, then tosses in all the air-fried cauliflower for about a minute. She plates the finished Gobhi 65 hot on the banana leaf. In the final scene, wearing a light denim shirt, she tastes it from a bowl, closes her eyes in enjoyment, and makes an "OK" hand gesture. The video ends with the "MY FOOD STORY" logo.

18146546881502362.summary:
This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make an 'Easiest One Pot Chicken Dinner.' The video opens with a close-up of the finished meal: a molded dome of rice, shredded poached chicken topped with a dark chili-garlic sauce, and a bowl of clear broth garnished with green onions and chili oil. Text overlay reads 'Easiest One Pot Chicken Dinner You'll Ever Make.'

The preparation sequence follows: a hand crushes fresh ginger and garlic cloves in a stone mortar. In a speckled pan, oil is heated, then the crushed aromatics, sliced ginger, and chopped scallions are sautéed. Raw chicken leg quarters are placed on top, drizzled with soy sauce and sprinkled with sugar, then stirred briefly before water is added and the pot is covered to simmer.

Separately, minced garlic is fried in oil, uncooked rice is added and toasted, then the cooked chicken pieces are placed back on top of the rice. The pot is covered again to steam. The video concludes by returning to the plated presentation, showing the chicken being shredded and mixed with sauce, ready to eat. The tone is calm, instructional, and focused entirely on the food process, with no dialogue, only ambient kitchen sounds and background music.

18120558541871682.summary: A woman in a home kitchen wearing a light gray Alo quarter-zip sweatshirt demonstrates how to make her favorite breakfast: an egg and cheese on a roll. She explains she grew up helping at her parents' deli where they made hundreds of sandwiches each morning, which is why she feels she has perfected the recipe. She cracks two eggs with salt into a striped bowl, then retrieves a fresh deli roll from the store, noting she scoops out some of the interior bread so it isn't too bready. She heats a 10-to-12-inch skillet on low with butter, pours in the eggs, and describes an optional Indian-inspired addition: mixing mayonnaise with 'lasanyu marchu,' a garlicky chili paste she calls dangerous depending on preparation but says her version is very spicy. Once the egg is set, she places one and a half slices of cheese on top and folds the egg over. She spreads the spicy mayo inside the hollowed roll, inserts the folded egg and cheese, shows the melted cheese pull, takes a bite, and tells viewers they have to try it and should brush their teeth afterward.

17973751889934411.summary: In a bright home kitchen, creator Zoha Malik (@bakewithzoha) demonstrates her recipe for banana bread chocolate chip cookies, posted September 16, 2026. She begins by holding overripe spotty bananas, explaining they are ideal for the recipe she has been dreaming about. She browns butter in a green pan until bubbly and nutty, then mashes the bananas in a small bowl. In a glass mixing bowl, she combines the brown butter, mashed banana, brown sugar (noting she uses only brown sugar), vanilla extract, a small amount of instant coffee dissolved in water, salt, and baking soda. She then adds flour and folds in roughly chopped milk and dark chocolate. Using a cookie scoop, she portions the dough onto parchment-lined baking sheets, presses reserved chocolate pieces on top, and sprinkles flaky sea salt. After baking for about 15 minutes, she tops each warm cookie with a thin banana slice. She tastes the finished cookie, describing it as nutty, caramelly, and toffee-like, and reacts with enjoyment. The tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and food-focused, with no risky or inappropriate content.

17976240278917437.summary: The video is a split-format cooking/reaction clip about a viral high-protein cheesecake hack. An older man with short gray hair in a kitchen cracks an egg into a bowl of Greek yogurt, whisks until smooth, adds honey and vanilla, then pours the mixture into a greased round pan and bakes at 350°F for 20 minutes. A younger, muscular blonde man in a black sleeveless shirt (identified on-screen as fitness coach Hadrian) narrates the reaction portion. He presents the finished baked ramekin, notes its caramelized top, and tastes it, expressing surprise at the creamy, cheesecake-like texture. He highlights the nutrition — about 300 calories and 30 grams of protein per serving compared to ~850 calories for regular cheesecake — calls it 'incredibly easy, incredibly tasty,' rates it 9 out of 10, and says he'll make it again. Throughout he promotes his Instagram account, encouraging viewers to follow and comment 'viral' to get his list of over 200 tested recipes. The tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and promotional, aimed at fitness-minded audiences seeking low-calorie desserts.

18093308912080681.summary: A woman with long dark hair wearing a black t-shirt and floral apron demonstrates how to make a summer carrot ribbon salad in a bright home kitchen. She begins by using a pink vegetable peeler to create long, thin ribbons from whole carrots on a wooden cutting board, then places them in a large glass bowl. She shows a jar of walnuts, chops them roughly on the board, and transfers them to a small food processor. She adds fresh cilantro, pours in honey, a dark liquid (likely soy sauce), and squeezes lime juice, along with garlic, then blends the mixture into a coarse green-brown dressing. She spoons the dressing over the carrot ribbons and mixes thoroughly by hand until coated. Throughout, she tastes the salad with chopsticks, expressing enjoyment. The audio narration emphasizes that summer salads don't need lettuce, highlights the walnuts' crunch and plant-based omega-3 content, and suggests using the dressing on sandwiches or roasted vegetables.

18116160334764249.summary: A person demonstrates how to make a quick 30-minute dinner of chicken-stuffed tortillas. Starting with minced chicken in a metal bowl, they add chopped onions, garlic, green chilies, red chili flakes, and seasonings, then mix by hand. Separately, they prepare a slaw by combining shredded cabbage and carrots with mayonnaise, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. They spread the seasoned chicken mixture onto small homemade tortillas, place them chicken-side-down in a hot pan, cook until golden and crispy, flip, add cheese, and fold. The finished flatbreads are shown cut open, filled with melted cheese and topped with the fresh slaw, served alongside a can of Coca-Cola. The creator narrates the steps throughout, describing it as an easy, good dinner.

18107810747582247.summary: This is a top-down cooking tutorial video titled 'HOW TO MAKE crispy garlic parmesan chicken rolls.' The video opens with the finished product: several golden-brown, crispy rolled tortillas on a white plate with red trim, served with a small bowl of creamy dipping sauce. A hand picks up a roll, cuts it open, and pulls it apart to reveal a cheesy, creamy chicken filling with visible pieces of red pepper. The tutorial then shows the preparation process: diced raw chicken is seasoned with spices and oil in a glass bowl, then cooked in a pan until browned. Diced red bell pepper is added and sautéed with the chicken. In the same pan, minced garlic is cooked, followed by cream, shredded cheese, and seasonings to create a thick sauce, into which the cooked chicken mixture is stirred back in. A flour tortilla is placed on a blue-and-white patterned plate, filled with the chicken mixture and additional shredded cheese, then tightly rolled. The rolls are placed seam-side down in a hot oiled skillet and fried until crispy and golden brown on all sides. The video focuses entirely on the food preparation with clean visuals and no dialogue or people visible beyond hands.

18486889045105442.summary: A young woman in a modern kitchen demonstrates a quick alternative to instant noodles. She holds up two eggs and explains she wants something fast but not instant noodles, then boils the eggs together with a block of udon in one pan. While they cook, she makes a sauce in a blender using miso paste, sesame oil, salt, and honey, blending it into a creamy mixture. Once done, she transfers the cooked noodles and eggs to a bowl, pours the sauce over them, peels and halves the soft-boiled eggs, and tops the dish with pan-fried mushrooms seasoned with paprika and cumin. She adds chili oil from a brand called White Mausu that was sent to her, snips fresh spring onions she grows herself directly onto the bowl, and finishes with a close-up of the finished meal. She then sits on a couch and eats the noodles with chopsticks. The video is presented as an easy, ~5-minute recipe with a friendly, conversational tone.

17916757308442608.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make Taiwanese popcorn chicken using a COSORI air fryer. The video opens with the finished dish—golden, crispy chicken pieces with Thai basil—and she describes it as 'so crispy' and 'so easy,' claiming it's better than the fried version. She then shows the preparation: cutting raw chicken into bite-size pieces, marinating for 30 minutes with soy sauce, rice wine, grated ginger, minced garlic, five-spice powder, salt, brown sugar, and white pepper. After marinating, she coats the chicken in egg white, then dredges each piece in coarse tapioca starch for a light, super crunchy crust. She sprays the air fryer basket with oil, places the coated chicken in a single layer, sprays again, and air fries at 375°F for 9 minutes. She flips the pieces, sprays again, and cooks for 6 more minutes at 400°F until golden and crispy. Finally, she adds fresh Thai basil leaves and cooks for 2 more minutes, then sprinkles a five-spice salt mix. She presents the finished basket of chicken, smiling, and reiterates that it's 'so crunchy.' The setting is a modern kitchen with dark cabinets.

18085625447218082.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make her husband's favorite home-cooked meal — a simple chicken with ginger scallion sauce — using an easy rice cooker method. The video shows her adding sesame oil, water, uncooked rice, sliced onions, and raw chicken thighs into a Cuckoo CRP-P1009S rice cooker pot, then starting the cook cycle. After cooking, she removes the chicken, shreds it with tongs and scissors directly in the pot, and mixes it into the rice. Separately, she prepares a ginger scallion sauce by combining chopped green onions, minced ginger, and salt in a bowl, then pouring hot oil over it. She adds this sauce back into the rice cooker, sprinkles toasted sesame seeds on top, and plates the finished dish as a molded mound of rice with chicken. Finally, she tastes the meal on camera, describing it as comforting, full of flavor, and truly the easiest one-pot dinner.

18431132914183059.summary: A short-form cooking video demonstrates how to make three-ingredient tahini cookies. On-screen text reads: 'One day someone will tell you to mix tahini with almond flour and maple syrup to make chewy nutritious cookies. It's very important you listen to them.' Visually, a person pours tahini, then almond flour, then maple syrup into a glass bowl, mixes with a spoon, rolls the dough into balls by hand, flattens them on a parchment-lined baking sheet, sprinkles sesame seeds on top, bakes them briefly, and removes golden-brown cookies from the oven. The finished cookies are shown broken open to reveal a soft, chewy interior. The video ends with a small child in pajamas holding a cookie and saying 'So good.' The creator's caption describes the recipe as healthy, easy, and kid-approved, posted by @lovinglylina in Atlanta, Georgia in September 2026. The tone is warm, instructional, and family-friendly.

17946812655313643.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating how to make Spicy Chicken Basil Stir-Fry. The video opens with diced chicken thighs in a glass bowl being marinated with soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper powder, and potato starch, then mixed thoroughly. Separately, a hand fries chopped green onions in a hot pan and cracks an egg directly onto them, creating a crispy-edged fried egg. The marinated chicken is then added to the pan and stir-fried until cooked through. Garlic, ginger, sliced shallots, and onion are added next, followed by small amounts of miso paste, doubanjiang chili bean paste, sweet soy sauce, and regular soy sauce, which coat the chicken in a glossy, savory sauce. A large handful of fresh Thai basil leaves is tossed in last and quickly wilted. The finished stir-fry is plated over a mound of white rice on a dark plate, topped with the green-onion fried egg, additional chopped green onions, and toasted sesame seeds. On-screen text emphasizes the umami from miso, the gentle kick from doubanjiang, and the importance of fresh Thai basil, noting the recipe works with ground beef, tofu, or chicken. The tone is calm, instructional, and appetizing, focused on simple technique and flavor building in a home kitchen setting.

18127955677755656.summary: A fitness and food creator named Anupriya documents a full day of vegetarian eating in 2026, framed around her goal of building lean muscle after losing 15 pounds. The video opens with her in athletic wear at home and in the gym, explaining she will show how she fuels workouts. Her morning starts with creatine and electrolyte supplements, followed by a homemade hot maple matcha latte. Breakfast is a honey pistachio cottage cheese toast (27g protein). She eats a banana as a pre-workout snack before training. After the gym, she makes lunch: smashed tofu and bean tacos topped with pickled onions and yogurt green chutney (25g protein). On a Saturday midday coffee walk, she gets an iced coffee. For dinner she prepares tofu kimchi fried rice with scallions and frozen vegetables (30g protein), noting it was flavorful and spicy. Dessert is a chocolate froyo creami (17g protein). Throughout, she emphasizes balanced, high-protein vegetarian meals, tags supplement brands, and maintains an instructional, upbeat tone focused on fitness nutrition.

17893365327673401.summary: The video is a cooking demonstration for high-protein chickpea cookies, presented by two men. An older man with gray hair and glasses in a white chef's coat introduces the concept outdoors, stating 'if you add peanut butter to chickpeas.' A younger muscular man with glasses and a beard, wearing a blue tank top, then demonstrates the full recipe indoors. He combines chickpeas, peanut butter, honey, vanilla extract, baking powder, and Himalayan pink salt in a glass bowl, blends the mixture smooth with an immersion blender, stirs in dark chocolate chips, and forms the dough into small cookies. He places them in a Ninja air fryer and cooks at 170°C for 12 minutes. After cooking, he removes the cookies, describes them as 'very fudgy,' and states each contains about 110 calories, 5g protein, and 4g fiber. He calls the recipe 'beautiful,' credits 'Recipes by AI,' gives it a 'Rating- 10/10,' and says it is 'definitely worth a try' and 'amazing.' The tone is enthusiastic and instructional, focused on healthy snacking.

18114000817819153.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video posted in September 2026 by @thetwincookingproject (Sheenam & Muskaan) for Ganesh Chaturthi. The video demonstrates how to make 'CRISPY AIR FRIED JAGGERY AND COCONUT RICE PAPER ROLLS,' described as modak-inspired. The process begins with the finished product: translucent crispy rolls filled with a brown coconut-jaggery mixture, served on a banana leaf with chopped pistachios and a creamy yellow saffron coconut syrup for dipping. The tutorial then shows the steps in order: melting ghee in a pan, adding desiccated coconut and crushed jaggery with cardamom powder, and cooking until combined. Rice paper sheets are softened in water, filled with the mixture, rolled tightly (with a double layer for crispness), brushed with ghee, and air-fried until bubbly and golden. Separately, coconut milk is heated with sugar, saffron-infused water, and cornflour slurry to make a thick syrup. The final shots return to the plated rolls being broken open to show the filling and dipped into the sauce. The tone is instructional, calm, and appetizing, focused entirely on the recipe.

18152001961458650.summary: The video presents a step-by-step recipe for a 'cosy dinner' described as better than takeout. It opens with the finished dish: a bowl of white rice topped with golden fried chicken pieces in a yellow corn sauce, garnished with chopped green onions. The creator then demonstrates the process: raw chicken breast is cut into bite-sized pieces on a wooden board, placed in a metal tray, and marinated with white pepper, salt, Shaoxing wine, and light soy sauce. For the chicken coating, cold oil and corn flour are added to a cold pan, mixed, then heated before the marinated chicken is coated and fried until golden and crispy, then removed to a plate. In the same pan, corn kernels, minced garlic, chicken stock, water, salt, and creamed corn are combined to form the sauce. A beaten egg and a cornstarch slurry are stirred in to thicken it, creating a classic Cantonese corn sauce. Finally, the sauce is ladled over rice in a bowl, the fried chicken is arranged on top, and it's garnished with green onions. On-screen text emphasizes the comforting nature of the meal.

18099390287127107.summary: In a bright home kitchen, creator Caitlin Shoemaker (@frommybowl) films "episode 2" of meal prepping for her husband as a Father's Day gift for June. She prepares two high-protein, no-reheat recipes with a loosely Thai-inspired flavor. First, she presses and cubes tofu, tosses it in a marinade, and bakes it. While the tofu cooks, she uses an Instant Pot to cook quinoa, then chops red cabbage, red bell pepper, carrots, cilantro, and edamame. She blends a creamy peanut-coconut-lime dressing and mixes everything into a colorful rainbow quinoa salad. Second, she makes strawberry overnight oats: she blends strawberries with plant milk, pours the mixture over oats, chia seeds, yogurt, and maple syrup, folds in chopped fresh strawberries, portions into jars, and tops with sliced almonds. She assembles lunch containers with the baked tofu and quinoa salad. Her husband briefly appears to give a thumbs-up. The tone is warm, instructional, and domestic, aimed at sharing easy vegan meal-prep ideas.

17987415764860202.summary: A man with a beard, wearing a dark hoodie and apron, presents a cooking tutorial in a home kitchen for 'banging firecracker chicken noodles.' He begins by showing the finished dish, then prepares the sauce in a metal bowl, adding Sriracha, light soy sauce, honey, freshly grated garlic and ginger, and chili flakes, noting it's meant to be spicy. He seasons sliced chicken in a separate bowl with garlic powder, paprika, and salt. After heating olive oil in a large pan, he cooks the chicken until browned, describing the pieces 'hugging' and forming a 'jacuzzi of chicken juices,' then removes them. Using the leftover oil, he stir-fries garlic and ginger, followed by white onion, red bell pepper, and carrot. He pours in the prepared firecracker sauce, lets it reduce, returns the chicken, then adds pre-cooked easy wok noodles and a splash of water to combine. He finishes with sesame seeds, chopped spring onion greens, and sesame oil, tastes the steaming noodles, comments on the heat level, plates the dish, garnishes with fresh cilantro, and takes a bite. The tone is casual, conversational, and instructional throughout.

18354951898216641.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial posted in September 2026 by creator @lhealthy__, showing how to make banana bread with cottage cheese. The video opens with a sun decoration, then displays the finished golden-brown loaf with text stating 'This banana bread has cottage cheese inside – no sugar, all protein.' The creator mixes mashed ripe bananas, eggs, cottage cheese, almond milk, and sugar-free maple syrup in a floral bowl, adds dry ingredients (whole wheat pastry flour, almond flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, salt), folds in dark chocolate chips, pours the batter into a parchment-lined loaf pan, tops it with sliced banana and a dusting of cinnamon, and bakes it. The final shots show the baked loaf being sliced to reveal a moist interior with chocolate chips. The accompanying caption lists the full recipe and markets it as naturally sweetened with banana and sugar-free maple syrup, with no refined sugar. The audio is soft instrumental piano music throughout. The overall tone is wholesome, health-focused, and instructional, aimed at busy mornings and family-friendly eating.

18096977915072025.summary: A man with glasses and a beard, wearing a light-colored sleeveless shirt, watches a recipe video on his phone for 'Malai Chicken Keema' and decides to recreate it. In a kitchen with blue ambient lighting, he heats oil and ghee in a pan, adds whole spices including cardamom and cinnamon, then ginger-garlic paste and chopped green chilies. He adds 400g of chicken mince and cooks it, while separately blending boiled onions with curd/yogurt into a smooth paste. He pours the onion-yogurt mixture into the pan, seasons with cumin powder, garam masala powder, black pepper powder, and salt, stirs, adds water, covers the pan, and simmers for 10 minutes. After uncovering, he adds fresh cream and chopped coriander, mixes, and presents the finished creamy keema. He notes it contains 450 calories and 50g protein per serving, then eats it with flatbread, describing it as 'super duper creamy,' giving it a 9/10 rating and calling it a fabulous recipe.

18123800732501564.summary: A creator demonstrates three quick recipes to transform a plain container of Good Culture cottage cheese into high-protein dips. The video opens with text stating '1,000 dip recipes later' and introduces the concept. Recipe 1 is a green vegetable dip: the cottage cheese is blended smooth with an immersion blender, then mixed with chopped avocado, herbs, and olive oil, and shown spread on toast. Recipe 2 is Spinach Artichoke Dip: grated parmesan, lemon juice, olive oil, and spices are blended smooth, then chopped spinach and artichoke hearts are folded in, served with toast. Recipe 3 is Buffalo Chicken Dip: cottage cheese is blended smooth, Frank's RedHot sauce is stirred in, then shredded chicken and chopped green onion are added, resulting in an orange creamy dip eaten with a chip. The creator appears on camera wearing a cap and t-shirt, holding the finished dips. The video ends with a call to action to comment 'yes' for the recipes. The tone is instructional, upbeat, and focused on easy, healthy snack preparation.

17903124030507969.summary: The video opens with a woman in a modern white kitchen carrying a Trader Joe's paper bag, with on-screen text reading 'dinner when I'm too tired after a Trader Joe's run.' She holds up two packages of frozen miso black cod, indicating it's a Nobu-style dupe. She begins cooking by adding rice, water, olive oil, and sliced mushrooms to a stainless steel pan on the stove, covering it to simmer. Separately, she opens the fish packages and places the marinated fillets into a baking dish, which she slides into the oven. She also steams a bunch of broccolini in a pot, drains it, and seasons it. She assembles the meal in a three-compartment stainless steel tray — fish in one section, mushroom rice in another, and broccolini in the third — and places a pink-handled fork on it for her child. The child is shown eating the fish with a fork at a table with coloring sheets. The woman then plates her own portion on a white dish and sits at the table to eat, commenting on the texture and seasoning while interacting with her child about school and friendship. The tone is casual, domestic, and relatable, showing a practical parent-friendly meal solution.

18086523755423282.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make a no-bake stuffed date dessert in a bright home kitchen. The video opens with on-screen text thanking the original recipe creator. She lines a baking sheet with parchment paper, then splits Medjool dates open and removes pits. She fills each date half with Toonie Moonie Organics vanilla marshmallow creme using a knife, then tops the cream with a Simple Mills Sweet Thins Honey Cinnamon seed-and-nut cracker. Next, she spoons melted dark chocolate over each assembled bite and finishes with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. The final shots show her picking up a finished treat and breaking it in half to reveal the stretchy marshmallow interior between the date, cookie, and chocolate coating. The creator's caption frames it as a healthy, easy sweet treat, and the overall tone is calm, instructional, and appreciative.

18091029638439045.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make her preferred protein pancakes using cottage cheese instead of protein powder. The video opens with finished pancakes topped with sliced banana, cream, and lime zest. She holds a bowl of cottage cheese and explains via on-screen text that this is the only protein pancake she will eat, having made it for over three years after trying dozens of recipes. She blends the cottage cheese into a smooth base, then mixes in melted butter, eggs, and honey (from a jar labeled 'Sweet Aloha'). Flour is added to create a thick batter, which she notes creates the creamiest texture and is even better the next day, making it ideal for meal prep. The pancakes are cooked until golden brown with a crispy outside and moist inside. She prepares a topping by peeling fresh bananas from a tree, whipping a creamy mixture, and assembling the dish with banana slices, cream, and lime zest. She tastes the final product on a porch and expresses that it is seriously addictive.

18025863140897645.summary: A working mom identified as Bri (@breezymumsy) films herself in the driver's seat of a car to share her "monthly meal plan" system she has used for months. She explains she refuses to cook more than three times a week because she is tired after work, so she created a two-week rotation: Weeks 1 & 3 repeat the same dinners, and Weeks 2 & 4 repeat a different set. Each cooking day she doubles the recipe, creating leftovers that cover the next day, resulting in six days of dinner covered from three cooks. Day seven is a free-for-all or takeout. She emphasizes sustainability and budgeting, showing screenshots of her Walmart app lists titled "July - Sept Week 1 & 3 Dinners" ($72.87 for 24 items) and "Week 2 & 4 Dinners," demonstrating how she adds ingredients to cart once to know weekly costs. On-screen text reinforces key points like "I'm only cooking 3 days," "Meals rotate every other week," and "Double every recipe!" The tone is enthusiastic, practical, and relatable, aimed at busy parents seeking to reduce daily cooking stress. Posted August 31, 2026, with hashtags #realmomlife and #mealplanner.

17982691347065116.summary: The video is a first-person (POV) cooking clip showing how to make a single-serve chocolate chip cookie using an air fryer. On-screen text reads 'pov: you have an airfryer and want a chocochip kookie' with cookie emojis. The creator mixes wet ingredients (sugar, brown sugar, oil, vanilla) in a small white bowl, adds flour and chocolate chips, forms the dough into a ball, places it on parchment paper, and bakes it in the air fryer. The finished large, golden-brown cookie with melted chocolate chips and sea salt is removed, placed on top of vanilla ice cream in a bowl, broken apart with a spoon, and eaten. The creator also holds up the cookie, breaks it in half to show the gooey interior, and takes bites. The setting is a kitchen with a checkered wooden surface and heart-patterned parchment paper. Audio includes a voiceover describing it as 'the best eggless single serve chocolate chip cookie recipe.'

18101486054256293.summary: The video is a short cooking demonstration for 'No Boondi Boondi Laddoos.' It opens with a close-up of finished golden-brown round laddoos in a light blue bowl, with on-screen text stating the name. A hand picks one up and breaks it open to show the granular interior. The preparation is then shown step-by-step: a grainy ingredient (identified in audio as amaranth) is sifted into a metal pan, water is added, and the mixture is cooked and stirred with a turquoise spatula until it thickens into a paste. A purple packet of 'Beyond The Sugar super sweetener' (monkfruit and allulose, zero calorie) is displayed and spooned into the mixture, which is stirred again. Finally, the warm mixture is rolled by hand into smooth balls. The audio explains this is a perfect, guilt-free option for Janmashtami bhog, made by soaking amaranth for 2-3 hours, boiling it, and adding the sweetener along with nuts, saffron, and cardamom.

18107609675111917.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make Hyderabadi Coriander Chicken. The video opens with the finished dish being poured from a pan onto a green plate, showing bite-sized fried chicken pieces coated in a creamy white sauce flecked with green coriander. On-screen text reads, 'Why did I never try Hyderabadi Coriander Chicken before?! 😭💚'. The process is then shown in sequence: raw diced chicken is placed in a white bowl, an egg is cracked over it, followed by spoonfuls of white flour/starch, which are mixed together. The battered chicken is then deep-fried in hot oil in a black kadai until golden brown and crispy, then removed to a patterned plate. In a separate clean pan, chopped garlic, green chilies, and herbs are sautéed in oil, seasoned with salt, then a white liquid (likely cream or yogurt) is added along with a large amount of chopped fresh coriander. The fried chicken is returned to the pan, tossed to coat thoroughly in the creamy coriander sauce, and finally plated again. The video has no spoken narration, only ambient kitchen sounds of mixing and frying, and maintains a bright, appetizing, home-cooking aesthetic throughout.

17906281326551630.summary: A young man in a black shirt sits at a wooden table in a home kitchen and presents a recipe for Taiwanese popcorn chicken marketed as weight-loss friendly. He explains that while restaurant versions are around 1,000 calories, his air-fried version tastes just as good with roughly half the calories. He demonstrates the process: marinating raw chicken pieces with seasonings, coating them in coarse potato starch (instead of flour and deep-frying), then cooking in an air fryer. After cooking, he tosses the chicken with fried basil leaves, five-spice powder, and white pepper. He tastes the finished dish, reacts enthusiastically, and exclaims that it is 'too fucking good.' The tone is casual, instructional, and promotional of a healthier cooking method.

18107687480597529.summary: The video is a short, upbeat cooking demonstration set to instrumental music. It opens with a close-up of a thick, glossy chocolate-colored mousse in a jar, with on-screen text reading "dates + cacao + cottage cheese = trust me." The creator then shows the ingredients one by one: a container of Good Culture 4% Milkfat Classic Cottage Cheese, which is spooned into a blender cup; cacao powder added from a measuring cup; pitted dates broken open and dropped in; milk poured over; and a pinch of coarse salt. The ingredients are blended until smooth, resulting in the same rich chocolate mousse shown at the start. The final product is scooped into a small patterned bowl and garnished with fresh raspberries and chocolate chips. The visual style is clean and focused on the food, with a red-and-white striped background.

18084936140689475.summary:
This is a cooking demonstration video from 'Chef Srijan' presenting a recipe described as comfort food: juicy, tender chicken drenched in a light, soothing broth with gentle flavors. The video opens with close-ups of the finished dish—shredded chicken mixed with herbs, chili oil, and broth being spooned over white rice in a patterned bowl.

The tutorial then shows the step-by-step process: placing raw chicken legs in a decorative bowl set inside a larger pot, adding sliced ginger, scallions, and dried chilies, covering, and steaming for 15-20 minutes. Meanwhile, finely chopped ginger, scallions, and coriander are sautéed in oil with chili oil to create a flavor base. After steaming, the chicken is removed, the collected broth is shown ('liquid gold'), and the chicken is shredded by hand on a plate. The sautéed herb mixture is seasoned with salt, white pepper, soy sauce, and oyster sauce, then combined with the shredded chicken and the hot broth. The final dish is presented as incredibly comforting, surprisingly healthy, and packed with protein, meant to be eaten like a warm hug over rice.

17950369476257666.summary: This is a short, visually-driven food recipe video posted in September 2026 by creator Emily Bonner (@_eating_with_emily). Set to gentle acoustic guitar music, the video demonstrates how to make a Greek breakfast she discovered on the island of Skopelos. The sequence begins with a finished dish in a rustic ceramic bowl, then rewinds to show assembly: two large scoops of thick Greek yogurt are placed in the bowl, followed by a generous drizzle of runny tahini, then honey, and finally topped with chopped toasted hazelnuts. On-screen text reads "You need to try this breakfast I discovered in Greece" throughout. The caption provides the full ingredient list and credits brands Belazu (tahini) and Lancashire Farm. The overall tone is warm, appetizing, and travel-inspired, emphasizing simple, healthy Mediterranean flavors with bright natural lighting and close-up food shots.

18220256359337219.summary: This is a bright, sunlit cooking tutorial by dietitian Manuela Helbing (@by_manuela) demonstrating her "Salted Caramelised Date Fro-Yo" recipe. The video opens with the finished dessert being drizzled with olive oil and eaten from a metal sundae cup. It then walks through the process in reverse order: mixing Greek yogurt with honey and freezing it flat on parchment paper; halving Medjool dates and caramelizing them in olive oil until sticky and slightly charred; blitzing the cooled dates with tahini and salt in a food processor; adding broken shards of the frozen yogurt and blending until creamy with date pieces throughout; transferring the mixture to a container for a final freeze; and finally scooping it into bowls, topping with extra caramelized dates, olive oil, and flaky salt. The creator tastes the result with evident enjoyment. The tone is calm, instructional, and appetizing, emphasizing the dessert as sweet, salty, creamy, and tangy. Audio includes her narration explaining the steps and noting it's perfect for summer.

17882567805682095.summary: The video opens on a finished snack bowl containing two scoops of purple ice cream, a round chocolate-coated treat sprinkled with sea salt, fresh blackberries, and pomegranate arils, with on-screen text reading "'What's for snacks?' me." It then shows the preparation process: a hand opens a container of FAGE Total 5% Greek yogurt and spoons it into a small ramekin. A vibrant purple paste is added and mixed in, followed by a drizzle of an amber-colored liquid (likely honey or syrup). The mixture is transferred onto a cheesecloth, gathered, and squeezed to drain excess liquid, forming a dense purple mass. This mass is placed in a shallow dish, shaped into a dome, and covered with melted dark chocolate using a spoon. Sea salt flakes are sprinkled on top. The finished chocolate dome is arranged on a plate alongside blackberries and pomegranate seeds, and two scoops of the same purple ice cream are added. The video concludes with a clear spoon breaking into the chocolate shell to reveal the purple interior, mirroring the opening shot.

18068574875709982.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial posted in August 2026 by creator Ashley (@eat_figs_not_pigs), a California-based vegan cookbook author. The video demonstrates how to make Thai Basil Tofu Stir-Fry, presented as a fast, beginner-friendly weeknight dinner that "converts all tofu skeptics." Visually, it opens with the finished dish being tossed in a black wok—crumbled golden-brown tofu mixed with wilted green Thai basil leaves and whole red chilies—then shows it spooned over white rice in a red bowl. The process is shown in sequence: mixing a dark sauce in a mason jar, pan-frying shredded tofu until crisp, adding diced onion and garlic, stirring in chopped red chilies, pouring in the sauce, and finishing with a large handful of fresh basil that wilts into the mixture. The audio narration reinforces the visual steps, emphasizing minimal ingredients, about 30-minute cook time, and the dish's crispy, savory, slightly spicy profile inspired by classic pad kra pao. The tone is upbeat, appetizing, and instructional, with no humor, innuendo, or controversial content. The post includes a call-to-action to comment "RECIPE" for the link.

18141616621571611.summary: A cooking tutorial video posted August 25, 2026 by creator @niharikamakes demonstrates making 'Chili Cottage Cheese Toast.' The video opens with the finished toast being sliced, showing melted cheese, green pepper, red onion, and chili flakes, with on-screen text stating '18g protein | 240 cal.' The creator then shows the preparation steps: finely dicing green bell pepper, red onion, green chili, and cilantro on a wooden board; combining them with cottage cheese in a glass bowl; spreading the mixture onto a slice of sourdough bread; topping with grated mozzarella; air-frying at 400 degrees for 7-8 minutes until golden; and finishing with chili flakes. The creator, wearing a gray tank top, then eats a piece dipped in sauce. The audio narration explains the dish tastes like pizza, is high-protein, uses simple ingredients, and is quick to make. The overall tone is instructional, casual, and health-focused, promoting an easy high-protein breakfast.

17910426897421855.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates how to make air fryer crispy cauliflower bites. The video opens with a close-up of the finished golden-brown, sesame-seeded cauliflower served with a creamy herb dip. She tastes it and addresses viewers who dislike vegetables, encouraging them to try the recipe. She then walks through the preparation: removing leaves from a whole head of cauliflower, cutting out the stem, breaking it into florets, washing them, and boiling until fork-tender. For the coating, she mixes King Arthur flour with Sadaf chickpea flour (noting it adds protein and fiber), spices, and water to create a thick batter, joking it should stick "like your toxic ex." She crushes cornflakes with nutritional yeast for the crunchy outer layer, dips each boiled floret in batter then crumbs, places them in an air fryer basket, sprays with Algae Cooking Club oil, and cooks until crispy. The video ends with her enjoying the finished snack, presented as a healthy, vegan, gluten-free alternative for vegetable skeptics.

18100008829756505.summary: This video is a concise and visually appealing tutorial on how to prepare Malai Broccoli, an appetizing Indian dish. The creator begins by demonstrating the preparation of the broccoli, showing how to blanch fresh florets in boiling water. Next, she meticulously prepares the marinade by combining hung curd with an array of flavorful spices like ginger garlic paste, crushed green chilies, corn flour, mozzarella cheese, lemon juice, cream, black pepper powder, chaat masala, kasuri methi, chili flakes, and oregano. She then mixes the marinated broccoli bites thoroughly before placing them into the basket of a Philips air fryer. After cooking them at 180°C for 12 minutes, she presents the golden-brown broccoli bites on a decorative plate alongside a creamy yogurt dip garnished with chili flakes and herbs. The dish is garnished with a decorative swirl of red onions. Throughout the video, the creator narrates the recipe steps in a cheerful and inviting tone, guiding the viewer through each stage with clarity and warmth.

18116837512934008.summary: A woman in denim overalls stands in a home kitchen and addresses criticism she has received about her recipes using too much sugar and being unhealthy, showing on-screen comments questioning the sugar content. In response, she decides to make a chocolate self-saucing pudding. She demonstrates the recipe step-by-step: mixing 1/3 cup sugar, 1 cup plain flour, baking powder, cocoa, salt, one egg, half cup milk, and 3 tablespoons oil into a batter and placing it in a dish. She then mixes 1/4 cup cocoa with 3/4 cup brown sugar and sprinkles it over the batter, before pouring 2 cups of boiling water on top — noting this method is also used in Italy. After baking, she explains the cake rises to the top while the liquid becomes sauce at the bottom, and shows the finished pudding with rich sauce. She concludes by saying she will put the full recipe in the caption and jokes that if viewers don't like sugar and baking, they shouldn't follow her.

18443398966126562.summary: A female nutritionist presents a recipe for 'Sticky Peanut Chicken Noodles' in a bright kitchen setting. The video opens with close-ups of the finished dish being lifted with forks and chopsticks, overlaid with text identifying it as 'A Nutritionist's STICKY PEANUT CHICKEN NOODLES' and nutritional stats '50:10:30 - 50G PROTEIN • 10G FIBRE • 30 MINS'. She explains she is a nutritionist and the meal delivers 50 grams of protein and 10 grams of fiber in under 30 minutes. The process shows ground chicken being cooked in a pan, then mixed with a red gochujang-based sauce until sticky and caramelized. Separately, udon noodles are tossed with a creamy peanut butter, miso, soy, lime, and ginger sauce. The dish is assembled in a white bowl: noodles first, topped with sliced cucumber, cilantro, the sticky chicken, a squeeze of lime, and crushed walnuts. The creator, identified in the post as Jennifer Medhurst, tastes the final dish and reacts positively. The tone is instructional, appetizing, and health-focused, emphasizing quick, high-protein, plant-point rich cooking. The location is listed as Los Angeles, California, USA, posted August 30, 2026.

18118904713851449.summary: This is a short-form cooking video by creator @_dishcovery demonstrating how to make 'miso butter caramelized onion noodles.' The video opens with a close-up of the finished dish in a blue-and-white patterned bowl, topped with chives, black sesame seeds, crispy fried onions, and miso rayu. The creator narrates the process while on-screen text reinforces steps. First, sliced onions are added to an orange pan and caramelized low and slow. Meanwhile, a sauce is prepared in a small brown cup by whisking together honey, soy sauce, and white miso paste (from @wearesaitaku), then loosened with starchy noodle water. Udon noodles are cooked separately. Once the onions are deeply golden, butter and pressed garlic are melted into them. The cooked noodles and miso sauce are tossed together until glossy. The noodles are plated, then garnished with chopped chives, black sesame seeds, extra fried onions, and a spoonful of @uce.rayu miso rayu chili crisp. The tone is cozy, instructional, and appetizing, emphasizing comfort-food flavors of buttery, mellow, and deeply umami.

18102979451524423.summary: This is a short-form cooking video presented as 'Episode 8' of a series called 'Michelin on a minimum wage,' aimed at people with expensive tastes but limited budgets. The creator demonstrates making Prawn, Ginger & Scallion Oil Noodles priced at £2.90 per portion. Visually, the process begins with oil being poured into a speckled frying pan, followed by chopping fresh green scallions on a wooden board. The chopped scallions are added to the hot pan and stir-fried, then minced ginger is incorporated. Raw prawns are added next and cooked until pink, after which a dark savory sauce is poured over the mixture. Separately, wide flat noodles are boiled in a pot of water, then transferred into the pan with the prawn-scallion sauce and tossed to coat. The finished dish is shown glossy and saucy, garnished with extra chopped scallions. The creator, wearing a dark blue top and patterned headscarf, lifts the noodles with chopsticks and presents them to the camera with an expressive, enthusiastic reaction. The audio narration matches the on-screen text, welcoming viewers to the budget-Michelin concept.

17972055581934609.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial posted August 29, 2026 by creator @ana.potard (Ana's Kitchen). Set to upbeat instrumental music with a female vocal track, the video demonstrates making 'SPICED-BUTTER YOGURT EGGS.' Hands prepare a garlicky yogurt base by combining Greek yogurt with minced garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, chopped parsley, salt and pepper in a white scalloped bowl, then mix until creamy. The mixture is spread onto a matching plate. Two soft-boiled eggs are placed on top, followed by fanned sliced avocado and halved cherry tomatoes. The eggs are cut open to reveal jammy yolks. Separately, butter is melted with paprika, chili flakes, and turmeric to create a warm spiced butter, which is drizzled over the assembled dish. On-screen text highlights 'The spiced butter that makes these yogurt eggs so addictive...' The final shots show the dish being scooped with bread. The tone is cozy, instructional, and appetizing, focused entirely on food preparation with no dialogue, jokes, or controversial content.

17918026740404302.summary: This is a short-form recipe video by creator @doctorbowl (Divya Sharma, identified as a GP) demonstrating a chocolate banana chia pudding. Filmed top-down in a blue-speckled bowl, the video shows a peeled banana being mashed, then layered with yoghurt, chia seeds, cocoa powder, and milk (visually censored on-screen as "M*lk"). Text overlays guide the steps: "Mix" and "Refrigerate." After chilling, the mixture is shown thickened into a creamy, speckled pudding, which is then served in a red bowl topped with blueberries, chocolate chunks, and granola. The creator's caption promotes it as tasty, thick, creamy, and easy. Viewer comments discuss texture, substitutions (blending, oat milk, applesauce), and portion size. Despite the wholesome, instructional tone and healthy-food context, the video is set to an energetic background track featuring a repetitive chant of the word "sex," creating a jarring sexual innuendo that dominates the audio experience. This incongruity makes the content potentially awkward for public viewing and results in an R rating for unsupervised 13-year-olds.

18096954173230398.summary: A woman identified as Helen Humphrey-Taylor (@helenhtaylor) films a step-by-step cooking tutorial for a lemon oat yogurt bowl, posted June 14, 2026. The video is overlaid with the text "we're leaving in 5 minutes" still me:, establishing a humorous, relatable premise about procrastinating on leaving by making an elaborate breakfast. Visually, she mashes banana in a white bowl, adds lemon zest, honey, an egg, and oats, mixes, then fries the mixture in butter in a pan until golden and crumbly. Simultaneously, she makes a quick raspberry chia jam by heating frozen raspberries with lemon juice, chia seeds, and honey in a saucepan. She assembles the bowl by spreading Greek yogurt, adding the jam, the cooked lemon oats, sliced strawberries, and a dollop of almond butter with a honey drizzle. The tone is bright, domestic, and self-deprecatingly funny, ending with her tasting the finished bowl. No dialogue is spoken; the audio consists of natural cooking sounds.

18096412328077482.summary: A registered nutritionist, Sophie Gastman (@sophiethenutritionist), presents a DIY salted caramel overnight oats recipe positioned as a cheaper, better alternative to the Marks & Spencer version priced at £2.75. The video opens with close-ups of the finished jar topped with grated dark chocolate, then walks through the method: blending pitted Medjool dates with milk, vanilla, and salt to create a caramel paste, then mixing it into a base of oats, chia seeds, Greek-style skyr/yogurt, and more milk. On-screen text highlights nutritional benefits — 23g protein and 12g fibre per serving — and cost (~£1 per portion), emphasizing satiety. She tops the jar with dark chocolate shavings, calling it 'extra vitamin P' for pleasure, and tastes it with an approving reaction. The tone is bright, educational, and promotional, encouraging viewers to get the full recipe via her Substack or by commenting. No risky content is depicted; it is a straightforward food-prep tutorial aimed at health-conscious adults.

18141126877586895.summary: The video is a top-down, close-up cooking demonstration of assembling a spicy noodle soup. It opens with a shot of the finished bowl containing thin noodles in a reddish-orange broth, topped with sliced roasted meat, a halved soft-boiled egg, chopped green onions, cilantro, and sesame seeds, with on-screen text reading 'adding this to our weekly dinner rotation.' The sequence then shows the preparation in reverse order: a hand pours the seasoned broth from a ladle into an empty white bowl, adds a portion of cooked noodles with tongs, places several slices of caramelized roasted meat beside them, sets two egg halves on top, and finishes by garnishing with fresh cilantro leaves, sliced green onions, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. A lime half and garlic bulb are visible on the wooden surface nearby. The video ends with a final close-up of the completed dish and text saying 'save for later' with a heart emoji. The tone is calm and appetizing, accompanied by gentle instrumental music.

18116209199316662.summary: A woman prepares a simple egg salad lunch in a modern kitchen. The video opens with text overlay 'it's that time again i remembered this lunch exists.' She places three brown eggs in a small metal saucepan, fills it with water from the tap, and sets it on an induction cooktop, turning the heat to 9. While the eggs boil, she finely dices a red onion and chops fresh dill on a wooden cutting board. After boiling, she peels the eggs into a white bowl and mashes them with a fork. She adds Maille Dijon mustard, mayonnaise, the chopped onion and dill, Maldon sea salt flakes, and black pepper, then mixes everything together. She slices a loaf of rustic bread, toasts a slice in a white SMEG toaster, and also slices cucumber. She spreads the egg salad generously onto the toast, tops it with several cucumber rounds, and sprinkles more pepper. Finally, she holds the plate and takes a large bite of the open-faced sandwich, appearing to enjoy it.

18458014315119999.summary: A woman in a light gray fleece jacket works behind the counter at Rebel Teahouse, preparing a Purple Rice Yogurt drink. On-screen text and dialogue show a customer asking if it is the purple rice yogurt, and she confirms it is, saying "I think this might be the last one that I make." When asked why it can't stay, she explains they sell only about two per day. She expresses that her whole team is sad about discontinuing it, but encourages the customer to try it, calling it a good thing. The video shows the preparation process: adding ingredients to a Vitamix blender, blending, pouring the speckled purple-white drink into a branded cup, and sealing it. The shop interior features pink floral ceiling decor, digital menu boards advertising May Specials, and typical tea shop equipment. The accompanying caption announces the drink's discontinuation effective 5/31/2026, shares the full recipe, and thanks loyal customers. The overall tone is bittersweet and appreciative, documenting the end of a menu item.

18088289264440426.summary: A cooking tutorial shows a person preparing steamed lentil dumplings called kadubu in a home kitchen. The video opens with text stating 'Your ancestors had protein' while holding a finished green-flecked ball, then demonstrates soaking three dals—moong dal, chana dal, and toor dal (one cup each)—with water, emphasizing that soaking is important. The soaked lentils are blended coarsely with ginger in a food processor. To the mixture, the creator adds chopped dill leaves, coriander, freshly grated coconut, optional chopped green chili, curry leaves, salt, and hing (asafoetida), then mixes well by hand. The mixture is shaped into oval balls and placed in a perforated steamer tray, which is set over boiling water on an induction cooktop and steamed for 15 minutes under a glass lid. The cooked kadubus are transferred to a bowl and served with ghee. Throughout, a female voiceover explains that ancestors consumed protein with fiber from whole grains and herbs, contrasting this with modern isolated protein powders, and claims the dish supports gut health, reduces bloating and constipation, and provides balanced nutrition. The video concludes with a prompt to DM 'DIET' for a personalized plan.

18131972221650971.summary: A creator presents their most-used kitchen tools that make cooking more functional and enjoyable, while promoting a fundraiser for 'Feed the People Bed-Stuy.' The video opens with an overhead view of tools including a cleaver, bench scraper, grater, spoon, scissors, citrus squeezer, and spatula. The creator demonstrates each item: using a metal spoon for portioning food into meal containers, pressing tofu in a pan, measuring edamame, mixing ingredients in a bowl, and using a heavy metal press by Chef Bruce Hill to cook fish for maximum contact. They highlight a 180mm Chinese cleaver from Bernal Cutlery as their most-used knife, noting its sharpness and built-in bench scraper function, and show a wooden alternative. Other favorites include a Microplane grater for garlic and spices, a yellow citrus squeezer that folds flat, a dark wood spatula for stirring, red Joyce Chen kitchen shears for cutting packages and tape, stainless steel Goldilocks cookware described as indestructible and reasonably priced, and a stone mortar and pestle from Holcomb Studios with a wooden stand. A blue cake tester is shown for checking doneness. Throughout, text overlays explain uses and praise the tools. The creator notes they carry tools in a bag, have raised over $20,000 for the charity, and directs viewers to links in their bio, extending the fundraiser through Thursday at midnight.

17874391005600492.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make a creamy stovetop oatmeal breakfast topped with mango. The video opens with an empty saucepan on a marble countertop, overlaid with text "don't forget this is an option pt2". She cracks one egg into the pan, adds rolled oats, honey or maple syrup, desiccated coconut, and milk, then places the pan on an induction cooktop set to level 6 and whisks continuously as it heats and thickens. While the oatmeal cooks, she peels a ripe mango with a vegetable peeler, slices off the cheeks, and dices the flesh into cubes on a wooden board. Once the oatmeal is silky and creamy, she transfers it to a white bowl, tops it generously with the diced mango, sprinkles additional desiccated coconut, and drizzles honey over the top. The final shots show her scooping and eating the finished bowl with a satisfied expression. The accompanying caption frames it as a summer breakfast idea featuring mango, oats, egg, and coconut, presented in a calm, aesthetic, instructional style.

18121652656667372.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video for 'Tofu Cabbage Muthiya/savory steamed dumplings,' presented as a high-protein vegetarian recipe. On-screen text states it contains 'whooping 37g protein/5g fiber' and uses '5 key ingredients.' The video opens with an oven set to 210 degrees, where a white baking dish containing formed logs is placed inside. After cooking, the golden-brown logs are removed, transferred to a cutting board, and sliced into bite-sized cubes. The cubes are then tossed in a hot black skillet, appearing to be sautéed with spices and seeds until browned, and finally poured onto a white serving plate. The ingredient showcase includes Kodiak Power Cakes Flapjack & Waffle Mix (Buttermilk), Kirkland Signature Organic Greek Yogurt Plain, Anthony's Premium Vital Wheat Gluten, Truvani Certified Organic Plant Based Protein (Unflavored & Unsweetened), a block of firm tofu, and finely shredded cabbage. The preparation sequence shows the cabbage mixed with spices, grated tofu added, and dry powders incorporated before forming the mixture into logs. The creator's caption describes the dish as soft, fluffy, packed with flavor, and ideal for meal prep, linking to a full recipe. The tone is instructional, wholesome, and promotional for healthy Indian-inspired comfort food, set to upbeat acoustic background music.

18111309917047782.summary: Creator Sarah Mackay (@liftwsarah) presents a troubleshooting guide for egg white oats, a high-protein breakfast she promotes as containing ~30g protein without powder. Opening with humor, she acknowledges online complaints that the dish turns out 'scrambled, rubbery, suspiciously eggy.' She then details three mistakes to avoid: 1) not enough water — oats should remain in starchy liquid before adding egg whites; 2) heat too high — turn heat down, whisk egg whites in slowly until frothy, then return to medium; 3) cooking too long — remove from heat once thick and creamy. The video shows step-by-step cooking in a saucepan on an induction hob, followed by plating with various toppings like chocolate, strawberries, cherries, coconut, and cinnamon. She describes the ideal result as thick, luxurious, and custard-like. Interspersed are meme clips for comedic effect. The post promotes her egg white oats e-book and workout plan, positioning the content within sustainable health and fitness.

18060549404788026.summary: This is a point-of-view cooking video demonstrating how to make mushroom roll-ups using an air fryer. The creator starts by roasting whole mushrooms, sliced red onion, walnuts, and garlic cloves with oil until caramelized, then blends them into a thick brown paste. The paste is spread onto a flour tortilla, which is tightly rolled, sliced into pinwheels, and threaded onto wooden skewers. A separate green sauce is made by blending cilantro, yogurt, lime juice, and garlic. The skewered roll-ups are brushed with a herbed oil mixture containing chopped herbs and chili flakes, then air-fried until golden and crisp. The finished roll-ups are plated, drizzled generously with the bright green sauce, and garnished with fresh herbs. The creator breaks one open to show the spiral filling, takes a bite, and makes an 'OK' hand gesture indicating approval. The tone is calm, instructional, and visually satisfying, with close-up shots emphasizing texture and color.

17864343483661430.summary: A woman presents and prepares 'Bhuna Chicken Tacos' in a bright kitchen setting. She opens by holding up a finished, golden-brown, cheese-filled taco, dipping it into a creamy white sauce, and taking an enthusiastic bite that shows a long cheese pull. The video then details the recipe: whole spices including coriander seeds, cumin, fennel, dried red chilies, bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and star anise are toasted and ground. Diced raw chicken is marinated with yogurt and the ground spice mix. In a pan, oil is heated with minced garlic, ginger, and green chili, followed by sliced onions and diced tomatoes, then the ground spices and marinated chicken are added and cooked until saucy. To assemble, a flour tortilla is placed in a hot pan, topped with shredded cheese and the bhuna chicken, folded, and pressed until crisp and golden on both sides. The finished taco is topped with a chopped red onion relish and drizzled with the creamy sauce before being eaten. The overall tone is cheerful, instructional, and focused on the appealing texture and flavor of the dish.

17979064409900267.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted by @lunches_at_home showing the preparation of a vegetarian bowl meal with homemade spicy peanut dressing. The video begins with cubed tofu being placed into a hot black skillet and dry-seared without oil until golden brown on multiple sides. Next, the dressing is made in a glass measuring cup by combining chili sauce, peanut butter, sweet soy sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil, which are stirred together before cold water is added to thin it to a pourable consistency. For assembly, a clear bowl is filled with warm white rice, topped with the seared tofu, fresh beansprouts, sliced cucumber, fried onions, chopped green onions, and toasted sesame seeds. The creamy orange-brown peanut dressing is poured generously over the top, followed by crushed prawn crackers. The final shot shows a spoon lifting a bite of the dressed bowl. On-screen text concludes with "No meat day" somehow turned into such a happy little moment! Sometimes the simplest meals really do bring the biggest smiles. The tone is calm, instructional, and positive, focused on simple home cooking.

17993266022828714.summary: This is a calm, instructional recipe video from creator @TheBalancedDish (Mal, MSc Food Scientist + Nutrition Coach) demonstrating how to make 'Creamy, High-protein Mocha Overnight Oats.' Set to gentle solo piano music, the video opens with the finished dish being stirred, then walks through the preparation: rolled oats, chia seeds, cocoa powder, maple syrup, brewed coffee, milk, and Greek yogurt are layered into a glass jar, mixed, covered, and chilled overnight. The next morning, semi-sweet chocolate chips are melted with milk in the microwave, then the oats are topped with additional Greek yogurt and drizzled with the melted chocolate. On-screen text emphasizes the nutritional benefits — 28g of protein and 10g of fiber per serving — and describes the result as tasting 'like dessert for breakfast.' The tone is clean, wholesome, and promotional of healthy meal prep, with no dialogue, jokes, or controversial content.

17891998428415131.summary: This is a short-form family cooking video posted by creators Hiral and Ankit (@hiralxankit), an immigrant couple in Ohio raising two boys. Set to upbeat instrumental music, the video demonstrates how to make 10-minute almond flour cookies to celebrate Rakshabandhan, a Hindu sibling festival. On-screen text and actions show a child adding almond flour, baking powder, melted butter, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and salt to a metal bowl, mixing the dough, lining a cookie sheet with parchment paper, and rolling dough balls with help from an adult male in a pink Google t-shirt. Text encourages recruiting the whole family. Optional chocolate chips are pressed onto the flattened cookies before they are placed in an oven set to 350°F. The finished golden-brown cookies cool on a wire rack, labeled "Ready for rakshabandhan thali," and a child is shown eagerly eating one with the caption "Couldn't wait." The tone is warm, instructional, and celebratory, emphasizing kid-friendly baking, healthy/gluten-free/vegan attributes, and sibling bonding.

18350346955220216.summary: A cooking tutorial shows the preparation of a savory soy mince noodle dish. A person pours a light-colored liquid over dry textured soy mince in a metal bowl, stirs it, then drains the rehydrated mince in a sieve. The mince is transferred to a hot pan, fried, and seasoned with oil, red chili paste, chopped green onions, dark soy sauce, sugar, broth, and a white slurry. The mixture simmers into a thick, saucy topping. Cooked udon-style noodles are placed in a ceramic bowl, topped generously with the soy mince sauce, and garnished with shredded green onions and sesame seeds. On-screen text and narration promote soy mince as high-protein, high-fiber, high-iron, low-fat, containing all nine essential amino acids plus magnesium, potassium, zinc, and B vitamins. It is described as cheap, shelf-stable, versatile, easy to cook, and delicious, especially for breakfast around 10am. The creator states his love for soy mince is a hill he would happily die on, then eats the finished dish with chopsticks.

18092263238433072.summary: In this installment of her 'Lazy Girl Dinners' series (episode 18), creator Jasmine Kim, a Korean-American mom of two, demonstrates how to make Hainanese chicken rice entirely in a rice cooker. Filmed in a bright home kitchen, she seasons boneless chicken thighs with salt, white pepper, and sesame oil, then rinses rice and adds it to a Cuckoo rice cooker with chicken broth, minced garlic, ginger, and a whole green onion stalk. She places the seasoned chicken on top, closes the lid, and starts the cook cycle. While it cooks, she prepares the signature ginger-garlic-scallion oil by combining minced ginger, garlic, and sliced green onions in a measuring cup, pouring hot oil over them, and transferring to a jar. After cooking, she removes the chicken, slices it on a cutting board alongside sliced cucumbers, fluffs the rice, and plates bowls topped with chicken, the aromatic oil, and cucumbers. She tastes the dish on camera and promotes the series as easy Asian-inspired meals for families, encouraging viewers to comment 'chicken' for the recipe and to follow for weekly lazy girl dinners. The tone is casual, instructional, and family-friendly.

17877588144518724.summary: In a bright home kitchen, creator Alfie Steiner (@alfiecooks), wearing a yellow and blue JVC apron, demonstrates a 10-minute peanut butter and chilli crisp noodle recipe. He places peanut butter, minced garlic, minced ginger, chopped spring onion, diced shallot, chilli crisp, sesame seeds, soy sauce, and rice wine vinegar into a stainless steel pan, then pours smoking hot oil over them and whisks into a sizzling sauce. He adds cooked noodles, tosses them to coat, and garnishes with more spring onion, sliced red chilli, and sesame seeds. He lifts the noodles with chopsticks, tastes them, and reacts with wide-eyed approval, calling the dish "unreal" and "ten out of ten." The video is presented as a quick, flavorful dinner solution, with on-screen text guiding the steps and a caption encouraging viewers to try it. The overall tone is upbeat, appetizing, and instructional, with no risky or controversial content.

18106342006805138.summary: Professional chef Nehal Karkera demonstrates his 'lemon and thyme chicken' meal-prep recipe in a home kitchen setting. He explains he cooks differently from typical meal prep to ensure his future self enjoys leftovers, avoiding 'boring chicken.' The process begins with mixing a marinade of oil, herbs, spices, and garlic in a glass bowl, coating raw chicken drumsticks, and letting them sit. He prepares a baking dish with sliced red onions, oil, salt, pepper, and thyme, places the marinated chicken on top, covers it, and bakes for 15 minutes until the onions soften. He then adds cubes of butter (acknowledging critics with on-screen text 'THAT'S TOO MUCH BUTTER NEHAL'), returns the dish to high heat to brown the skin, and simultaneously sautés a vegetable mix of broccoli, carrots, and potatoes. After cooking, he removes the chicken, emulsifies the pan juices with cold butter to create a sauce, plates the vegetables topped with chicken, and drizzles the sauce over. The video ends with him tasting the dish, expressing delight that he 'can eat this every day,' and directing viewers to the pinned recipe in comments. The tone is warm, instructional, and lightly humorous.

18117074140681461.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted July 8, 2026 by creator Sophie (@sophiebale_), kicking off a "Day 1" series. She demonstrates her version of Korean-style marinated soft-boiled eggs, which she calls "drug eggs" for their addictive taste. The video shows the process top-down: mixing a marinade of soy sauce/tamari, water, diced red chili, spring onion, garlic, and sesame seeds in a glass container; adding peeled 6.5-minute boiled eggs; sealing and refrigerating overnight for 24 hours. After marinating, the eggs have a dark soy color and a jammy, runny yolk. She serves one halved over a bowl of white rice topped with the marinade, chili, and scallions, emphasizing the texture and flavor. On-screen text reinforces the steps and the "jammy egg a day keeps the doctor away" hook. The tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and appetizing, aimed at home cooks looking for an easy protein-rich meal.

17896208994542239.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to prepare a dark, spiced chicken dish. The video opens with close-ups of the finished meal on a teal plate: glossy, caramelized chicken pieces served with white rice and sliced onions garnished with herbs. A hand pulls apart a chicken drumstick to show tender meat, then mixes it with rice. The process is shown in reverse order: whole spices including coriander seeds, dried red chilies, cinnamon, and cardamom are dry-roasted in a pan; raw chicken pieces are marinated with turmeric powder, salt, and other seasonings by hand; oil is heated with whole spices, then sliced onions and green chilies are sautéed until golden brown; the marinated chicken is added and cooked down until deeply browned and saucy. The final plated dish is presented again, and the video ends with a hand holding up a chicken leg while on-screen text reads 'Save & Follow for more'. The audio features traditional Indian-style music throughout. The overall tone is appetizing and instructional, typical of food content.

18021033830873860.summary: A woman with glasses and a striped shirt stands in a bright kitchen demonstrating her 'only overnight oat recipe you will ever want to make.' She builds the recipe in glass jars, adding a third cup of rolled oats (from Costco), a dash of cinnamon, two tablespoons of chia seeds, and two diced pitted dates, which she notes taste like caramel after soaking. She adds a tablespoon of peanut butter, explaining the jar contains about 500 calories and is high in fiber and protein, and offers alternatives like reducing the amount or using PB Fit powder, which she tests alongside the regular version. She pours in three-quarters cup of soy milk (noting any milk works), seals the jars, and shakes them, advising they need at least four hours in the fridge — ideally overnight. She prepares multiple jars, marks the PB Fit versions with blue lids, and later crushes three to four walnuts on top for added texture. After letting one sit, she stirs and tastes it, reacting with enthusiasm ('Oh my gosh, it's so good').
