The tone is casual, instructional, and enthusiastic, focused entirely on food preparation and personal preference testing.

18108778178102502.summary: The video opens with a man wearing glasses in a home kitchen holding a glass dish of cooked green beans, with on-screen text promising a side dish nobody gets excited about until now, achievable in 10 minutes with one toss. He introduces pre-trimmed green beans as a shortcut that saves prep time, then pours them from a bag into a metal mixing bowl. He seasons the beans step-by-step: adding salt, grinding Kirkland coarse black pepper, sprinkling Trader Joe's Cuban Style Citrusy Garlic Seasoning Blend, adding Kirkland crushed red pepper flakes for heat, and drizzling Terra Delyssa organic olive oil to help nutrient absorption. He gently massages the seasonings into the beans by hand, transfers them to a glass baking dish, and places them in a Ninja air fryer set to 10 minutes. Halfway through he tosses the beans for even crispiness. The final result shows golden-brown, slightly charred green beans coated in spices. He returns on camera holding the finished dish, noting green beans provide vitamins K, C, and folate, and encourages viewers to save the recipe and follow his account. The tone is instructional, upbeat, and health-focused, with bright kitchen lighting and clear text overlays guiding each step.

18005090795771369.summary: A tattooed man in a black t-shirt stands in a modern kitchen and demonstrates how to make a quick weeknight noodle dish. He begins by heating neutral oil in a stainless steel pan on a gas stove, adding ground pork and seasoning it with salt. While the meat cooks, he finely chops spring onions, separating the white and green parts, and smashes and minces garlic. He returns to the pan, breaks up the meat, and adds the white parts of the spring onion and garlic. He then adds a large spoonful of peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and lime juice, stirring until the peanut butter forms a glossy sauce. He adds a splash of water to thin it, noting the sauce will reduce further. For heat, he stirs in chili crisp to taste. He shows pre-cooked udon noodles from a packet, tastes the sauce, then adds the blanched noodles to the pan along with the reserved green spring onion tops, tossing everything together. He plates the steaming noodles into a bowl and eats them with chopsticks, concluding that the meal takes about 15 minutes to make.

17905996290532867.summary: This is a bright, overhead cooking video presenting a high-protein porridge recipe designed to taste like dessert. The video opens on a finished white bowl of creamy oatmeal topped with dark blueberry compote and fresh blueberries, with a spoon lifting a bite. On-screen text states: 'If you like dessert for breakfast but still want something nutritious, filling, high protein, make this recipe.' A female narrator explains she has never understood people who don't like porridge, but accepts most traditional recipes don't have enough protein to make a balanced breakfast. The preparation is shown step-by-step: milk is poured into a light-colored saucepan, an egg is cracked in, honey is drizzled from a dipper, and rolled oats are added. After cooking and stirring until thick, a dollop of white yogurt is mixed in. The porridge is transferred to a serving bowl and topped with blueberry sauce and fresh berries. The narrator notes the dish provides over 20 grams of protein per portion and can be topped with whatever you like. The setting includes a crate of eggs labeled 'OEUFS FRAIS' and a jar of honey in the background.

18089164943536235.summary: A woman with red nail polish and glasses, wearing a white t-shirt and denim apron (@crumbaleft), prepares her 'newest obsession' — savory egg muffins — in a home kitchen. The video shows a step-by-step assembly in a muffin tin lined with paper cups: she adds roasted sliced zucchini, sweet corn kernels, crumbled cooked meat, sautéed spinach, blistered cherry tomatoes, and pickled red onions into different cups. She then tops them with various cheeses including cheddar slices, crumbled feta, and shredded cheese, sprinkles dried herbs, and pours a blended yellow egg mixture from a blender over each cup. After baking, the muffins are shown golden-brown and puffed. She lifts one to display the cooked interior with visible vegetables and melted cheese. The on-screen text 'Making my newest obsession:' remains throughout. The overall tone is cozy, domestic, and focused on meal prep.

17964017262173635.summary: The video opens with an overhead shot of shredded poached chicken arranged on a pale green platter as a vibrant red chili-oil sauce loaded with chopped scallions, ginger, and sesame seeds is poured over it. A woman in a pink t-shirt tastes the chicken with chopsticks, reacting positively. The tutorial then walks through the process step by step: two raw chicken breasts are shown, then placed in a stainless steel pot with water, sliced ginger, scallion stalks, whole cloves, and peppercorns to gently poach for about ten minutes without aggressive boiling. Doneness is checked with a chopstick. The cooked chicken is removed and shredded by hand into chunky strips on a wooden board. For the sauce, chopped spring onions, ginger-garlic paste, and chopped red chilies are combined in a bowl; hot oil is poured over to release aroma, followed by soy sauce, chili oil, oyster sauce, sesame seeds, and ladles of the reserved poaching broth. The finished glossy, fragrant sauce is stirred and then generously poured over the plated chicken. The creator speaks throughout, explaining the method and encouraging viewers to try the easy high-protein dish.

18113136854000145.summary: The video is a short, visually clean food-prep reel focused on making a seasonal toast. It opens with a finished plate: toasted bread topped with cottage cheese, sliced fresh figs, chopped pistachios, and a drizzle of honey, with on-screen text reading 'Me during fig season: this easy, high-protein cottage cheese toast with figs and pistachios on repeat.' The sequence then shows the preparation steps in order: a hand places a slice of rustic bread into a black toaster; fresh dark figs are sliced on a checkered wooden board; a container of Good Culture cottage cheese is opened; the cottage cheese is spooned generously onto the toasted bread; thin fig rounds are arranged over the cheese; shelled pistachios are scattered on top; honey is drizzled over everything; and finally a light dusting of spice (likely cinnamon) is added. The final shot presents the completed toast on a textured white plate next to a colorful speckled mug, suggesting a breakfast or snack setting. The tone is calm, wholesome, and aspirational, typical of social media food content celebrating seasonal ingredients.

18111297295963015.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted in July 2026 by creator Pari Patel (@_let.her.cook__), demonstrating how to make "High Protein Oats and Ragi Cookies" (~9.5g protein per cookie). The video opens with finished cookies in an air fryer basket, then walks through the recipe step-by-step: creaming butter and brown sugar, adding chocolate protein powder and milk, then incorporating ragi flour, oats flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt, followed by folding in dark chocolate chunks. The dough is portioned onto parchment paper and air-fried in a Philips RapidAir appliance. The final shots show the soft-centered, crispy-edged cookies being broken open to reveal melted chocolate. On-screen text labels each ingredient. The tone is calm and instructional, set to a gentle jazz-style female vocal track. The video is presented as a healthy dessert recipe using millets and protein powder, with no dialogue, jokes, or controversial content.

18108982483950162.summary: This is a short-form cooking video titled 'Lazy Weeknight Dinners, Episode 1: 10-minute garlic chili noodles.' The creator demonstrates a quick recipe while noodles boil. In a stainless steel pan on a wooden board, he adds chopped shallots, minced garlic/ginger, peanut butter, sesame seeds, chili crisp, and chopped green onions. He pours hot water from a pot into the pan, mixes everything into a sauce, then adds the cooked flat noodles and tosses them to coat. The finished dish is shown being lifted with chopsticks and eaten by the creator, a young man with glasses and dark hair. The tone is instructional and casual, aimed at fast weeknight meals.

18101749498966856.summary: This is Episode 3 of the 'Iron Matters' series by creator Neha Poddar (@blwbynehapoddar), presented as a quick baby-led weaning recipe. The video demonstrates how to make 5-minute oat, banana, and raisin pancakes suitable for babies from 6 months onwards. Visually, it shows a hand peeling a ripe banana, adding it to a Sujata blender with oat flour and soaked black raisins, blending to a smooth batter, then pouring small portions into a hot cast-iron skillet with ghee and cooking on low flame until golden on both sides. The finished pancakes are shown broken open to reveal a soft interior, placed on a light-blue divided baby plate. On-screen text and narration emphasize the recipe is iron-rich, naturally sweet, and perfect for tiny tummies, encouraging viewers to save the recipe and follow for more simple iron-rich baby meals.

18113587972947487.summary: This is a 'What I eat in a day as a Nutritionist' video posted August 21, 2026 by Chandigarh-based creator Srishti Gola Lubana (@fitfusionmommy), identified as a certified nutrition coach who lost 40kg. The video documents Day 20 of a 45-day series focused on high-protein, high-fiber meals for fat loss and blood sugar stability. It opens with a chicken uttapam topped with cheese, then shows her morning routine on an empty stomach: electrolytes, Iron and Vitamin C tablets, and an anti-inflammatory tea made with turmeric and black pepper. Breakfast is a chicken veggie uttapam with avocado plus two eggs, claimed as 50g protein. She then prepares a 28g protein shake with whey isolate, creatine, and collagen. A midday snack is a fruit bowl with banana, papaya, dragon fruit, soaked almonds and walnuts (5g protein). She takes Vitamin B12. Lunch is a plate with Palak chicken, Rajma masala, and veggie rice totaling 42g protein. Later she drinks Kokum buttermilk (5g protein) and takes Omega-3. At bedtime she has chamomile tea with Magnesium and Ashwagandha. Text notes she practices 18-hour intermittent fasting. The tone is instructional and promotional, encouraging viewers to save, share, and comment 'Eat' for more recipes.

17955032313235561.summary: A woman in a modern kitchen with white cabinets and granite countertops demonstrates a one-pot meal hack. Wearing a dark t-shirt reading 'MAMA. MOMMY. MOM. BRUH.' and jeans, she opens her refrigerator and gathers ingredients including carrots, snap peas, green beans, red bell pepper, onion, tofu, and canned coconut milk. On-screen text claims DoorDash charges $18 while this costs $4. She chops the vegetables and tofu on a wooden board, rinses rice in a white ramekin, then mixes coconut milk with Panang curry paste and seasonings in another bowl. In an Instant Pot, she sautés garlic and ginger, adds curry paste, then the vegetables, pours in the curry mixture, and adds tofu cubes. She places a trivet over the curry and sets the rice ramekin on top, seals the lid, and pressure cooks. After cooking, she removes the perfectly cooked rice, stirs fresh basil into the curry below, plates the dish, tastes it, and states 'Every time. Perfect. Never fails. Ever.' The video concludes with a prompt to comment 'CURRY' and follow.

18102899621522717.summary: A blonde woman in overalls presents her 'Brown Butter Sticky Date Rice Pudding' as the first recipe in a 'Food For Burnout Month' series. She demonstrates the process step-by-step: browning butter in a cast-iron skillet, frying pitted dates until caramelized, then adding pre-cooked and cooled white rice, coconut milk, water, cinnamon, vanilla, and maple syrup. She tempers whisked egg yolks with the hot mixture before combining everything back in the pan to thicken into a creamy pudding. While cooking, she narrates the purported benefits—resistant starch from cooled rice for gut health and blood sugar control, egg yolks for brain and nervous system support, dates for magnesium/potassium, and added collagen powder for protein and satiety. The finished dish is served in a speckled bowl, topped with the sticky dates, a drizzle of brown butter, and cinnamon. The tone is warm, nurturing, and wellness-focused, positioning the pudding as comforting, easy-to-digest nourishment for stressful times, with a call to action to join her Recipe Club.

18064963505747701.summary: A woman in a brown fleece top introduces a 'Weeknight Indian' recipe for Air Fryer Tandoori Chicken Breast. She prepares the marinade in a clear glass bowl, starting with a cup of thick yogurt, then adding a colorful array of spices including Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, and salt. She adds grated ginger-garlic paste, dried fenugreek leaves, fresh lemon juice squeezed from a yellow juicer, and mixes everything into a creamy orange paste. Fresh chopped cilantro and mint are stirred in along with soy sauce and vinegar. On a green cutting board, she scores raw chicken breasts with diagonal cuts to help the marinade penetrate, then thoroughly coats the chicken by hand with the marinade. The marinated breasts are placed in a parchment-lined air fryer basket, sprayed lightly with oil, and cooked until charred and golden. The finished chicken is transferred to a speckled plate, brushed with melted ghee or butter for shine, then sliced to reveal moist, cooked-through white meat. The video opens and closes with her holding and eating a piece, emphasizing the flavor and texture. The tone is warm, instructional, and focused on quick, healthy weeknight cooking.

18051881792794795.summary: A person prepares an elaborate oatmeal dish in a modern kitchen with a white marble countertop. The video opens with text overlay 'the only correct way btw'. They place chopped dates into a small stainless steel saucepan, add milk, then rolled oats, and cook the mixture on an induction cooktop while whisking until thick. Separately, they mix a brown paste (appearing to be peanut butter) with milk in a white bowl to create a smooth sauce. A banana is peeled, sliced lengthwise, and fried in butter in a non-stick pan until caramelized. The cooked oatmeal is poured into a decorative white bowl with yellow trim, topped with the fried banana halves, a spoonful of the peanut sauce, and sprinkled with dark cacao nibs. The creator, a woman in a white sleeveless top, then eats the finished dish with apparent enjoyment. The entire sequence focuses on food preparation with close-up shots of ingredients and cooking actions.

18439256071123632.summary: The video is a short-form cooking tutorial focused on budget meal prep. It opens with a close-up of a finished savory rice dish with cubed tofu being lifted with chopsticks. On-screen text states 'my partner and I spend $50 a week on food.' The creator then demonstrates building the meal in a rice cooker: adding uncooked rice, water, diced onion, minced garlic, chopped ginger, sesame oil, and soy sauce, followed by cubed tofu. The mixture is stirred and cooked. After cooking, the lid is opened to reveal steaming rice mixed with tofu, which is fluffed and served. A voiceover explains this is the base of their meals, based on a 'rice cooker grain bowl meal formula,' and promotes an 'implementation guide' offering three recipes from two formulas, with cost breakdowns and a shopping list to stay under budget and reduce waste. Viewers are instructed to comment 'SYSTEM' to receive the link.

18162731530480782.summary: This is Episode 5 of 'The Better Bite' series by creator Geneviève Paige (@inseason.withgenevieve), filmed in Cascais, Lisbon, Portugal. The video demonstrates how to make chocolate chickpea truffles without refined sugar. The creator blends canned chickpeas, Medjool dates, cocoa powder, nut butter, vanilla, and salt in a food processor until fudgy, rolls the mixture into balls, then dips them in melted dark chocolate mixed with cacao nibs. On-screen text and voiceover emphasize that the truffles are 'fudgy, chocolatey, and so easy to make,' and that her partner, a professional French chef, could not tell they contain chickpeas. The final shots show the finished truffles on parchment paper, sprinkled with sea salt, and the creator tasting one with enjoyment. The tone is warm, instructional, and promotional of a healthier dessert alternative.

18119150539705736.summary: A male creator wearing a red-and-black checkered apron presents a one-pan Punjabi Pepper Chicken Pulao recipe. The video opens with the finished dish being uncovered and mixed, with on-screen text stating "Not gatekeeping this one pan dish anymore!" He claims the meal helps with cutting to 12% body fat, providing 35 grams of protein at 500 calories per serving, and calls it easy dinners after work. The tutorial then walks through steps: slicing two onions, washing and soaking 250g rice, heating 3 tbsp ghee, adding cumin, whole garam masala (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, mace), bay leaves, sautéing onions, then 6 crushed garlic cloves and 3 inches julienned ginger. He adds 600g chicken, cooks on high heat, seasons with 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, and 2-3 tbsp black pepper powder, stirs, adds 2 tbsp lime juice and 400ml water, then adds the soaked rice, covers and cooks 15-20 minutes. After garnishing with fresh coriander, he plates the pulao with tomato and cucumber, eats it with his hands, and gives a thumbs-up. Background audio features an upbeat country-style song with male vocals. The tone is casual, instructional, and promotional of a high-protein home-cooked meal.

18130823509717319.summary: A young boy wearing a light blue shirt stands in a home kitchen and demonstrates how to make "Shoyu Garlic Chicken Rice" using a rice cooker, part of a "rice cooker series." He begins by washing rice in a bowl, then adds water to the rice cooker pot. He sequentially adds ingredients: shoyu (soy sauce), mirin, grated garlic, and onion powder, gently mixing them together. He then adds sliced onions and raw diced chicken, spreading the chicken out before closing the lid and pressing START to cook. After cooking, he opens the rice cooker to reveal the finished dish, inverts a yellow duck-shaped bowl over a plate to mold the rice, and serves it. He says "Itadakimasu!" before eating, expressing enjoyment with "It's so goooood." The video has a cheerful, instructional tone, presented as a family-favorite recipe first made two years prior, posted by @easypeasyjordan.

18083104226217964.summary: A cooking tutorial video by creator Nícola Graham (@estaesmicocina) demonstrates how to make "Spicy Peanut Noodles," presented as a viral recipe test. The video opens with a finished bowl of noodles topped with chopped peanuts and green onion, then shows step-by-step preparation in a stainless steel bowl: adding peanut butter, grated ginger, chopped scallion, pressed garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, crushed peanuts, sesame seeds, chili crunch, and chili oil, followed by whisking into a smooth sauce. Cooked instant noodles are added and tossed to coat. The final dish is plated in a white bowl and garnished. The creator, wearing a white patterned cardigan, tastes the noodles with chopsticks and reacts positively. On-screen text reads "Spicy PEANUT NOODLES" and the Spanish caption lists ingredients and asks viewers if they've tried the viral recipe. The tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and food-focused, set in a modern kitchen with a "VIETNAMESE" cookbook visible in the background. Posted July 23, 2026.

18113021671979475.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates a quick, low-effort meal using leftover rice. On-screen text explains 'when I don't feel like cooking and there's leftover rice.' She opens a Cuckoo rice cooker containing cooked rice, then adds raw ingredients: carrot sticks, zucchini pieces, whole mushrooms, and chunks of raw chicken. She adds an optional Korean seafood stock packet and water, closes the lid, and sets the cooker to the 'porridge' setting (display shows 36 minutes). After cooking, she cuts the softened vegetables and chicken into smaller pieces inside the pot, then seasons the porridge with sesame oil, salt, and pepper. She portions the porridge into bowls and serves it on stainless steel divided trays alongside cubed radish kimchi. The video shows her placing the meals on pink placemats for children, including a toddler in a high chair whom she feeds with a small spoon. The overall tone is calm, nurturing, and practical, focused on easy family feeding.

18075240422379292.summary: This is a short-form cooking video by creator @jstplated demonstrating how to make "viral cottage cheese bagel bites." The video opens with a close-up of the finished product — small round baked bites coated in everything bagel seasoning, and others topped with melted cheddar and jalapeño slices — being broken open to show a soft, fluffy interior. The creator narrates the process while showing each step: cottage cheese is poured into a blender and blended until smooth, then mixed in a bowl with flour, baking powder, and salt to form a dough. The dough is divided into eight equal portions and rolled into balls. Each ball is dipped in milk and then rolled in everything bagel seasoning, placed on a parchment-lined tray, with some left plain and others topped with shredded cheddar and a jalapeño slice. After air-frying or baking until golden brown, the final bites are shown again. The tone is upbeat and instructional, emphasizing that the recipe is "totally worth the hype" and "so fluffy and honestly so good."

17982291123050369.summary: A young woman, wearing a brown t-shirt and denim apron, introduces herself as an 18-year-old chef preparing dinner for her sister and brother-in-law on a Tuesday night. In a modern white kitchen, she unpacks groceries from a Trader Joe's bag and proceeds to cook multiple dishes. She makes 'Lemon herb chicken Meatballs' by mixing ground chicken with breadcrumbs, chopped red onion, fresh herbs, and lemon juice, then rolls them into balls. She also prepares 'Garlic and herb Roasted potatoes' and 'Honey roasted Brussel sprouts,' washing, halving, and seasoning the vegetables before roasting. She blends a 'Whipped honey Lemon feta' dip and a 'Honey, garlic, and dill Yogurt sauce.' After cooking the meatballs in a pan and roasting the vegetables, she plates everything into bowls. Later, now in an orange sweatshirt, she tastes the meal, reacting positively while holding a plate of food. The video has a bright, casual, lifestyle-cooking aesthetic with on-screen text labeling each dish.

18144432859558052.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates how to make a savory 'bhajiya waffle' as a healthier alternative to traditional deep-fried bhajiyas. Wearing a black t-shirt, she mixes besan (chickpea flour), rice flour, vital wheat gluten, nutritional yeast, spices (turmeric, chili powder, ginger-garlic-chili paste, hing), Greek yogurt, water, and black sesame seeds into a thick batter, then folds in chopped spinach and onion. She pours the batter into a waffle maker, adds chopped green chilies on top, closes the lid, and cooks until golden brown and crispy. The finished waffle is removed, placed on a plate, garnished with fresh cilantro, and drizzled with green and brown chutneys. On-screen text emphasizes 'Crispy. Spicy. So satisfying. Made in the waffle maker. No deep frying.' The audio features upbeat instrumental music and a female voiceover inviting viewers who grew up eating bhajiyas with chai to try the twist and follow for more content. The overall tone is instructional, wholesome, and family-friendly, promoting a creative, less-oily version of a classic Indian snack.

17885303154613540.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make 'Jalapeno Poppers High Protein Toast' in a bright kitchen setting. The video opens with close-ups of finished toast slices on a wooden board, topped with melted cheese, sliced jalapeños, and a reddish-orange crumbled topping. On-screen text highlights '15 grams of protein' and '15 minutes.' She then shows the preparation: mixing mashed tofu (labeled as vegan cheese base) with shredded cheddar, chopped green bell peppers, red onion, cilantro, nutritional yeast, hemp seeds, non-dairy yogurt, salt, and black pepper. The mixture is spread onto toasted bread slices, topped with more cheese and jalapeño rings, and baked. Separately, she sautés crumbled tempeh with garlic, lime zest, and Kashmiri chili powder to create the crunchy topping. The final product is assembled by spooning the spiced tempeh over the baked toast. The creator, wearing glasses and a patterned blue top, smiles while holding a piece at the end. The tone is instructional, upbeat, and focused on healthy eating.

18116194300900269.summary: A male creator in a blue sports jersey demonstrates his 'favorite way' to make Turkish-style pasta designed to convert tofu skeptics. He starts by crushing extra-firm tofu by hand into a mince-like texture, then fries it in oil until golden brown before removing it from the pan. In the same pan he sautés diced onion and grated garlic, adds tomato paste and dried herbs/spices, cooks them down, then returns the tofu to coat it in the savory mixture. Separately, he prepares a garlicky yogurt base and makes a topping of browned bubbling butter flavored with Turkish red pepper flakes (pul biber). For assembly, he spreads the yogurt on a plate, tops with cooked farfalle pasta, adds the seasoned tofu mince, and finishes with fresh herbs, chopped tomatoes, and sliced radish. He tastes the finished dish and emphasizes that despite sounding unusual, the combination of pasta, yogurt, and tofu 'works so well.' The video ends with the 'alfiecooks at home' logo.

17980645914098665.summary: The video is a top-down, close-up demonstration of preparing a warm chicken bone broth drink. It opens on a speckled countertop where a white plate holds multiple pale, translucent, molded cubes of frozen broth in decorative shapes like flowers and bundt cakes. A person's hand reaches in, picks up one flower-shaped cube, and drops it into a light-colored ceramic mug. On-screen text reads 'healing chicken broth' and expands to 'our go to broth recipe - intentionally designed to support gut healing.' Hot water is then poured from a metal kettle into the mug, covering the cube. As the water fills the mug, the frozen broth begins to melt and dissolve, turning the water a light golden-brown color. The final shot is a static overhead view of the mug filled with the melted broth. The accompanying caption explains this is a foundational recipe from The Nutrition Clinic for gut healing, leaky gut, eczema, and inflammation, made with a whole chicken, vegetables, and herbs, and provides full ingredient and method details. The tone is calm, instructional, and wellness-focused.

18055468922543492.summary: The video opens with a title card reading "Sweet Potato Egg Tarts — zero flour, simple & healthy" over a wooden table, then shows four golden-brown finished tarts on a wooden board, one being sliced open to reveal a creamy yellow filling and a dense orange crust. The creator then walks through the preparation in reverse chronological order. Cooked sweet potato chunks are placed in a white bowl and mashed with a fork until smooth. Almond flour and a pinch of salt are added from a black container and mixed in to form a pliable dough. Small portions are pressed by hand into pink and white fluted silicone molds to create the tart shells, which are arranged on a wooden board and then placed in an oven for a pre-bake. Separately, the filling is prepared in a Pyrex measuring cup: two egg yolks are cracked in, followed by a spoonful of Greek yogurt, a drizzle of liquid sweetener, and milk, then whisked into a smooth pale-yellow custard. The pre-baked crusts are filled with the custard mixture and baked again until the tops caramelize. The final shots show the completed tarts, one broken open to display the texture, before three are plated on a decorative floral dish. The setting is a bright home kitchen with a white pot and a small plant in the background, and the tone is calm and instructional.

18094356245365767.summary: A woman identified as @wendythefoodscientist presents herself as a food scientist explaining the proper way to prepare tofu. Holding a bowl of glazed tofu, she states there is only one proper way: boiling cubed tofu in salted water instead of pressing or freezing. She credits her Chinese mom and food science, explaining via on-screen text that osmosis causes water to leave and salt to enter, the protein network opens up, leading to improved texture and better flavor absorption. Visuals show tofu boiling, then being marinated where it soaks up sauce in minutes, followed by cooked examples including stir-fry and bowls. The video concludes by promoting her 'Tofu Mastery Guide' with 17 techniques and 49 recipes, encouraging comments for a DM link. Tone is instructional, enthusiastic, and promotional.

17952419160014867.summary: This is a short-form cooking reel presenting a savory Korean-inspired shredded tofu bulgogi as a favorite plant-based meal. The video opens with a hand lifting the lid off a dark blue ceramic bowl with white marbled pattern, revealing a steaming mound of saucy, shredded tofu topped with chopped scallions and sesame seeds. On-screen text reads 'this will be your favorite way to cook tofu.' The scene cuts to a pan where the tofu, crumbled and coated in a glossy red-brown sauce, is being stirred with a wooden spatula, showing its texture and caramelized bits. The cooked tofu is then scooped generously over a bowl of white rice, filling the bowl. A hand sprinkles white sesame seeds over the top, followed by sliced green onions for garnish. The lid is placed back on the decorative bowl, closing the presentation. Throughout, the focus remains on the food's texture, color, and appetizing plating, with bright natural lighting highlighting the sheen of the sauce. The caption provides the full sauce recipe ingredients and invites viewers to comment 'RECIPE' to receive it via DM, indicating a direct engagement tactic. Comments show numerous viewers requesting the recipe, with the creator replying individually to send it privately, reinforcing the interactive format. The overall tone is instructional and appetizing, aimed at home cooks interested in Asian-inspired vegetarian recipes.

18614362720059456.summary:
This is a short-form cooking video presenting a 'thai basil tofu one pan recipe.' The video opens with a close-up of the finished dish — crumbled, saucy tofu topped with chopped green onions and basil, served over white rice in a dark bowl, with a hand squeezing fresh lime juice over it. A man in a light blue t-shirt and glasses is then shown tasting the dish with enjoyment.

The preparation sequence follows: finely diced shallots are added to oil in a hot pan, followed by minced garlic and chopped red chilies. Crumbled tofu is poured in and stir-fried until browned. A dark sauce is drizzled over the tofu, which is mixed thoroughly. Finally, sliced green onions and fresh basil leaves are added and tossed in while steaming. The cooked mixture is spooned generously over a bowl of white rice, and the video ends with a final shot of the plated meal ready to eat. The tone is clean, appetizing, and instructional, with upbeat background music and no spoken dialogue.

18156068092438471.summary: An older male chef with gray hair, wearing a white chef's coat embroidered with 'ASANEBE', demonstrates how to make his version of tasty tofu. The video opens with another person about to pour Sriracha onto a block of tofu, prompting the chef to intervene with "Wait! What are you doing? I make you tasty tofu Asanbebo Style!" He then prepares a marinade in a glass container, adding soy sauce, mirin, finely diced onion, chopped green onion, grated ginger, grated garlic, brown sugar, chili pepper, sesame oil, and sesame seeds, which he mixes and heats for one minute. He places a block of tofu into the sauce, cuts it into cubes while submerged, and explains it should marinate for a couple of hours. After marinating, he serves the tofu over a bowl of white rice, calls it "My Mayak Tofu," tastes it, and reacts with satisfaction saying "Very good" before giving a thumbs-up and repeating "Asanbebo Style!" The tone is instructional, friendly, and enthusiastic, set in what appears to be a restaurant kitchen.

18156175558494262.summary: This is a cooking demonstration video posted August 16, 2026 by creator Amisha Gurbani (@thejamlab) showing how to make 'Corn and Shishito Pepper Kofta in Corn Curry.' The video opens with the finished dish plated with garlic naan, sliced red onion, and lime wedges. The creator then walks through the process: blistering fresh green shishito peppers in a pan (noting 1 in 10 may be spicy), finely chopping them, and mixing them into a kofta batter made of grated and whole fresh corn kernels, boiled mashed potatoes, alliums, cilantro, dry spices, and cornflour. The mixture is formed into balls and deep-fried until golden brown. For the curry, she sautés whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cumin), then adds chopped onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeño, followed by boiled corn kernels, cashews, heavy cream, and dry spices. The mixture is cooked and blended into a smooth yellow sauce. The final plating shows the fried koftas served in the creamy corn curry, garnished with blistered shishito peppers, alongside naan. The tone is instructional and appetizing, emphasizing seasonal summer corn.

18109707215474744.summary: In a bright home kitchen, creator Jasmine Kim demonstrates how to make Korean mayak eggs, also known online as 'drug eggs' for being addictively tasty. She begins by boiling 12 eggs for 7 minutes, then prepares a marinade in a glass dish with 1 cup soy sauce, 1 cup water, 1/2 cup agave sweetener, diced half onion, a bunch of chopped green onion, sliced jalapeño, 2 tablespoons minced garlic, a generous drizzle of sesame oil, and 1/3 cup sesame seeds, tasting the mixture. After cooling the boiled eggs in an ice bath, she peels them and places them in the marinade, covers with a paper towel to submerge, seals the container, and instructs to refrigerate for 24+ hours. The video opens with her noting her best friend is coming over for a taste test, and the tone is casual, friendly, and instructional throughout.

18329190931278027.summary: This is a cooking video from 'Episode 10 of the Period Diaries' featuring congee with miso-glazed mushrooms. The creator presents the finished dish first—a bowl of creamy congee topped with dark glazed mushrooms, sliced green onions, sesame seeds, red chili oil, cilantro, and a lime wedge—then walks through the preparation. The process begins with rinsing white rice multiple times, then adding it to boiling water with minced ginger, garlic, scallions, and stock cubes. The mixture simmers on the stove with occasional stirring until thickened. Soft tofu is added, followed by final seasonings (soy sauce and sesame oil). The narrator describes it as her favorite recipe in the series so far, noting it's ideal comfort food when eating the same meal for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, especially during menstruation because it's gentle and 'hands-off' when cramping. The tone is calm, instructional, and cozy, focused entirely on food preparation.

18615332260024465.summary: A woman identified as Steph Bae (@happy_baes) demonstrates an easy weeknight dinner after a Trader Joe's run, dated August 14, 2026. In her bright home kitchen, she places rice, water, frozen shelled edamame, and sliced beech mushrooms into a white Cuckoo rice cooker. Separately, she seasons raw peeled shrimp with minced garlic and honey, then sautés them in a pan with butter and more honey until glazed. She opens the cooker mid-cycle to steam fresh bok choy inside for four minutes. After cooking, she mixes the rice with lime juice, chopped cilantro, and green onion, then plates it in a blue-patterned bowl topped with the honey garlic shrimp and bok choy, finishing with sesame seeds. She serves the same components in divided metal trays for a child. While eating, she and the child discuss the shrimp's texture, noting it has "just salt texture" and confirming it is honey garlic shrimp. The tone is casual, instructional, and family-oriented, emphasizing quick, convenient cooking for busy parents.

18051856460716688.summary: The video presents a POV-style cooking hack set to upbeat pop music with lyrics about acceptance. It opens with a close-up of beaten egg in a white bowl, with text overlay reading 'Pov: Wish you knew this rice paper hack.' A hand places sliced bananas into a hot non-stick pan with oil, then lays a sheet of rice paper over the bananas and egg mixture. The rice paper cooks until golden and crispy, is flipped to show the caramelized banana side, then transferred to a plate. Chocolate-hazelnut spread is spooned onto the cooked sheet, which is folded and torn open to reveal the melted chocolate and banana filling inside. The entire sequence focuses on the food preparation steps without any people visible beyond hands, and contains no dialogue, only background music.

18419133772150319.summary: A blonde female creator (@organicmindedmom) films a selfie-style shopping tour inside a Trader Joe's, titled 'Hidden Gems at Trader Joe's.' She walks through the store presenting several products she considers clean or nontoxic options. First, she holds up Trader Joe's Kettle Cooked Olive Oil Potato Chips, noting they passed a UC Davis test for real olive oil and no seed oils. Next, she shows Trader Joe's Corn Tortillas, highlighting the three-ingredient list (white corn, water, lime). She then features Lundberg Family Farms Lightly Salted Brown Rice Cakes, calling the brand top-notch. She presents Trader Joe's Apple Chip Duo made with red and green apples, followed by Trader Joe's Organic Sour Cream, which she calls a must-buy organic dairy product. She also shows Trader Joe's Organic Balsamic Vinegar of Modena as a clean ingredient option, and Trader Joe's Apple + Banana Fruit Bars and Apple + Coconut Fruit Bars as simple two-ingredient snacks. The video ends outside the store in the parking lot with a call to follow for more. The tone is informative and promotional, focused on 'nontoxic living' and clean ingredient swaps.

18089846285410528.summary: The video is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating how to make 'Din Tai Fung sesame noodles at home.' It opens with a finished bowl of creamy noodles topped with chopped green onions and chili flakes. The creator then prepares the sauce in a metal bowl, adding ingredients one by one with on-screen text: 2 tablespoons peanut butter, 2 tablespoons sesame paste, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon chili onion crunch, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, 1 grated garlic clove, and 1 teaspoon salt, which are mixed together. Next, dry noodles are boiled in a white pot with a pink handle. One cup of the starchy pasta water is added to the sauce to thin it, then the sauce is poured over the cooked noodles in the pot and tossed to coat. The noodles are plated into a white bowl, garnished with more chili onion crunch and fresh green onions, and shown being lifted with a fork. The entire process is set to upbeat background music with no spoken dialogue.

18085177103216439.summary: A young woman introduces herself as an 18-year-old private chef in Phoenix, Arizona, and presents a 'day in my life' meal-prep session. She displays numerous pre-portioned containers of food already prepared, then begins cooking from scratch. She makes Banana Chocolate Chip Protein Muffins, mixing batter in a blue bowl, portioning into a muffin tin, baking, testing with a toothpick, and tasting one while calling it fluffy. Next she prepares Chocolate Chip Banana Bread Protein Balls, combining oats, peanut butter, and other ingredients by hand. She chops yellow squash, zucchini, and carrots for Roasted Veggies, seasons them, and places them on sheet pans. She also makes Coconut Lime Cilantro Rice. For the main proteins, she prepares Honey Dijon Crusted Salmon, coating fillets with a honey-dijon mixture and a herb-breadcrumb topping before baking. She cooks seasoned chicken breasts in a cast-iron skillet for about six minutes per side, explaining the technique, then makes a spicy garlic-butter sauce in the same pan. She also breads chicken cutlets and finishes a creamy tomato-based dish with heavy cream. Throughout, she speaks directly to the camera in an upbeat, instructional tone. At the end she washes dishes at the sink, noting she does all the cleanup herself, and shows the refrigerator stocked with labeled meal-prep containers.

18578880574066119.summary: A close-up cooking video shows hands preparing a baked donut recipe on a wooden surface. A roasted sweet potato is peeled into a clear glass bowl, followed by a peeled banana, two cracked eggs, a generous amount of cocoa powder, and white baking powder. The ingredients are mashed together with a fork until a thick brown batter forms. The batter is spooned into a bright pink silicone donut mold with six cavities, then after baking, a dark brown cooked donut is removed and held up. The donut is dipped in melted chocolate glaze, placed on the wood, and sliced in half with a knife to reveal a moist, dense interior. Throughout, a male voice in Spanish narrates the steps: adding roasted sweet potato, banana, two eggs, pure cocoa powder, yeast/baking powder, mashing, distributing in molds, baking, unmolding, and covering with chocolate to get healthy, gluten-free donuts. The tone is instructional and clean, with no dialogue beyond the recipe narration.

17927635257388060.summary: The video opens with a top-down view of a pan of dark chocolate brownies on parchment paper, with on-screen text reading "POV: getting your kids to eat enough fiber doesn't have to be a fight." Hands enter the frame and slice the brownies into squares with a large knife, then lift one square to show its dense texture. Text identifies it as "Black bean brownies ~4g fiber." The scene shifts to a glass jar of deep-red chia berry jam; a spoon scoops it and spreads it thickly on toasted bread, labeled "Chia berry jam ~4g fiber." Next, a pot on a stovetop shows tomato sauce with white cannellini beans; an immersion blender blends them into the sauce, followed by a plated bowl of spaghetti coated in the blended sauce, captioned "White beans into pasta ~6g fiber." Then a small white ramekin holds a smooth chocolate pudding; a spoon stirs it, identified as "Avocado chocolate pudding ~7g fiber." Finally, a tray of golden-brown blueberry muffins in a silicone mold is shown on a cooling rack in a bright kitchen, labeled "Blueberry muffins (fresh milled flour) ~3g fiber." Throughout, the visuals are clean, home-cooking focused, with no narration, only a light humming soundtrack. The caption explains the creator is a mom prioritizing whole, nutrient-dense foods and provides full ingredient lists for each recipe, encouraging viewers to save and try them.

18109347932119939.summary: In this 2026 social media cooking video, creator Monica (@therealmonicasingh), described as 'Every Zillennial's internet mom,' demonstrates her 'easy peasy' Masala Peas recipe. Opening with the finished dish served alongside roti and two curries, she explains she makes it for her daughter to add more fiber to 'girl dinners.' The tutorial proceeds step-by-step: heating two tablespoons of ghee in a pan, tempering with two dried red chilies, half teaspoon cumin seeds, a pinch of hing, and turmeric, then adding one pound of frozen petite green peas. After stirring, she seasons with salt, smoked paprika, and coriander powder, cooks, then adds mango powder, roasted cumin powder, and water, simmers covered, and finishes. The video is calm, instructional, and family-oriented, with on-screen text guiding the recipe. No jokes, innuendo, or safety risks are present; the content is suitable for all ages.

17976412557074040.summary: This is a cooking tutorial titled 'Welcome Back to Another Episode of Realistic Dinners.' A woman demonstrates how to make 'One Pot Creamy Coconut Curry Chicken in 30 Minutes.' She starts by showing raw chicken thighs (noting breast can be substituted) and seasons them with paprika, garlic powder, turmeric, curry powder, salt, black pepper, and olive oil, then massages the spices in. She pan-fries the chicken for 7 minutes per side until browned, removes it, and sets aside. In the same pan, she sautés diced onion and garlic for 2-3 minutes, then adds coconut milk and a Japanese curry cube, mixing and simmering for 2 minutes to create a thick sauce. She places a molded dome of hot white rice into the center of the sauce, arranges sliced cooked chicken around it, and garnishes with chopped green onions and black sesame seeds. The video ends with her tasting the dish with chopsticks and a spoon, reacting with enjoyment.

18138115342607569.summary: This is a step-by-step cooking tutorial for making a dense, crusty seed bread. A person's hands are shown soaking steel-cut oats in water for about six hours, then draining them. The soaked oats are transferred to a glass bowl and mixed with sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, flax seeds, quinoa or oat flakes, and psyllium husk. Separately, apple cider vinegar is added to water, whisked, and poured into the dry mixture, which is stirred and left to sit. The thick mixture is then pressed firmly into a white loaf pan and baked. The finished loaf is removed, shown to hold together well, placed on a wooden board, and sliced easily without crumbling. The presenter, a woman in a blue top, holds up a slice and eats it while on-screen text claims the bread does not spike blood glucose and can help lower 'bad' cholesterol. The tone is calm, instructional, and focused on healthy eating.

18158261830458221.summary: A woman in a modern Los Angeles kitchen demonstrates how to make "Rice Paper Dumpling Rolls," presented as a healthier twist on her mother's famous recipe. She chops red cabbage, scallions, carrots, ginger, and garlic, then mixes them with ground chicken, diced shrimp, cilantro, egg, soy sauce, and sesame oil. She softens rice paper sheets in water, fills and rolls them, then pan-fries until golden brown and crispy. The finished rolls are plated, garnished with cilantro, and drizzled with a fish-sauce-based dipping sauce. She tastes one with chopsticks while a golden retriever watches, and later a man also tries the dish. Throughout she speaks directly to camera, noting the recipe is quick and healthy, and promotes her debut cookbook, "Maxi's Kitchen." The video has an upbeat, instructional, family-friendly tone.

18104745721837219.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial posted in June 2026 by creator Anastasiia Veriasova (@anadovada), a mom based in Texas. The video demonstrates her "mom hack" for getting kids to eat vegetables: zucchini waffles designed for meal prep. Opening shots show a finished golden-brown waffle with the text "Prep once, enjoy all week," followed by a stack of waffles on a dark plate. The creator grates fresh zucchini on a box grater, places it in a metal bowl, adds salt, then squeezes out excess liquid over a sink while wearing blue gloves. She cracks an egg into the bowl, adds sour cream, shredded cheese, chopped parsley, melted butter, and flour, mixing everything into a thick batter. She spoons the batter into a white Disney Mickey & Minnie Mouse four-section waffle maker, closes it, and reveals four cooked mini waffles with visible green zucchini flecks. The video ends with close-ups of the stacked waffles. The caption frames it as a zero-drama way to serve veggies for breakfast, snacks, or lunchboxes, noting adults will want to steal them too. The overall tone is wholesome, practical, and family-oriented, set to soft instrumental piano music.

18141731656502877.summary: A young woman identified as @ricesprinkles presents the fifth and final installment of her rice cooker chicken prep series, making ginger scallion chicken rice. She holds up a bowl of the finished dish—rice mixed with chunks of chicken and chopped green onion—and tastes it, calling it her favorite and simplest meal, requiring only five ingredients (six with oil, seven with salt, eight with salt). The video demonstrates the process: uncooked rice and broth are placed in a rice cooker pot, followed by pre-marinated chicken pieces from a bag, then cooked. While it cooks, she finely minces ginger and chops scallions, heats oil in a stainless steel pan, adds the aromatics to infuse the oil, seasons with salt, and then mixes the hot ginger-scallion oil into the cooked chicken rice. The tone is casual, instructional, and enthusiastic, with on-screen captions guiding steps. The creator's profile notes she is a Chinese girl 'trying to grow a butt and poop well,' and the post directs viewers to her website or to comment for the recipe.

17938965303303624.summary: A woman with long dark hair demonstrates how to make a comforting chicken rice soup in a home kitchen. The video opens with her holding a bowl of the finished dish, topped with shredded chicken, chopped green onions, and crispy fried shallots, while on-screen text reads 'it's so good I want to cry.' She takes bites and reacts with satisfaction. The preparation sequence shows raw chicken leg quarters being seasoned with salt and pepper, sliced ginger being pan-fried in oil, then the chicken seared until golden brown. The seared chicken is transferred to a white pot decorated with Snoopy characters, water is added, and it is boiled. After cooking, the chicken is removed, shredded by hand (with text 'hottt'), and returned to the broth along with cooked white rice and a large amount of finely chopped green onions. The mixture is stirred into a soupy congee. The final dish is plated in a decorative bowl and garnished with more fried shallots before she eats it again, giving a thumbs-up over the empty bowl. The overall tone is cozy, satisfying, and focused on simple home cooking.

18007069133944296.summary: A woman in Miami demonstrates how to make make-ahead egg muffins for a quick weekly breakfast. The video opens with her pouring oil into a 12-cup muffin tin and brushing it, then cracking one whole egg into each cup. She adds toppings to customize each muffin: diced red tomatoes, diced orange bell peppers, diced cooked chicken/turkey, crumbled organic blue cheese, shredded goat cheese, dollops of green pesto, sun-dried tomatoes, and Everything Bagel seasoning. She stirs each cup with chopsticks to combine, then bakes the tray until puffed and golden brown (she states 15-20 minutes at 300°F). After baking, she removes a muffin, plates two with roasted asparagus, breaks one open to show the interior with melted cheese and vegetables, and takes a bite while smiling at the camera. The Spanish audio explains this is a super easy, delicious solution for busy mornings that stays good in the fridge for up to three months, so you don't worry about breakfast. The tone is upbeat, instructional, and promotional for healthy meal prep.

18000168428791446.summary: The video opens with a close-up of plated food: seasoned chicken thighs on white rice, being drizzled with a pale green creamy sauce from a spoon, with yellow on-screen text reading 'Wtf is I don't like chicken.' The scene then rewinds to show preparation. Dried red chilies are placed in a metal blender jar, followed by peeled garlic cloves, toasted coriander, cumin and caraway seeds, smoked paprika, black pepper, salt, olive oil, lemon juice and zest. These are blended into a thick red harissa paste. Raw boneless chicken thighs in a bowl are coated with the marinade, then arranged on parchment paper in an air fryer basket. The cooked chicken, now caramelized and speckled with red chili flakes, is plated over a mound of white rice and finished with the green sauce drizzle. The caption provides the full ingredient list and method for the homemade harissa-style marinade, noting a 190°C air-fry for 12-15 minutes. The setting is a bright indoor kitchen with a marble countertop. The tone is instructional and appetizing, focused on comfort food and easy protein cooking. Two viewer comments praise how yummy and fiery it looks. No people are clearly shown beyond a hand, and no safety risks are present.

18101938040188902.summary: The video opens with a close-up of a mint-green mini waffle maker being opened to reveal a cooked savory waffle, with on-screen text reading 'C what I created today.' The creator then places a round patty of vegetable and millet dough into the waffle iron, presses it down, and closes the lid; text states 'Healthy & Tasty Waffles for lunch.' The cooked waffle is shown, golden-brown with visible green beans and orange carrot pieces. The scene shifts to the creator, a woman with long dark hair in a colorful printed shirt, leaning over a marble kitchen counter with ingredients laid out: measuring cups of ragi/finger millet flour and rajgira/amaranth flour, chopped carrots, beans, coriander, ginger, chili, spices, and curd. She mixes the flours, adds aamchur powder, chaat masala, chili powder, turmeric, and salt, then incorporates the chopped vegetables and 1/4 cup dahi/curd to form a thick mixture. She shapes it into a patty, greases the waffle maker with ghee, cooks the patty, and removes the finished waffle. Separately, she prepares a dip by mixing green chutney into a bowl of dahi/yogurt until smooth and pale green. She plates the waffles on a banana leaf in a decorative bowl, adds the dip in a small heart-shaped dish, and finally tastes a piece dipped in the chutney-yogurt, showing enjoyment. The tone is instructional, warm, and focused on a nutritious Indian-inspired alternative to rotis.

18083827760676288.summary: A woman in a striped shirt presents a recipe for a vegetable-heavy rice dish she makes when she wants lots of veggies that still taste delicious. She shows fresh leafy greens—specifically tong hao (chrysanthemum greens), noting she also uses spinach and bok choy—and explains the process: blanching the greens for 1-2 minutes, squeezing out excess water, and chopping them finely. She seasons the chopped greens with sesame oil and roasted sesame seeds. For added fiber, she chops shiitake mushrooms and sautés them for 2-3 minutes with soy sauce and black pepper until softened. She then combines hot cooked rice with a generous amount of furikake seasoning, adds both the seasoned greens and the sautéed mushrooms, and mixes everything thoroughly. The video ends with close-ups of the finished mixed rice, emphasizing its texture and ingredients.

18121650910801179.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating a recipe for sweet potato meatballs. It opens with a baked sweet potato being split open and mashed with forks. The mashed sweet potato is then added to a bowl of raw ground meat, followed by salt, pepper, and dried herbs. The mixture is combined thoroughly with a fork, then portioned into uniform balls using a metal scoop and placed on a parchment-lined baking sheet. The meatballs are shown baking in an oven until browned, then tossed in a glossy dark sauce. The final dish is plated over white rice with steamed broccoli, garnished with chopped green onions and sesame seeds, and eaten with a fork. On-screen text frames the recipe as a superior alternative to traditional meatballs made with breadcrumbs or eggs.

18094876385062362.summary: This is a short-form social media cooking video posted by @scrambled_eats in August 2026, promoting a family-friendly savory muffin recipe. The visual sequence opens with a plate piled high with golden-brown muffins, as small children's hands reach in and pick one up, then break it open to show a soft interior. On-screen text reads 'The savoury muffins I make when I need my kids to eat some veggies.' Subsequent shots show the batter being mixed in a metal bowl with Greek yoghurt, eggs, and melted butter, followed by chopped vegetables (zucchini, mushrooms, red capsicum) being folded in. Another text overlay lists the ingredients: 'Made with Greek yoghurt, zucchini, mushrooms, capsicum + cheese.' The final shots show the baked muffins in trays and being pulled apart to reveal a fluffy texture, with text stating 'Light and fluffy... they taste just like a pizza.' The accompanying caption provides the full recipe and markets the muffins as healthy, high-protein, freezer-friendly snacks suitable for kids and parents. The overall tone is warm, practical, and wholesome, aimed at parents seeking easy ways to incorporate vegetables into children's diets.

17911188891444125.summary: The video opens with on-screen text asking 'Still making plain banana pancakes? Try this instead.' and introduces Day 2 of the Avocado Challenge. The creator, in a home kitchen, shows a whole avocado and then cuts it open on a wooden board. The scene shifts to a divided toddler plate already displaying the finished golden-brown mini pancakes alongside white yogurt and bright pink cubed dragon fruit. The tutorial begins with a stainless steel mixing bowl where a peeled banana is placed, followed by scooped avocado chunks. Using a fork, she mashes both together until combined. She then adds spoonfuls of ragi powder and whole wheat flour, a pinch of salt, and a sprinkle of cinnamon powder. Water is poured in and the mixture is whisked into a smooth, pourable pale-green batter. Moving to a stovetop, she heats a light-colored non-stick pan with ghee and uses a ladle to drop small portions of batter, forming tiny delicate pancakes. She flips them, covers the pan with a lid, and cooks both sides until browned. The finished pancakes are plated on the toddler tray with the yogurt and dragon fruit. A final shot shows the empty plate with only crumbs and pink stains, indicating the toddler devoured the meal. The creator narrates throughout in an upbeat, instructional tone, emphasizing it is a new dish for her toddler and expressing excitement for the series.

17950522716216498.summary: The video is Episode 7 of 'Undercover Iron,' a series focused on delicious recipes designed to help address common nutrient deficiencies, particularly iron deficiency in women. It opens with text over a wooden board showing orange slices, then shows a hand placing a bowl of finished chocolate squares topped with orange zest. The preparation process is shown from above: ingredients including dates, tahini, orange zest, and pumpkin seeds are blended into a dark paste, then pressed into a blue silicone ice-cube tray. Melted dark chocolate is poured over the mixture and spread, followed by sprinkling more orange zest on top. The final product—small chocolate-coated bites—is displayed in a brown ceramic bowl next to orange wedges. A blonde woman wearing glasses and a black sleeveless top holds up the bowl, smiles at the camera, and presents the treat. The narration explains that dark chocolate provides iron and magnesium, and combined with pumpkin seeds, dates, and orange, creates a small, tasty bite packed with nutritional value.

17927626422388328.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make 'crispy rice paper SHRIMP BITES,' as labeled by on-screen text. The video opens with the finished dish—golden-brown, round bites piled on a dark gray plate, garnished with chopped green onion and served with a creamy pink dipping sauce. The process then rewinds to show preparation: minced raw shrimp in a bowl is seasoned with white powder (likely starch), a dark liquid sauce, chopped green onions, and ground pepper, then mixed with chopsticks. A sheet of translucent rice paper is laid on a cutting board, filled with the shrimp mixture, rolled tightly, and cut into small cylindrical pieces with scissors. The pieces are arranged on parchment paper, sprayed with oil, and placed in an air fryer/oven where they cook until puffed and crispy. The final shots return to the plated bites, some skewered on wooden sticks, being dipped into the sauce. The video has bright, clean visuals, natural lighting, and upbeat instrumental background music with no spoken narration.

17894673390578752.summary: A woman in a kitchen demonstrates how to make a chocolate protein cake using non-traditional ingredients. She starts by pouring soaked red lentils into a blender, then adds mashed bananas, explaining they are 'not the enemy' and together create a gentler blood glucose response. After blending, she transfers the smooth orange batter to a bowl, prepares a flax egg with water and ground flaxseed, and adds it along with unsweetened dark cocoa powder, mixing until well combined into a smooth chocolatey batter. She then incorporates baking soda, baking powder, and an acid, pours the batter into a gray fluted bundt pan, and bakes it. The finished cake is inverted onto a wooden board, sliced, and shown to have a fluffy, moist crumb. She holds up a slice and eats it with chocolate sauce, stating it has 17 grams of fiber and 14 grams of protein for 250 calories per serving, and calls it 'incredible.' The video is presented as a healthy, high-protein dessert recipe.

18104294197990936.summary: A creator (@everyday.resets) posts a 'Day 4 of making my home 1% better' cleaning video focused on deep cleaning wooden spoons. Wearing bright pink then purple gloves, she scrubs a perforated wooden spatula, soaks multiple spoons and spatulas in a white dish, adds a white powder (likely baking soda) which fizzes with water, scrubs again, rinses under running water, and dries them on a cloth over a pomegranate-patterned surface. She sands one piece with 220-grit sandpaper, then conditions all the wood with Howard Butcher Block Conditioner, rubbing the oil in until the grain darkens and shines. The video is shot in close-up, satisfying ASMR style. The audio is a mellow lo-fi track with a female vocalist singing reflective lyrics about self-forgiveness, healing from past scars, and seeking love. The overall tone is calm, methodical, and motivational for home care.

18030852371650212.summary: Creator Nevaeh Victoria (@the.cycle.kitchen) presents episode 21 of her meal prep series, focused on the week after your period (the follicular phase). In a bright kitchen, she prepares four dishes over two hours: Peaches & Cream Overnight Oats topped with caramelized peaches, an Olive Dense Bean Salad with chickpeas, white beans, olives, radishes and herbs, Anti-Inflammatory Ginger Lime Salmon Bowls with spinach, cucumber-avocado-edamame salad, and Chocolate-Covered Raspberry Yogurt Stuffed Dates. She explains that nutrition during the follicular phase can affect menstrual intensity, mentions her own adenomyosis, and frames the meals as fiber- and protein-packed, anti-inflammatory support. The video ends with her tasting the dishes and inviting viewers to comment 'PREP' for recipes via DM. Tone is enthusiastic, instructional, and wellness-oriented, centered on women's hormonal health.

18112132570757654.summary: In a bright modern kitchen, creator GQ Jordan presents a viral recipe reaction video as part of her 'Second Servings' series. She begins holding two large glass jars of rolled oats and red lentils, introducing the idea of turning them into something incredible. She scoops red lentils into a bowl, rinses them, and adds them to a Vitamix blender along with oats, banana, milk, dates, baking powder, apple cider vinegar, cinnamon, and vanilla. On-screen text highlights the nutritional claims: 28 grams of fiber and 30 grams of protein per serving, made with seven whole foods, providing slow-digesting carbs for blood sugar stability. She pours the blended batter into glass containers, tops them with banana slices, blueberries, strawberries, and chocolate chips, and bakes them. After baking, she tastes the resulting dense pancake slab and delivers her nutritionist analysis: oats provide slow-release carbs and beta-glucan fiber for gut health, lentils add plant protein, iron, and extra fiber, together slowing digestion for steady energy and satiety. She notes the recipe is balanced, easy, accessible, and tasty but a little dense, recommending an optional egg for lightness (not vegan) and adding fat like peanut butter or Greek yogurt for a complete meal. She concludes positively, calling it a great way to add more plants to the diet, and says goodbye with 'Sláinte.'

18120614917738660.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted May 31, 2026 by creator @mydarr (Lalada) in Tampa, FL, demonstrating "Caramelized Banana Peanut Butter Toast." The video opens with a top-down view of two peeled bananas on a wooden board, with text overlay reading "No matter how hard life gets! Eat this toast first Everything will be okay." A knife slices each banana lengthwise without cutting through, creating accordion-like strips. The sliced bananas are placed on parchment paper and put into an oven/air fryer to caramelize. Meanwhile, a slice of toasted sourdough is shown, then generously spread with natural peanut butter. The warm, caramelized banana halves are laid on top of the peanut butter. Dark chocolate is grated over the bananas using a microplane, followed by a sprinkle of flaky sea salt. The finished toast is cut in half diagonally. The tone is calm, soothing, and instructional, presenting a simple breakfast/dessert recipe with ASMR-style sound effects of chopping and grating. No dialogue is spoken; the focus is entirely on the food preparation process.

18020618837896331.summary: The video opens with a close-up of a golden-brown round waffle held over a black plate, with on-screen text reading 'Quinoa & Paneer Waffles.' The creator, a woman with dark hair wearing a floral sleeveless dress, introduces the recipe as the only way she can get her husband to eat quinoa. She shows dry quinoa grains being poured into a metal pot, washed with water by hand, then boiled on a stove until cooked. The cooked quinoa is transferred to a blue-and-white marbled bowl. She adds mashed boiled potato, grated paneer, chopped fresh coriander, red spice powder, chopped onions, and rice flour for binding, mixing everything with a fork. She forms the mixture into a patty with her hands. Next, she greases a small light-blue electric waffle maker with a green silicone brush, places the patty inside, closes the lid, and cooks until crispy. She removes the finished waffle with tongs, shows its grid texture, and serves it. She suggests serving with green chutney or ketchup, and advises cooling on a wire rack before packing in a kids' tiffin. She tastes the waffle, smiles, and waves goodbye. The setting is a home kitchen with warm lighting, and the tone is friendly and instructional.

17979065124071638.summary: The video opens with a close-up of a finished dark chocolate almond brownie on a white plate with a blue rim, sliced and topped with chopped walnuts and melted dark chocolate chunks. On-screen text introduces it as an 'Almond brownie' that is 'No sugar | No eggs | Gluten free' and 'Less ingredients, easy to make.' A hand lifts a slice to show its dense, fudgy texture. The scene shifts to a kitchen where the preparation begins: dates are placed in a white bowl and milk is poured over them, with text noting 'Dates soaked in milk For 30 minutes.' Next, in a black square baking pan, dry ingredients are added sequentially — almond flour from a visible Kirkland Signature bag, followed by cocoa powder, baking soda, and ghee — while on-screen text lists 'Almond flour, Cocoa powder, Baking soda, Blended dates, Ghee.' The soaked dates are then blended into a thick paste and poured into the pan, followed by melted ghee. A spoon mixes everything into a thick brown batter. The batter is transferred to a round pan lined with parchment paper and spread evenly. Chopped walnuts and chopped dark chocolate are sprinkled on top as garnish. Text instructs to 'Bake for 350F for about 40-45 minutes.' The baked brownie is shown risen and set, then transferred to a plate, sliced outdoors in sunlight, and finally presented to two young boys who give thumbs-up approvals, indicating the recipe is kid-friendly.

17972031540081130.summary: This is a cooking tutorial by creator Binal Patel (@binalstastytales) demonstrating how to make 'High Protein Muthiya,' a Gujarati savory snack adapted for high protein and low calories. The video opens with the finished dish—golden, sesame-topped muthiya pieces on a white plate, labeled '25g Protein | 375 Cal per serving.' The creator then shows the preparation: blending Greek yogurt, low-fat paneer, green chilies, ginger, garlic, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, cumin-coriander powder, and dry fenugreek leaves into a paste. This paste is mixed in a bowl with chopped spinach, grated bottle gourd, carom seeds, sorghum (jowar) flour, and chickpea (besan) flour with water to form a soft yellow-green dough. The dough is shaped into small logs, placed in a steamer, and cooked for 15 minutes. After cooling, the steamed logs are sliced into bite-size pieces and stored in a container marked 'Good till 1 Week.' For serving, the pieces are tossed in a hot pan with oil, sesame seeds, and curry leaves, then seasoned with turmeric and red chili powder. On-screen text and the caption emphasize the nutritional profile, meal-prep convenience, and ask viewers to comment 'MUTHIYA' for the full recipe. The tone is instructional, wholesome, and health-focused, aimed at the Indian diaspora seeking vegetarian protein-rich meals.

18117837160853597.summary: A creator demonstrates assembling a healthy vegetarian meal-prep lunch that she describes as repeatable and never boring. The video opens on a rustic wooden tabletop with text overlay reading 'a lunch you can make on repeat and never get sick of >>'. An empty rectangular glass container is placed down, then filled in sections: first a scoop of cooked quinoa mixed with rice and bright green edamame beans, then a portion of seasoned crumbled tofu in the middle compartment, followed by sliced garlicky zucchini added to the third section. A hand sprinkles white sesame seeds over the zucchini and adds chopped green onions. The final shot shows two identical completed containers side-by-side, neatly portioned with the three components, before a pair of hands with pink nail polish and a ring seals one with a red silicone lid. The accompanying caption notes the recipe includes maple garlic sauce, crumbled tofu, quinoa rice with edamame, garlicky zucchini, green onions, and sesame seeds, and promotes the full recipe on her Substack, tagged with #healthyrecipes #mealprep #vegetarian #cleaneating #wholefood. The tone is calm, instructional, and wholesome, aimed at easy weekly lunch planning.

18092790065528444.summary: This is Episode 8 of a recipe series titled 'High Protein & Low Calorie Soya Afghani.' The video, posted by @prasannaspalate_, is a step-by-step cooking demonstration. It opens with the finished dish—a creamy green curry with soya chunks topped with cream and cilantro—shown in a pan and then plated with roti, with on-screen text noting ~35g protein and ~430 kcal. The creator narrates while preparing the dish: she soaks dry soya chunks in hot water, squeezes out excess water, then sautés garlic, ginger, sliced onion, and green chilies in oil. She blends low-fat paneer with cashews, coriander, and the sautéed aromatics into a smooth green paste. The drained soya is mixed with curd, the green paste, and spices (salt, pepper, chole masala, garam masala), then cooked in the pan with a little water. After a few minutes, she adds fresh cream, kasuri methi, and chopped coriander, stirring until creamy. The final shots show the rich green curry being served and eaten with roti. The tone is instructional, positive, and focused on healthy eating, emphasizing the dish as a delicious, high-protein alternative to traditional preparations.

17981034990019514.summary: This is a fast-paced, visually appealing cooking montage set to upbeat South Asian music. The creator, identified as Ayesha Aslam (@etta_esthetic_ps), frames the video as a POV of being the 'Ghar ki CHOTI Beti and personal chef of the family,' highlighting the humorous burden of cooking for everyone. The sequence showcases multiple homemade dishes: a large tray of chicken pulao/biryani with herbs, hands pulling apart tender chicken; grilled chicken patties covered in a creamy white sauce; a plated sweet-and-sour style chicken with sesame seeds served over rice; creamy penne pasta topped with seasoned chicken thighs; golden fried croquettes broken open to show a cheesy interior; a plated chicken steak with mashed potatoes and julienned vegetables smothered in gravy; another colorful biryani; and finally, butter chicken curry with naan bread being torn and dipped. The tone is warm, proud, and relatable, celebrating home cooking skills with satisfying close-ups of textures and sauces.

18120799099846462.summary: The video opens with a plated finish: a white scalloped plate holding a vibrant orange-red cottage cheese bhurji topped with chopped cilantro, served alongside two slices of toasted whole-grain bread, with on-screen text reading "COTTAGE CHEESE BHURJI RECIPE". The scene shifts to a modern kitchen with gray tile backsplash and a gas stove, where a person's hand prepares the dish step-by-step. Oil is poured into a stainless steel pan, followed by cumin seeds and a spoonful of ginger-garlic paste. Finely diced red onion and green serrano pepper are added and sautéed. The cook then adds a series of spices from a metal masala box — red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and finally pav bhaji masala described as a secret ingredient — stirring them into the vegetables. A large spoonful of white cottage cheese is added to the pan and mixed thoroughly until it absorbs the spices and begins to melt slightly, becoming a cohesive scramble. The pan is removed from heat, fresh cilantro is sprinkled on top, and the creator demonstrates eating it by scooping the bhurji onto a piece of toast. Throughout, the creator speaks directly to the camera in a friendly, instructional tone, emphasizing the recipe's simplicity, 15-minute timing, and flavor. The overall tone is enthusiastic, wholesome, and focused on everyday vegetarian breakfast cooking.

18092735312071669.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make 'Cheesy spinach bites.' The video opens with a close-up of finished golden-brown pastry bites topped with black and white sesame seeds, which are pulled apart to show a melted cheese and green spinach filling; on-screen text notes '10.5g of protein per serve.' The preparation sequence follows: cooked spinach is placed in a glass bowl, then cottage cheese, low-fat mozzarella, salt and pepper, and onion and garlic powder are added and mixed. An egg is cracked into the mixture and stirred in. A sheet of puff pastry is laid out, the spinach-cheese filling is spooned along one edge, and the pastry is rolled and cut into individual portions. The pieces are brushed with egg wash, sprinkled with sesame seeds, and baked in an oven until puffed and golden. The final shots show the baked bites on a baking tray and plated on a white dish with green trim, with text directing viewers to 'Full recipe in the KICApp.' The video has bright lighting, upbeat background music, and focuses entirely on the food and hands preparing it.

17870721339630465.summary: The video opens with a close-up of a beige bowl holding three small green-brown patties resting on white yogurt, held over a woven mat in a home kitchen. On-screen text introduces them as 'Melt-in-the-Mouth Protein Patties 10 months+'. A hand uses a spoon to lift a patty, showing its soft texture. The recipe process follows: soya chunks are poured into a metal blender jar, followed by chopped onion, coriander leaves, cubes of paneer, and garlic, each labeled with nutritional benefits like high protein, antioxidants, and immunity support. The mixture is blended smooth, transferred to a blue bowl, and seasoned with salt, black pepper, cumin powder, gram flour, and lemon juice. The hand mixes the dough and shapes small patties. Desi ghee is heated in a small pan on a gas stove, and the patties are shallow-fried for 2-3 minutes until golden. Finally, a cooked patty is placed onto yogurt, with text noting calcium and probiotics, and a closing message encourages mothers to try it for their babies, mentioning 'My Ali loved it!' and asking to save and share. The tone is warm, nurturing, and instructional, aimed at parents seeking healthy baby meals.

18052428560575206.summary: The video opens with a close-up of the finished dish: tender chunks of chicken in a thick, golden-yellow creamy sauce speckled with red chili flakes and fresh chopped cilantro, simmering in a gray non-stick pan. On-screen text reads 'creamy afghani chicken.' The scene cuts to a plate where a hand tears a piece of flaky layered flatbread and dips it into the saucy chicken. The tutorial then rewinds to the beginning: raw cubed chicken thighs in a glass bowl are topped with a generous pour of white yogurt, followed by chopped fresh cilantro, grated ginger-garlic, a mix of brown and yellow spices, and lemon juice, then mixed by hand. The marinated chicken is added to a hot pan with melted butter and cooked until the marinade reduces. After removing the chicken, the same pan is used to sauté finely chopped onion and garlic in oil until golden brown, then flour is stirred in, followed by a stream of milk to create a bubbling white sauce. Seasonings including black pepper and chili flakes are added, then shredded mozzarella cheese melts into the sauce. The cooked chicken is returned to the pan, stirred into the creamy gravy, and simmered until coated. Finally, fresh cilantro is sprinkled over the top as garnish, and the hand returns to dip bread into the finished curry directly from the pan. The entire process is presented in bright, close-up food videography with no spoken narration.

18115598980935567.summary: A woman with long dark hair prepares and eats a comforting bowl of scallion chicken soup rice in her kitchen. The video opens with her tasting the finished dish, with on-screen text saying "it's so good I want to cry." She explains this is what she makes after a long day when she wants something warm and comforting, noting she loves eating rice with soup. She recounts that as a child her father never let her eat pao fan (rice soaked in soup) because she would swallow it whole without chewing, but now as an adult she has "free will." The cooking process is shown step-by-step: she places two raw chicken leg quarters on a tray, finely chops a large amount of green onions and shallots, seasons the chicken with salt, sears it skin-side down in a pan with ginger slices until golden brown, then transfers the chicken to a white pot, pours in hot water, and simmers covered for 15 minutes. After cooking, she removes the chicken, which has a beautiful golden color, shreds the meat by hand while noting it's hot, and returns the shredded chicken to the broth. She adds cooked white rice and "lots and lots of spring onions," stirs everything together, and serves it in a decorative bowl topped with crispy fried shallots.
