The final shots show the steaming, green-flecked soup rice, which she describes as a "super cozy bowl of scallion chicken soup rice" that is "so good."

18110592898945033.summary: A woman in a home kitchen introduces her homemade 'beauty boba' made from peach gum. She holds up the dried amber-colored resin, explains it is peach gum, and shows it in her palm. She pours water over the pieces in a glass bowl with on-screen text instructing to 'Soak for 24 hours.' After soaking, she displays the enlarged, translucent, gelatinous pieces, noting they grow 3-5x, and carefully picks out residual bark. She transfers the cleaned gum to a white pot, adds water, and simmers it with a red date, describing the texture as chewy, lightly bouncy, and flavor-neutral. She then layers the cooked peach gum into a glass jar with a milky base, tops it with diced fresh mango and a dollop of white cream or yogurt, and drizzles more liquid over it. On-screen text reads 'Eat your skincare = eat whole foods God created.' She stirs and eats the dessert. Throughout, she encourages viewers to comment 'PEACH' for details on sourcing, preparation, and benefits. The tone is calm, instructional, and wellness-focused, with gentle piano music in the background. No speech is audible.

17930737866348815.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates how to make 'soy marinated eggs' as a quick meal or high-protein snack. She starts by boiling brown eggs for 6-7 minutes for a medium-boiled texture, then cools them in an ice bath before peeling. She prepares a marinade in a glass container with chopped green onions, garlic, sliced red chilies, sesame seeds, light and dark soy sauce, water, and sesame oil. The peeled eggs are placed in the marinade, covered with a paper towel to keep them submerged, sealed, and refrigerated for at least 8 hours or overnight. After marinating, she shows the finished glossy eggs served over rice. She then emphasizes not wasting the leftover marinade, pouring it into a pot, bringing it to a boil to kill germs, adding blocks of tofu and more green onions, and simmering briefly. The cooked tofu is also served over rice. The tone is instructional and casual, with on-screen text guiding each step.

18088610420543874.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial video posted July 17, 2026 by nutritionist Solaine Douglas (@solainedouglas_nutrition). Set to upbeat instrumental music, the video demonstrates a "High Protein Dill Pickle Egg Smash" sandwich claimed to be a 5-minute lunch with 25g protein. On a wooden checkered cutting board, hands peel two hard-boiled eggs, then display ingredients: half an avocado, two dill pickles, spring onion, fresh parsley, Dijon mustard, and East Coast by Barambah Organics cottage cheese. The ingredients are chopped together, mixed with mashed avocado and cottage cheese, seasoned, and piled onto seeded multigrain bread. The finished sandwich is cut in half, revealing a green, chunky filling. The creator, a woman with brown hair in a striped shirt, then eats the sandwich at her kitchen counter. On-screen text reinforces "25g PROTEIN EGG SANDWICH 5 minute lunch idea." The overall tone is clean, instructional, and health-focused, presenting a quick macro-friendly meal.

18417882574177440.summary: A woman in a grey sweater stands in a modern kitchen and demonstrates her favorite way to eat chicken. On-screen text reads 'My fave way to eat chicken:'. She lays out a round rice paper wrapper on a pink wavy cutting board, spoons a seasoned orange-colored chicken mixture onto it, and rolls it tightly into a log. She repeats this to make several rolls, then slices each roll into bite-sized pieces. The pieces are placed in an air fryer basket, cooked until golden brown and crispy, then transferred to a white scalloped serving plate. She garnishes the dish with fresh cilantro leaves and serves it with a small bowl of creamy orange dipping sauce. She picks up a piece, dips it in the sauce, and eats it with an appreciative expression. The video has no dialogue, only background music, and focuses entirely on the food preparation process.

17888832885604076.summary: This is a split-screen cooking tutorial video posted in July 2026. The top half shows actress Keke Palmer seated outdoors at a table, narrating a recipe while the bottom half demonstrates the steps. She instructs to boil eggs for seven minutes, transfer them to an ice bath for three minutes (joking 'like the cool kids are doing with the ice plunge'), then prepare a marinade in a container with soy sauce, tamarind, rice vinegar, sliced chili, ginger, and garlic. The peeled eggs are submerged overnight. The next morning, an egg is cracked open over rice and sliced in half to reveal a bright orange, runny 'jammy' yolk. Palmer delivers the punchline, 'that's a jammy egg for your ass.' The video concludes with a different scene of a man and woman in a kitchen tasting the finished marinated egg, saying 'cheers,' 'hmm,' and 'oh yeah that's really good.' The overall tone is casual, instructional, and humorous, blending celebrity commentary with a popular Asian-style soy-marinated egg recipe.

18099626390272588.summary: A woman wearing a green sari with red trim presents a cooking experiment she calls "Kerala's fish nirvana, but with prawns and rice paper noodles." Speaking directly to camera, she explains her approach is asking "what if," inspired by the rice paper noodle trend. The video shows her blending fresh cilantro, curry leaves, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, and spices into a green paste, then marinating raw prawns in it. She fries the marinated prawns in a pan, adds coconut milk to create a creamy yellow-green sauce, and simmers. Separately, she softens round rice paper sheets, cuts them into strips, and adds them to the sauce to soak up the flavor. The finished dish is plated in a white bowl and garnished with chopped scallions, roasted peanuts, and chili oil. She tastes it with chopsticks, reacting with wide-eyed surprise, saying "This was not supposed to taste this good. Oh my God," and concluding "Safe to say, this what if really worked." The tone is enthusiastic, personal, and focused on fusion cooking, posted July 8, 2026 by creator @jishageorges.

18015228347857859.summary: The video is a short-form cooking reel demonstrating how to make Saunf ka Sharbat (fennel seed drink). Shot from a top-down perspective on a dark marbled surface, a hand measures 1/4 cup of fennel seeds into a 1/3 cup measure, then pours them into a small metal grinder jar. Rock sugar crystals, green cardamom pods, black peppercorns, and black salt are added. After grinding, the resulting light green powder is spooned into a clear glass mug, mixed with cold water, and stirred until dissolved. The final drink is held up outdoors against a green lawn backdrop. On-screen text reads "Him : Coming home in 5 mins," suggesting the drink is being prepared quickly for someone arriving home. The creator's caption provides the ingredient list and instructions, noting the powder can be stored for a month, and tags the content as healthy, easy, and quick recipes. The audio features a male vocalist singing a gentle Hindi melody throughout. The overall tone is calm, domestic, and instructional.

18104437142328732.summary: A woman in a white t-shirt films herself in a modern home kitchen making her first meal after returning from two weeks in Europe. On-screen text and her narration identify the dish as Khatta Mug, a savory and sour Gujarati dal made with yogurt. She shows the process step-by-step: tempering mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, chilies, turmeric and chili powder in ghee, adding ginger and garlic, then pouring in a whisked yogurt-besan mixture. She then adds pre-cooked whole green moong dal from an Instant Pot, stirs it into the creamy yellow sauce, seasons it, and tastes it. The finished dal is served in a light blue bowl alongside roti and raw sliced red onion. She eats it by hand, dipping the bread into the dal and also eating onion slices, expressing that it is comforting and satisfying. The tone is warm, personal, and instructional, presented as a simple post-vacation comfort food recipe.

17991800523005660.summary: A woman identified as Caroline (@carolinescozycorner) films a cozy kitchen cooking tutorial for a "simple high-protein breakfast (toddler approved)". Speaking directly to camera in a red oversized sweatshirt, she explains she has eaten this protein Dutch baby almost daily since Christmas and shares the recipe adapted from another creator. She preheats her oven to 400 degrees with butter melting in a cast iron skillet, then weighs ingredients on a digital scale into a NutriBullet cup: six eggs, 226g cottage cheese (Daisy brand), 120g Kirkland organic flour, and vanilla extract. She blends the mixture, pours it into the hot buttered skillet, and bakes for 20-22 minutes. The finished dish is a puffy, golden custardy pancake shown on a wooden table next to daisies. She cuts a slice to show the texture. The tone is warm, maternal, and wholesome, emphasizing simplicity, nutrition, and family life in the Texas Hill Country, with no problematic content.

18109488643777207.summary: This is a cooking tutorial from the social media account @crowded_kitchen (mother-daughter duo Lexi Harrison & Beth Sinclair) for their 'Better Than Store Bought' series. The video demonstrates how to make homemade Milano cookies. It opens with finished cookies being filled with chocolate ganache, while the narrator jokes, 'Hopefully this recipe doesn't get us sued,' explaining that when Trader Joe's released a Milano copycat in 2015, Pepperidge Farms took them to court. The process shown includes mixing butter, sugar, flour and egg into a butter cookie dough, piping oblong shapes onto parchment, baking until golden, then making a whipped chocolate ganache filling by pouring hot cream over chopped chocolate and whisking. The cooled cookies are sandwiched together with the ganache. The tone is warm, approachable, and promotional, ending by encouraging viewers to try their homemade Oreos or Nutter Butters next. The video was posted July 12, 2026.

18104173586025519.summary: A top-down cooking video shows the preparation of a simple baked egg dish intended for toddlers and families. On a green-and-white checkered cloth, hands add chopped broccoli to a greased square metal pan, then layer in sweetcorn, shredded cheese, and beaten eggs with herbs, mix everything together, and sprinkle more cheese on top. After baking, the golden-brown slab is cut into finger-sized strips and placed on a wooden bear-shaped toddler plate alongside a dollop of white yogurt dip. Throughout, text overlays deliver a supportive message to mothers: 'This is your reminder... Perfect meals don't make perfect mums. But easy ones? They just might give you your patience (and peace) back.' The accompanying caption reinforces this, explaining the creator stopped shaming herself for shortcuts and developed a recipe app with 800+ BLW/toddler-friendly recipes, inviting viewers to comment 'App link' for access. The tone is calm, practical, and empathetic, aimed at overwhelmed mums seeking low-stress meal solutions.

18063937157738233.summary: A woman in a white tank top prepares a breakfast dish in a modern kitchen. The video opens with an overhead view of a stainless steel saucepan on a marble countertop, with the text 'like i said, i won't be going back' overlaid throughout. She adds rolled oats, chia seeds, fresh lemon zest (grated directly into the pan), honey, and milk, then places the pan on an induction cooktop and whisks the mixture as it cooks and thickens. Separately, she prepares a topping by placing frozen raspberries in a bowl, adding lemon juice, chia seeds, and honey, then microwaving them until they become a jam-like compote. Once the oatmeal is cooked, she transfers it to a decorative white and gold Louis Vuitton plate, spoons the warm raspberry compote onto one side, adds a dollop of FAGE Total 5% Greek yogurt in the center, sprinkles chopped pistachios over the top, and drizzles more honey. The video concludes with her taking a bite, closing her eyes, and placing a hand on her chest in apparent enjoyment.

18113947603846931.summary: A woman identified as Neha Panda, a 38-year-old costume stylist and actor, presents her personal daily food guide in an upbeat, direct-to-camera style. She introduces herself as 38 and walks through meals: morning empty-stomach soaked almonds and walnuts; breakfast options including Greek yogurt or coconut milk chia pudding, avocado toast with egg, boiled eggs, besan/moong dal cheela, and banana-egg oat pancakes; pre-workout choices like black coffee with MCT oil, oats with non-dairy milk, bananas, apple, peanut butter, or nuts; post-workout whey isolate with collagen, creatine, blueberries, or rice cakes with milk; lunch options such as ragi roti with sabzi, soybean rice, fish curry, palak paneer, veggie pasta, and chole rice; dinner options including rice paper rolls, quinoa salad, sweet potato with protein, rice noodles, grilled chicken/fish, and North Eastern-style chicken; and desserts like dark chocolate, mango, raspberries, and sugar-free Greek yogurt cocoa mousse. She adds hydration advice (2.5-3 liters water) and daily goals prioritizing protein, vegetables, healthy fats, and workout-timed carbs. The tone is instructional and promotional of a wellness lifestyle, ending with a call to follow for more.

18042141866800992.summary: A cooking creator demonstrates how to make "High-Protein Veggie Tofu Rotis" as a healthier alternative to regular rotis. The video opens with finished golden-brown rotis speckled with vegetables and seeds on a white plate, served with small bowls of white yogurt and bright pink pickled cabbage. The creator then shows the step-by-step process: steaming broccoli florets and sliced carrots, then blending them in a food processor with tofu, fresh spinach, and cilantro into a coarse green mixture. This is transferred to a wooden bowl where whole wheat flour (atta), chickpea flour (besan), flaxseed powder, chili flakes, turmeric, other spices, and yogurt are added. The creator kneads everything by hand into a soft, colorful dough, portions it, rolls it flat on a wooden board while sprinkling seeds on top, and cooks it on a hot cast-iron tawa until browned. The final shots show stacking the cooked rotis and the creator folding one with the toppings and taking a bite, giving an "OK" gesture. On-screen text and the caption emphasize the nutritional benefit — approximately 57g protein per batch, 8-10g per roti — and encourage viewers to save the recipe. The tone is upbeat, instructional, and food-focused, set to energetic background music.

18130697050622827.summary: A woman with long dark hair, wearing a white floral shirt, presents a homemade "Carrot Milk" as "A warm hug in a cup!" She holds up a ceramic mug filled with an orange-colored drink topped with chopped pistachios. The video then demonstrates the recipe step-by-step: steamed chopped carrots are placed in a blender jar with date syrup and milk, blended into a smooth puree, then transferred to a saucepan with additional milk and saffron strands. The mixture is heated on a gas stove, cardamom powder is added and whisked in, and the finished hot drink is poured into the mug and garnished. On-screen text and the caption describe it as a healthy, no-refined-sugar recipe for a rainy day. The overall tone is cozy, comforting, and instructional, set to a soft romantic background song. The creator is identified as @sprinkle.some.green, posting a healthy global recipe.

18091660874118526.summary: A woman identified as Neha (@greensoverguilt) from Bengaluru presents a POV-style kitchen video titled 'You ask for a snack in my home ft. my 15 clean snacks.' Set to an upbeat Hindi pop song, she opens containers on her black countertop and sequentially showcases 15 homemade snacks with on-screen labels: 1. High-Protein Chocolate Bites, 2. Makhana Namkeen Mix, 3. High-Protein Granola Bars, 4. Crunchy Chickpeas, 5. Coconut Cookies, 6. High-Protein Pizza (no bread), 7. Oats Cookies, 8. Mint Makhana, 9. Blueberry-Chocolate Pudding, 10. Oats Cupcakes, 11. Sweet Potato Chaat, 12. Mango-Yogurt Snack, 13. Paneer Cheese Toast, 14. Chana Jor Garam, and 15. Fruit Salad Bowl. Each item is shown in close-up as she handles, breaks, or serves it. The tone is cheerful, instructional, and promotional of a healthy, high-protein, clean-eating lifestyle for busy professionals. The caption encourages viewers to comment 'Details' for a recipe PDF via DM, indicating standard social-media engagement bait.

17893322382540210.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted in June 2026 by creator @theglampan (Chandana) from Michigan, USA. The video demonstrates how to make "Clean Almond Pistachio Biscuits" marketed as grain-free, starch-free, and healthy. It opens with a hand holding a finished rectangular biscuit topped with chopped pistachios, with on-screen text calling it "The healthiest biscuit you'll ever make." The process is shown step-by-step: almond flour is placed in a glass dish, followed by chopped pistachios, cardamom powder, melted ghee, and honey or maple syrup. The ingredients are mixed into a dough, shaped into rounds and rectangles on parchment paper, pressed with a fork, topped with more pistachios, and baked in an oven at 350°F (180°C) for 12-14 minutes. The final shots return to the baked biscuits on a wooden board. The tone is calm, instructional, and wholesome, accompanied by gentle instrumental flute music, with no dialogue. The caption provides the full ingredient list and instructions and encourages followers for more clean-eating recipes.

18006163106929099.summary: In a kitchen setting, creator Josie Li (@jos13_37) presents her 'default Chinese grocery run' focused on foods she uses for hair density, a nourished glow, and stable energy. She displays five staples: organic tremella (white fungus), which she calls a 'full-body hydrating mask'; a pre-ground black powder containing black sesame, black beans, black rice, mulberry, black goji berries, and yam for hair follicle nutrition; fermented glutinous rice (sweet rice wine) for gut health and quick energy; lotus root starch for replenishing iron and coating the stomach; and raw Chinese brown sugar for cramps and poor circulation. The video intercuts her speaking directly to camera with close-ups of preparing soups, porridges, and drinks using these ingredients, including chopping tremella, blending the black mix, and adding brown sugar to simmering pots. The tone is educational and personal-wellness oriented, framed as traditional Chinese medicine food-as-medicine practice.

17920336545161512.summary: A woman with long dark curly hair, identified as Shereen Helly (@simply_sherryx) in San Francisco, presents Episode 5 of her 'Blue Zone Bites' series, making a Coconut Miso Dumpling Soup. Speaking directly to camera, she frames the recipe around longevity diets in places like Okinawa, emphasizing simple, traditional ingredients—broth, vegetables, tofu, fermented foods—rather than trendy wellness marketing. Visually, she chops shallot, ginger, and garlic, tears bok choy, cubes tofu, and pan-fries frozen chicken dumplings. She then sautés aromatics in sesame oil, adds bok choy, gochujang for heat, pours in broth and coconut milk, stirs in miso, and simmers with tofu and dumplings. The finished orange-colored soup is ladled into a light blue bowl, topped with chili crisp and sesame seeds. She tastes it, smiles, and encourages viewers to follow for more Blue Zone bites. The tone is cozy, educational, and wellness-oriented, with on-screen text reinforcing the ingredients and health messaging.

17998112468948532.summary: This is a "what I eat in a day" food vlog posted May 2, 2026 by creator Nilani D (@nilanidurai), who frames her day around prioritizing whole foods and high protein. The video opens with finished plates, then walks through preparation. For breakfast, she makes fluffy folded scrambled eggs, serves them with avocado toast topped with spinach, salt, pepper, chili oil, honey, and chili oil, plus orange slices and a masala tea made with toasted spices and coconut kefir for gut health. For lunch, she cooks pre-marinated chipotle chicken thighs, then assembles a bowl with white rice, sliced chicken, and a fresh pineapple salsa made from diced pineapple, avocado, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, lime juice, salt, and pepper. For dinner, she sautés broccoli and red bell peppers with salt and red bell pepper seasoning, then pan-sears a salmon fillet seasoned with salt, pepper, chili, and garlic powder. She makes a hot honey sauce in the same pan with grated garlic, honey, soy sauce, white vinegar, and chili flakes, coats the salmon, and finishes the plate with sesame seeds. The tone is instructional, positive, and health-focused, with on-screen text reinforcing recipes and meal prep tips.

18094626242239836.summary: This is an overhead cooking video posted May 28, 2026 by Cloie (@nourishment.nutrition), a registered dietitian in Utah. The video demonstrates 'what I ate for dinner & why as a dietitian,' building a balanced bowl step-by-step. She spoons cilantro lime rice onto a white plate, adds taco-seasoned shrimp for protein, then mango salsa, black beans, and sliced avocado for fiber and micronutrients, finishing with a drizzle of Greek yogurt cilantro lime crema for healthy fats. On-screen text reads 'WHAT I ATE FOR DINNER & WHY as a dietitian' and later 'HOW TO BUILD A BALANCED MEAL in the caption.' The voiceover explains the nutritional rationale for each component — carbohydrates, protein, fiber, healthy fats — and notes the meal was inspired by finding juicy mangoes at the store. The caption provides full recipes for the rice, crema, shrimp, and salsa, and invites followers to comment for an ebook link. The overall tone is educational, upbeat, and practical, aimed at teaching simple meal-building principles.

18067683077397733.summary: This video is a detailed, visually rich cooking tutorial for Kangachi Nevri (also called Kangachyo Nevryo or Ratalyachi Karanji), a traditional Goan sweet potato dumpling associated with festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali. Set to traditional Indian vocal music, the video opens with the finished golden-brown crescent dumplings served on a banana leaf. It then walks through the full process: red-skinned sweet potatoes are boiled, peeled, and pressed through a ricer into a strawberry-patterned bowl. Whole wheat flour and salt are mixed in to form a soft dough, which is divided into small balls. Separately, organic cow ghee is heated and used to cook a filling of grated coconut, jaggery, cardamom, and poppy seeds until caramelized. On a greased banana leaf, a dough ball is flattened by hand, filled with the coconut mixture, folded into a half-moon shape using the leaf, and sealed. The dumpling is then shallow-fried on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp and golden on both sides. The final shot displays two cooked nevris on a banana leaf beside a jar of Akshayakalpa Organic Cow Ghee. The tone is calm, instructional, and celebratory of sustainable, heritage cooking.

18327559480254543.summary: The video is a social media recipe tutorial by creator Kridha Singh (@kridhasingh15), a dietitian mom based in Delhi, India, posted July 2, 2026. It opens with her 11-month-old daughter in a car seat, with on-screen text promoting 'THE ULTIMATE TRAVEL-FRIENDLY FOOD! HIGH-PROTEIN QUINOA & PUMPKIN COINS.' The tutorial demonstrates making the coins: soaked quinoa is placed in a bowl, followed by steamed pumpkin (described as keeping digestion smooth), black pepper, water for consistency, and garlic, then blended into a smooth paste. Homemade paneer is stirred in, and the mixture is spooned onto a hot iron tawa with desi ghee to pan-sear into small golden coins. Text emphasizes 'QUINOA + PANEER = COMPLETE PROTEIN TO KEEP THEM FULL!' The finished coins are packed into a stainless steel container with a pink lid, noted as staying soft for hours and '100% MESS-FREE!' The video closes back on the baby eating the coin, with text stating it's 'PERFECT FOR FLIGHTS, CAR SEATS, OR STROLLERS.' The tone is nurturing, instructional, and promotional, ending with a CTA to comment or DM for a slot in her program.

18126358750628165.summary: This is a short-form social media video by Australian-based Indian creator Deepika Gill (@veerkimummy), who identifies as studying infant nutrition at Deakin University. The video presents '7 Finger Foods I rotate for my 11 month old' as quick and easy recipes. Visually, it opens with a pot on a stove where a spoon adds a powder to a yellow mixture, then cycles through seven stainless steel divided plates held over a wood floor: 1) Sweet Potato Tikkis with kiwi and green puree, 2) Avocado Toast cubes with banana and avocado mash, 3) Veggie Uttapam with a pink dip and grain side, 4) Rajma Pancakes with red sauce and white yogurt, 5) Veggie Chilla with white dip, 6) Boiled Egg Tikkis with scrambled egg and green mash, and 7) Egg Muffins with watermelon and sweet potato wedges. On-screen text labels each item. The audio throughout is a soft female vocal lullaby singing about a baby boy. The caption promotes saving the video for meal inspiration and uses comment-to-DM calls to action ('FOOD' for recipes, 'BABY' for age-appropriateness). The overall tone is nurturing, instructional, and family-friendly, aimed at parents of infants.

18116818987834260.summary: In a bright commercial bakery kitchen with stainless steel tables, refrigerators, and mixers visible in the background, a man wearing glasses, a dark blue shirt, a patterned bandana, and a white 'Sensible Bakery' apron speaks directly to the camera while holding a black spatula. Over the course of the video he rapidly lists his core baking principles as yellow on-screen text appears with each point. He advises to never use unsalted butter, to bake by weight not volume, to avoid using same-day batter and instead use second-day batter, that baking soda needs an acid while baking powder works alone, to stop mixing once flour disappears, to always bloom cocoa powder, and explains how butter temperature affects texture—cold for flaky, soft for tender, melted for chewy. He states cookies should be baked over 375 degrees, to hydrate batters overnight especially for gluten-free, to brown butter and nuts for more flavor, that psyllium husk acts as gluten for gluten-free baking, that salt and vinegar enhance all flavors, that room-temperature ingredients work better, and defines sugar as moisture, protein and starch as structure, and fat as texture. He also recommends blooming cinnamon, using internal thermometers instead of toothpicks for doneness, starting at 350 degrees for any bake, and concludes by telling viewers to slow down and enjoy the process.

18056364977742644.summary: This is a faceless, slow-living cooking reel demonstrating how to make Dahi Phulki, presented as a forgotten Indian summer food. The video opens with text stating "A forgotten Indian summer food people need to bring back" over blurred shots of the finished dish. The creator prepares a soaked moong dal paste seasoned with salt, cumin, coriander, red chili powder, turmeric, and Eno fruit salt, then spoons small dollops onto an oiled metal plate to steam. After steaming, the yellow phulkis are soaked for 10 minutes in salted boiled water, then gently squeezed dry. Separately, buttermilk is prepared with fresh coriander, mint, and soaked whole red chili paste, topped with cumin powder. The squeezed phulkis are dumped into the cold spiced buttermilk and mixed. The final presentation shows the light, airy dumplings served cold in a white bowl, described as perfect for hot summer afternoons. The entire process is set to a continuous traditional Hindi folk song, and the tone is calm, comforting, and instructional, emphasizing home cooking and seasonal refreshment.

17910753156390626.summary: This is a calm, instructional cooking video posted by Melbourne-based creative director and food stylist Kirsten Jenkins (@kirstenljenkins) showing how to make chicken and mushroom congee. The video opens with finished bowls of creamy porridge topped with shredded chicken, mushrooms, soy sauce, chili oil, spring onions, and black sesame seeds. It then details the process: slicing ginger, cutting spring onions, halving a garlic bulb, and placing a whole chicken in a pot with these aromatics plus shallots. Water and fish sauce are added, and the chicken simmers for hours. After cooking, the chicken is removed, the broth is strained, and the meat is hand-shredded while soft garlic is squeezed from its skin. In a separate pot, rice is cooked in the broth until thick, then mixed mushrooms and the shredded chicken are stirred in. The final dish is served and garnished. The creator is shown eating the congee at a wooden table, smiling. The tone is soothing and "food for the soul," with no dialogue, focusing purely on the tactile, comforting preparation of the meal.

18194008150371520.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video posted June 6, 2026 by creator Aathira Sethumadhavan (@aathirasethumadhavan), identified as a chef and certified nutritionist. The video demonstrates how to make 'Kanthari Paneer,' a Kerala-style creamy curry. Visually, a hand adds chopped coriander to a finished yellow coconut-milk gravy with paneer cubes, then stirs and serves it with bread. The step-by-step process is shown: heating coconut oil, adding fennel seeds, sliced shallots, curry leaves, then a crushed paste of kanthari (bird's eye) chilies, ginger, and garlic. Turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, and salt are added, followed by coconut milk and a pinch of sugar. Cubed high-protein paneer is gently mixed in and simmered for 3-4 minutes, then finished with coriander leaves. The narrator explains the cultural context of a Malayali-Punjabi household and frames the dish as a quick, 20-minute comfort food that works with paneer, chicken, prawns, or egg, suitable with rice, roti, appam, dosa, or bread. On-screen text lists approximate macros (~245 cal, 15g protein per serving).

17907331716422811.summary: A woman identified as Raquel, a former midwife who creates content under @raquels.pantry, presents her 'Microbiome Monday' series focused on turning research into simple meals. She revisits her viral probiotic piña colada recipe, which she says was one of her first posts and immediately got 80,000 views, indicating audience interest in probiotics and pineapple. The video shows close-ups of her preparing the drink: cutting a fresh pineapple, adding chunks to a blender with soy kefir, coconut water, lime juice and zest, and a pinch of salt. She blends it and pours the thick, creamy yellow mixture over ice in a glass jar, letting it overflow. Throughout, on-screen text and her voiceover describe it as ultra-creamy, refreshing, packed with live cultures and bromelain, and 'the most fun thing your gut bacteria have been invited to.' The caption reinforces the health angle, calling it the 'probiotic piña colada that started everything' and tagging women's health, gut health, and iron deficiency. The overall tone is upbeat, instructional, and wellness-focused.

18098840956978971.summary: A woman demonstrates how to make mutton paya (goat trotters) broth as a natural collagen source. The video opens with her showing the finished product: a bright yellow-green broth that has set into a firm, jiggly, amber gelatin, which she squeezes between her fingers. She then heats a portion in a pan, adds salt, pepper, and spices, and drinks it from a glass, speaking in Telugu about its benefits. The tutorial portion shows the full process: cleaning chopped trotters, boiling them briefly with Kirkland apple cider vinegar to remove impurities, draining, then placing them in a white Bella slow cooker. She adds water, chopped carrots, red onion, garlic, celery, bay leaves, cumin seeds, turmeric, and more apple cider vinegar, stirs, and sets the cooker to low for 20-24 hours. After cooking, the broth is dark and rich with softened meat and vegetables, which she strains. The caption lists ingredients and steps, branding it as 'liquid collagen gold' for skincare and lifestyle, posted by @smalltowngirl_isha in April 2026.

18580245538054514.summary: This video is a short, engaging food documentary that introduces the viewer to 'Marag,' a rich and creamy mutton soup from Hyderabad, India. It begins with a passionate narration that provides the cultural and historical context of the dish, explaining its origins as a fusion of Arab and Hyderabadi culinary traditions under the Nizams. The video then transitions into a clear, step-by-step cooking demonstration, showing the preparation of the soup from sautéing onions to pressure cooking the mutton and finally combining it with yogurt, saffron, and herbs. The overall tone is warm, inviting, and celebratory, aiming to educate and inspire viewers to try this traditional and luxurious dish.

18317368618287716.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video demonstrating how to make Sri Lankan Miris Wadai, also called Mirchi Vada. The creator, speaking in Hindi with English terms, narrates a recent trip to Sri Lanka where a local guide introduced the spicy snack. The video shows the full recipe process: soaking moong dal, grinding it with garlic and ginger, whipping the paste until light, then mixing in reserved dal, semolina, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, chili flakes, dried fenugreek, garam masala, crushed coriander seeds, cumin, and fresh coriander. After resting, chopped onions are added. The mixture is shaped around whole green chilies, coated completely, and deep-fried in hot oil until golden and crispy. Finished vadas are served on a metal plate with newspaper lining, accompanied by red chili powder and green chutney. Interspersed are travel clips of Sri Lankan beaches, surfboards, street scenes, and a bakery display showing similar fried snacks priced at Rs. 50. The tone is enthusiastic and instructional, aimed at challenging viewers' spice tolerance.

18058764974709538.summary: A male Indian food creator demonstrates how to make a viral 'Ema Datshi Eggs' recipe, described as creamy, cheesy, spicy eggs inspired by Bhutan's iconic chili-cheese comfort food. The video opens with ingredients laid out: eggs, cheese slices, green chilies, and garlic. He melts butter in a pan, sautés garlic and chilies, adds water, then melts cheese into a sauce, seasoning it. In a separate pan, he fries several sunny-side-up eggs. He pours the hot cheese-chili mixture over the frying eggs, lets it cook together, then plates the combination onto grilled toast and drizzles chili oil on top. Throughout, on-screen text narrates his internal monologue about judging viral recipes before trying them due to ego or creator syndrome, concluding that this simple dish works because it hits a basic craving at the right time. He tastes the finished toast, smiles, gives a thumbs up, and confirms the hype is deserved.

18255760258291009.summary: A nutritionist dad (@burhan_ah) demonstrates how he makes bone broth from scratch for his 7-month-old daughter. The video opens with a spoonful of thick, gelatinous amber broth, then shows him chopping carrots and celery on a wooden board. He explains the broth provides collagen and calcium for strong bones and teeth and supports digestion. He uses leftover roasted bones from making her "whipped marrow," placing them into a Bosch slow cooker. He adds the chopped vegetables, covers everything with water, and adds apple cider vinegar to help break down collagen. After cooking low and slow for 36 hours, he lifts the lid to show the finished broth, strains it, and pours it into small glass jars for the freezer. He notes the broth is ideal for mixing into her purees and main meals like soup, ending with a shot of a prepared bowl and a call to like and follow for more recipes.

18071207564288389.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating a recipe for 'New Crispy Eggs Obsession.' A person's hands place piles of shredded mozzarella into a hot non-stick pan, then top each with a halved hard-boiled egg (yolk side down). After the cheese crisps and turns golden brown, the egg-cheese rounds are lifted and assembled on a slice of toasted sourdough bread layered with sliced avocado. The dish is finished by drizzling Marion's Kitchen Crispy Chilli Oil over the top and sprinkling finely chopped chives. On-screen text reads 'New Crispy Eggs Obsession.' The video has an upbeat, modern pop song with female vocals playing in the background. The overall tone is clean, instructional, and appetizing, focused solely on food preparation with no dialogue, jokes, or controversial content.

17988813503990627.summary: This is a cooking reel by home chef Vritta Sawhney (@snapsfromkitchen) demonstrating how to make Masala Bati using moong dal. The video opens with the finished dish: golden-brown spiral-shaped bati served on a white plate with moong dal, red chutney, onion and green chili. The preparation begins with soaked moong dal being ground into a paste, then transferred to a bowl. Spices are added sequentially: salt, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, asafoetida, crushed coriander seeds, crushed fennel (saunf), chopped green chili, and fresh coriander leaves. Desi ghee and sesame seeds are mixed in, followed by wheat flour to form a dough, which is kneaded smooth. The dough is rolled into a thin sheet, brushed with ghee, dusted with flour, folded, rolled again, and cut into small portions. Each portion is shaped into a round ball with a visible spiral pattern and placed in a multi-cavity appe pan. The bati are cooked until golden brown and slightly charred on top. Throughout, upbeat devotional music plays in the background. The tone is warm, instructional, and focused on comfort food, presented as a healthy, protein-rich Indian vegetarian recipe.

18091468616194107.summary: A cooking video by creator Sarah Bond (@liveeatlearn), who identifies herself as a nutritionist and sensory scientist, demonstrates her refined black bean burger recipe. The video opens with a close-up of a finished double cheeseburger with sauce, pickles, tomato and lettuce, captioned 'me when I find black beans in the pantry.' She then shows the process: draining and rinsing two cans of black beans, patting them dry, finely chopping green bell pepper, onion and garlic in a food processor, draining excess liquid, combining the vegetable mix with the beans and spices (salt, paprika, cumin, etc.), pulsing to blend, transferring to a bowl, adding panko breadcrumbs and an egg (with gluten-free and flax-egg substitutions noted), mixing, scooping and shaping into patties, chilling, then cooking in a cast-iron skillet until browned and topped with melted cheddar cheese. The final shots show assembly and holding the completed burger. The tone is upbeat, instructional, and promotional for her website, encouraging viewers to try the 'classic vegetarian recipe' and comment for the recipe link.

17918612796161273.summary: Creator Terrance Coleman presents his 'iconic Coconut Chilean Sea Bass' recipe in a kitchen setting in Chicago. The video opens with the finished baked dish in a white Staub baking dish, showing two fillets covered in a vibrant green herb-coconut sauce with browned edges. He then demonstrates the process: pouring coconut milk into a food processor, adding garlic, fresh cilantro, scallions, onion, and lime juice, and blending into a creamy green sauce. Raw sea bass fillets are placed in the oiled dish, seasoned with oil and black pepper, then smothered with the sauce before baking. After baking, he plates a portion on a green plate alongside rice and drizzles a red chili oil on top. The audio explains he returned from traveling ('jet-setting') and wanted something festive but quick, claiming it took less than 30 minutes and is one of the most delicious dinners he's made. The caption directs viewers to the full recipe on Substack.

18081207311570908.summary: A woman wearing a pink and purple floral top presents a cooking tutorial for "Weeknight Indian Chicken Kofta" dated April 23, 2026. Wearing a glove, she mixes everything thoroughly, then rolls the mixture into small round koftas with damp hands. The koftas are cooked in a pan until browned, plated, and sprinkled with fresh coriander. 17889710319510509.summary: This is Episode 10 of the #SweetSummerTreats series by Indian baker and cookbook author Shivesh Bhatia (@shivesh17). He begins by soaking whole almonds overnight, then peeling them and blending the peeled almonds with milk to form a thick paste. In a pot on the stove, he heats additional milk, adds sugar, saffron-infused milk, and a custard powder slurry, stirring until it thickens slightly. He then adds cardamom powder and the almond paste, followed by chopped almonds and pistachios. The finished creamy yellow drink is funneled into small glass bottles, chilled in a wooden bowl of ice, and presented by the smiling creator who takes a sip. 18404893189145498.summary: A woman in a white floral tank top demonstrates how to make crispy chicken bites in about 15 minutes. She soaks rice paper wrappers, places the seasoned chicken in the center, rolls them tightly, and cuts the long rolls into bite-sized pieces with scissors. The pieces are placed in a GLEN air fryer basket, sprayed with oil, and cooked at 180 degrees for 15-20 minutes until crispy. She finishes by drizzling chili oil over the bites and eating them with evident enjoyment, calling them the "best thing I've made this week" and saying she "inhaled a bowl of this in just five minutes." The tone is upbeat, instructional, and focused on quick, addictive snack preparation.

17994665123917948.summary: This is a clean, overhead cooking video demonstrating how to make 'crispy chicken kafta smash tacos.' The mixture is spread thinly onto mini flour tortillas, then cooked chicken-side down in a hot skillet until golden and crispy before flipping. After cooking, six finished rounds are placed on a wire rack. 17916746547366876.summary: This is a short-form cooking video posted by @f5_flavours demonstrating how to make a crispy potato fry. The creator adds oil to a hot pan, adds the diced potatoes, salt, and a little water, and cooks for 5 minutes before turning off the heat. On-screen text reveals "The crispy secret? Turn off the stove for 5 mins in between." After the rest, turmeric is added, followed by chili powder and jeera (cumin) powder, and the mixture is fried on low flame until crisp. While the chicken cooks, she prepares a glaze in a pan with melted butter, chopped red chilies, chili oil, honey, lemon juice, black pepper, lemon zest, and fresh coriander, stirring until combined. The cooked skewers are plated in a blue bowl, drizzled with the glossy glaze, and garnished with herbs. She holds up the finished skewers, takes a bite, and reacts enthusiastically. 18134524126544084.summary: This is a fast-paced cooking tutorial for Chilli Garlic Prawn Rice, posted April 24, 2026 by creator Aathira Sethumadhavan (@aathirasethumadhavan), identified as a chef and certified nutritionist. The dish is finished off-heat with chopped coriander leaves and lemon juice, then served from a brass bowl. For Lunch 2, she roasts green beans, sweet potato, and red onion with oil, then portions sliced chicken over the vegetables. 18079012169540155.summary: This is a short-form cooking tutorial demonstrating how to make a high-protein spinach and tofu roti. The creator adds blocks of tofu to a food processor containing fresh spinach, blends them into a coarse green paste, then transfers the mixture to a bowl. She takes a portion, rolls it into a ball, flattens it by hand, and uses a wooden rolling pin on a wooden board to form a thin round flatbread. 18074190608442885.summary: This is a bright, instructional cooking video by creator Salonie Malkar (@buns_and_dosas) posted from Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad in May 2026, demonstrating her recipe for 'Steamed Podi Eggs.' Separately, she prepares podi by heating coconut oil in a pan, sautéing curry leaves and dry red chilies, then adding urad dal, chana dal, and sesame seeds, stirring until lightly golden. These roasted ingredients are transferred to a blender with salt, hing, and turmeric and ground into a fine yellow-brown powder. For assembly, she heats ghee in a clean pan, adds fresh curry leaves and the freshly made podi, then tosses in the demolded steamed eggs to coat them evenly. The dish is finished with chopped fresh coriander. On-screen text and voiceover emphasize that these are soft-steamed eggs shaped like idlis, coated in spicy podi, presented as an easy, flavorful breakfast. The tone is enthusiastic and appetizing, with no jokes, innuendo, or safety concerns.

18050707805760521.summary: In this 2026 social media cooking video, creator Shruthi (@urbanfarmie) addresses the common problem of buying a 12-pack of Costco croissants when you don't have a large family. Opening with the on-screen text 'This is what happens when Costco lets me make decisions unsupervised,' she presents the croissants as needing an 'exit strategy.' She demonstrates turning slightly stale croissants into a French toast bake: tearing the pastries into a baking dish, mixing eggs, milk, vanilla, and spices in a measuring cup, pouring the custard over, covering with foil, then later sprinkling brown sugar and baking until golden brown. She explains that stale croissants hold structure better than fresh ones. The finished dish is served on a plate with syrup, and she eats it while asking viewers what they bulk buy at Costco. The tone is warm, humorous, and practical, aimed at home cooks looking for a way to use up excess bakery items. No risky content is present.

18079918271158481.summary: A woman in a home kitchen demonstrates how to make salted honey and vanilla cookies. She portions the dough into 50g balls, places five per tray, bakes at 180°C for 14 minutes, taps the tray at 8 minutes to flatten bubbles, and reshapes the warm cookies with a ring cutter before sprinkling flake salt. The finished cookies are golden brown with crisp edges and soft centers. She tastes one on camera, expressing enjoyment. On-screen text reinforces the tips throughout. 18089463872018413.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make "easy & spicy peanut chilli oil maggie." Hot water is then poured over the mixture, which is stirred into a bubbling reddish-brown sauce. Cooked Maggi noodles are added to the pan, tossed to coat thoroughly, and finished with a garnish of cilantro. The final shot shows a spoon lifting the glossy, saucy noodles. On-screen text reads "easy & spicy peanut chilli oil maggie" throughout. The video is set to upbeat instrumental music with no spoken dialogue. The overall tone is instructional, appetizing, and promotional of a quick, flavorful noodle recipe.

18114882940773256.summary: The video presents a step-by-step visual guide to making Spiced Sattu Chaas, a traditional Indian summer drink. Everything goes in'. After closing the lid ('Pressure cook Walk away'), she opens it to reveal the cooked pasta ('OPEN LID. MAGIC INSIDE'), stirs, and tops with shredded cheese. She tastes the dish, reacts positively, and the final shot shows two plated servings with garlic bread and the text 'YUMM...'. 18523199380066040.summary: The video is a step-by-step guide to preparing a dish called 'Coconut Chilian Sea Bass'. The creator begins by pouring coconut milk into a food processor, then adds green onions and cilantro. She then seasons two fish fillets with olive oil and black pepper, pours the blended green sauce over them, and bakes the dish. In her kitchen wearing a striped apron, she prepares a homemade alternative for summer hydration. She peels and mashes ripe mangoes, explaining that heat causes loss of salt and water from the body, so juice is needed. She makes hot honey by infusing honey with chili flakes, then combines mango pulp, lime juice, hot honey, and ice in a shaker. She mixes as usual and states the result is rotis that stay soft for hours, not just minutes. 18091542842590124.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video by creator Raunak Sunder (@chefron.cooks) demonstrating how to make 'Chicken Chukauni,' presented as an easy post-work meal. The video includes on-screen text reinforcing the steps and ingredients, and the creator is shown tasting the final dish approvingly.

18099912557078915.summary: A young woman identified as MerBear (@merbearwithme) films a casual indoor video in 2026, speaking into a small lavalier microphone while seated against a plain wall with an air conditioner visible. She counts down five recommendations: 1) Lemon Pound Cake with glaze from AllRecipes.com, which she calls foolproof; 2) How to Make the Best Brownies by Broma Bakery, noting the special technique of microwaving butter and sugar first; 3) Any biscotti recipe from Sally's Baking Addiction, praising its customizability and saying plain biscotti is amazing; 4) Creme Caramel from Buzzfeed Tasty, described as really simple yet impressive-looking for guests; and 5) Hokkaido Milk Bread by The Flavor Bender, using the Tangzhong technique, which she calls the fluffiest bread due to milk and butter, rating it 10 out of 10. She closes by asking viewers to try the recipes and tell her if they work, mentioning she has 50 followers. The tone is enthusiastic, friendly, and instructional, focused entirely on baking tips.

18070930922303819.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video by creator Saloni Kukreja, who introduces herself and states her dream is to open an Asian-inspired cafe. 18102403474777628.summary: A woman wearing a dark hijab and long-sleeve top demonstrates how to make fluffy baked egg patties for weekly breakfast meal prep in a modern kitchen. After straining the mixture for smoothness, she pours it into a square baking pan, places the pan in a larger dish filled with hot water, covers with foil, and bakes it. Once cooled, she removes the solid yellow egg slab, cuts it into nine neat squares, and layers them with parchment paper in a glass storage container for the fridge or freezer. The video then shows two assembly ideas: building an English muffin sandwich with the egg patty, a sausage patty, arugula, and sauce; and making a breakfast burrito with the egg patty, avocado, bacon, and hash brown in a tortilla. The tone is calm, instructional, and practical, emphasizing convenience and texture, with on-screen text labeling "breakfast meal prep EGG PATTIES" throughout.

17921576013312141.summary: This is a short-form cooking video titled "Quick & Easy Peanut chilli oil noodles" by creator Saralein (@saral3in_), posted on April 26, 2026, from Zürich, Switzerland, and inspired by @vegscratchkitchen. 18120626122718031.summary: This video is a concise and visually appealing cooking tutorial that demonstrates how to prepare a Kathi roll using marinated tofu as the protein source. Filmed from overhead, the video shows a finished bowl of thick porridge topped with peanut butter swirls, a dollop of chocolate spread, and honey drizzle, with a hand with red nail polish scooping it to show texture. The voiceover explains the dish is delicious and addresses a common criticism that porridge is low in protein, stating this version provides around 20 grams of protein per portion plus good carbs from oats, making it ideal fuel for a busy morning. The preparation sequence shows milk poured into a pan, an egg cracked in, vanilla and honey added, then oats stirred in and cooked until thick, followed by mixing in Greek yogurt off the heat. The final dish is plated and topped. The tone is instructional, positive, and health-focused, presented as an easy nutritious breakfast recipe.

17995904885925061.summary: This is Episode 2 of 'Snack Time,' a cooking video demonstrating how to make Moong Malai Ladoo, presented by creators Sumit & Priyanka Kapoor (@dillifoodies). The video shows a step-by-step process: roasting split yellow moong dal in a hammered metal wok, cooling it, grinding it into a fine powder, then cooking the powder with ghee until fragrant. Milk cream is stirred in, followed by transferring the mixture to a bowl where crushed peanuts, whole roasted melon seeds, and powdered sugar are added. Melted ghee is poured over the mix, which is then hand-formed into small round ladoos. The finished sweets are placed in a lined brass container. The Hindi narration frames the recipe as a beloved homemade snack for kids and adults alike, evoking nostalgia for hostel life when students would bring tins of sweets from home and hide them to last more than a few days. The tone is warm, instructional, and family-oriented, emphasizing the ladoo's melt-in-the-mouth taste.

18100037267300130.summary: This video is a step-by-step tutorial on how to make a chana sattu porridge, a type of baby food. A woman, the main subject, narrates the recipe while demonstrating each step in her kitchen. She begins by explaining that she has been making this recipe for her baby since he was six months old and describes how delicious it is. The visual sequence follows her narration precisely: she adds ghee to a pan on the stove, then adds chana sattu powder, stirs the mixture as it cooks into a porridge, and finally pours the finished product into a bowl. She concludes by presenting the porridge and reminding viewers that the full details are available in the caption. The overall intent is to inform and assist parents looking for recipes for their infants.

18576514378012707.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make "healthy brownies" that are easy, flourless, and made with 8 ingredients. The creator, identified as Cori Samuel (@staybycorisamuel), prepares the recipe in a bright kitchen setting. The process begins with combining tahini and maple syrup in a white bowl, followed by cracking in two eggs and adding vanilla. After whisking, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt are incorporated, then melted chocolate chips are folded in to create a thick, glossy batter. The batter is poured into a parchment-lined glass baking dish, spread evenly, baked, and then removed. Once cooled, coarse sea salt is sprinkled on top before the slab is cut into squares. The final shots show the finished fudgy brownies being served—one piece topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream—and held up to display the texture. On-screen text reinforces the recipe attributes, and the accompanying caption provides the full ingredient list and instructions. The video has a warm, homey aesthetic with tulips in the background and upbeat instrumental music, presenting a simple, wholesome dessert tutorial with no controversial or risky content.

18137492395518782.summary: A woman identified in the caption as nutritionist Sonakshi Joshi demonstrates how to make "Yogurt mango chocolate bites" in her kitchen. She begins by whisking plain yogurt in a bowl, then adds diced fresh mango, chopped pistachios, and a drizzle of maple syrup, mixing everything together. She spoons small mounds of the mixture onto a plate and places them in the freezer to firm up. After freezing, she melts dark chocolate, dips each frozen cluster into the chocolate to coat it, and returns them to the freezer. Once set, she breaks the coated bites apart and holds one up to the camera, showing the creamy mango-pistachio interior inside the chocolate shell. She tastes the bite, reacts with enjoyment, and describes the snack as a seasonal summer treat with protein from yogurt, healthy fats from pistachios, natural sweetness from mango, and a little indulgence from dark chocolate. The video is presented as a simple, healthy recipe tutorial with no dialogue beyond the cooking narration.

18092299520184038.summary: This video is a recipe reveal for a French Orange Cake. It begins with the creator introducing the cake as a classic that has been baked in grandmothers' kitchens and fills Parisian bakeries with its scent. The creator emphasizes that this version is gluten-free, dairy-free, and naturally sweetened, yet maintains an 'insanely soft' texture. The video then shows the steps of making the cake, including cracking eggs into a bowl and mixing in dry ingredients. The final product is presented as a moist, golden-brown loaf. The creator concludes by stating that the cake is more than just food, but a moment and a memory, and encourages viewers to enjoy the recipe and follow for more content.

18145424221431321.summary: A woman with long curly hair demonstrates how to make a high-protein vegan chocolate pudding in a bright kitchen setting. She begins by holding a banana, saying she would usually peel it but invites viewers not to judge her method. She places the unpeeled banana into a personal blender, adds cocoa powder and plant-based milk, blends the mixture, then transfers it to a small saucepan on the stove. While whisking, she explains this is part of her 'Eat More Plants' series aimed at adding more fiber and protein to plates without overthinking. After heating, she pours the smooth chocolate mixture into a decorative bowl, states it should set in the fridge overnight, and later inverts it onto a plate to reveal a firm dome-shaped pudding. She tastes it, expresses surprise that it works, and presents the finished dessert garnished with sliced strawberries and cocoa powder. On-screen text highlights its nutrition: approximately 16g protein, 8g fiber, and 4 plant points per serving. The tone is friendly, educational, and enthusiastic, focused on simple plant-based nutrition.

17916754563144964.summary: This is a short-form cooking video demonstrating how to make "Healthier Banana Bread" that is labeled as gluten-free and refined sugar free. The creator, a woman with blonde hair wearing a navy zip-up top, narrates the process while showing each step. The video opens with the finished loaf topped with chocolate chips, then shows it being sliced. The preparation begins with mashing ripe bananas in a large white bowl, followed by adding two eggs, Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, and olive oil, which are mixed together. Dry ingredients are then incorporated: almond flour, oat flour, cinnamon, and baking powder. Dark chocolate chunks are folded into the batter. The mixture is poured into a parchment-lined loaf pan, topped with additional chocolate chips, and placed in the oven to bake for about 45 minutes. The final shot shows the baked loaf being removed from the oven. The on-screen text and caption promote the recipe as a yummy, moist dessert naturally sweetened with bananas and containing healthy fats, and advertise the creator's ebooks with 265 recipes. The tone is bright, instructional, and promotional.

17986930913975912.summary: The video opens with a title card 'CHAAT DIARIES - EVERY BITE TAKES YOU HOME' over a plated sev puri being held up. Text warns 'Stop – you're making sev puri wrong' as a hand adds toppings. The creator then prepares two chutneys. For the green chutney, she adds fresh cilantro, mint, green chilies, ginger, garlic, spices, grated ginger, and lemon juice into a small blender jar and blends it into a smooth vibrant green paste, described as non-optional for freshness. For the red chutney, she soaks dried red chilies with garlic, then blends them with sev, tamarind water, and spices into a thick reddish-brown sauce, called the game changer for bold, garlicky, spicy punch. Assembly begins with placing round fried puris on a white scalloped plate. She tops each with mashed potato, sprinkles red chili powder, adds diced tomatoes and chopped red onions, then spoons both red and green chutneys onto each puri. The dish is finished with a generous shower of sev, boondi, and fresh cilantro leaves. The final shot shows a hand holding up a completed sev puri. Throughout, on-screen text and voiceover frame sev puri as nostalgia, not just food, recalling college bunking, Juhu Beach breezes, and carefree moments with friends, ending with a call to comment 'Sev Puri' for the recipe and to save, share, and follow.

17968689780013370.summary: This video is a social media recipe tutorial for making cookies. It begins with a woman walking down the stairs of her home, setting the scene for a 'Sunday Baking' theme. She proceeds to the kitchen, where she retrieves ingredients such as almond flour, almonds, baking powder, maple syrup, and milk. The video provides a clear, step-by-step visual guide to the entire process, from chopping the almonds and mixing the dough to shaping the cookies and baking them in the oven. The video concludes with the woman sharing the freshly baked cookies with a young boy. The entire video is set to an upbeat, electronic dance track that is unrelated to the visual content, serving as generic background music to make the video more engaging.

17950539204121134.summary: This is a cooking reel by creator @mykitchennndiary titled "Easy Lunchbox Ideas - Healthy & Delicious," posted April 3, 2026. The video demonstrates how to make moong dal and lauki (bottle gourd) vegetable patties. It opens with the finished dish: golden-brown round patties topped with sesame seeds, served on a steel thali with orange chutney and a piece of sweet. The process shows soaking 1/2 cup moong dal, then grinding it with green chili and garlic. Lauki is peeled and grated, then mixed with chopped onion, shimla mirch (capsicum), grated carrot, and chopped beans. Spices added include turmeric powder, red chili flakes, chaat masala, cumin, and salt, followed by 1/2 cup suji (semolina), 1/4 cup curd, and fresh coriander. Baking soda is mixed in last. The batter is spooned into hot oil in a pan with white sesame seeds and mustard seeds, fried until crisp on both sides. The tone is instructional and appetizing, set to upbeat Hindi music. Trust and safety analysis finds no jokes, innuendo, or policy-risk content; the video is suitable for all ages.

17972961710863221.summary: This video is a step-by-step tutorial on how to make healthy almond bites. It begins with the creator presenting the finished product, which are small, rectangular baked goods studded with chopped almonds and chocolate chips. The video then shows the process of making the bites, starting with cracking an egg into a bowl. The creator whisks the egg, adds flour, and mixes in chocolate chips to create a thick batter. The batter is then poured into a gray silicone mold, and the creator adds more chocolate chips and chopped hazelnuts on top. The final scene shows the filled mold on a wooden board, ready for baking. The video is shot in a bright, well-lit kitchen, with a focus on the hands and the food, creating a clean and inviting aesthetic. The overall tone is informative and instructional, guiding the viewer through each step of the recipe.

18032196581792183.summary: This is a bright, upbeat cooking reel demonstrating how to make melt-in-your-mouth besan laddus. It opens with a finished plate of golden-brown laddus topped with chopped pistachios and the text 'POV: guests are coming but you already ate 3,' establishing a playful, indulgent tone. The creator then walks through the recipe step-by-step: 2 cups besan is mixed with 2 tbsp ghee and 2 tbsp milk until crumbly, then sieved. Half a cup of Anveshan Gir Cow Ghee is heated in a pan, the sieved mixture is added and cooked on low flame for 15-20 minutes until it turns soft, aromatic, and caramel-colored. The hot mixture is transferred to a tray, 1 cup of sugar (boora) and cardamom powder are added, and everything is mixed by hand. The dough is rolled into smooth balls, arranged on a black plate, and garnished with pistachios. Throughout, the video features traditional Indian instrumental music and promotes the Anveshan ghee brand with a discount code (SADHNA18). The overall presentation is clean, appetizing, and family-friendly, focused entirely on food preparation.

18095200199031663.summary: A woman in a home kitchen presents a recipe for an iron-rich dessert she calls aleev-subja pudding, positioning it as healthier than chia pudding. She shows the two main seeds - reddish-brown aleev (halim) and black subja (sabja/basil) seeds - explaining aleev is a rich iron source and subja is cooling. She soaks the seeds, then cooks them in coconut milk in a brass pan, sweetening only with chopped dried dates (khareek) which she notes also add iron. While cooking, she states over 50% of Indian women are anemic and this traditional dish helps address that gap. After cooking to a pudding consistency, she spoons it into a glass, tops it with pomegranate arils and pumpkin seeds for vitamin C and texture, and tastes it. On-screen text and her narration emphasize moderation due to aleev being heating and heavy to digest, and advise consulting a doctor if pregnant. The tone is educational, warm, and focused on traditional Indian food culture.

18116616382659664.summary: The video is a step-by-step tutorial on how to prepare a high-protein meal using traditional Indian ingredients. The creator, a young woman, begins by introducing the meal, which consists of daal, roti, and yogurt. She then demonstrates how to make the roti dough by blending tofu with water and mixing it with atta flour. The dough is then rolled and cooked on a pan. The final scene shows the finished meal, with the roti drizzled with olive oil, and the creator explains that this meal provides 40 grams of protein. The video is informative and practical, with the creator providing a clear and concise explanation of the recipe and its nutritional value.

18345133411200699.summary: A woman in a kitchen setting presents a recipe for a protein and collagen ladoo. She holds up a jar of the finished product and then displays the three main ingredients: flax seeds, urad dal, and black sesame seeds. She explains the health benefits of each ingredient, such as reducing hair fall, strengthening hair follicles, and promoting collagen production for healthy skin and hair. The video concludes with her holding up the final ladoo, emphasizing its benefits.

17952290625051173.summary: This video is a step-by-step recipe demonstration for making 'Black Sesame Ladoo'. The creator, a woman named Person_A, begins by presenting the finished product to the camera, holding a white plate filled with the dark, round ladoos. She then proceeds to show the preparation process in a top-down view of a kitchen counter. She adds various ingredients into a stainless steel blender jar, including black sesame seeds, white sesame seeds, amaranth powder, dried ginger powder, cardamom powder, nigella seeds, date paste, and coconut oil. Each ingredient is clearly shown and identified with on-screen text. After all the ingredients are in the jar, she uses a spatula to mix them into a cohesive, dark paste. The final scene shows the finished black sesame ladoo stored in a glass jar. Throughout the video, the creator provides a voiceover explaining the recipe and its health benefits, such as being low glycemic, free of refined sugar and dairy, and suitable for specific health conditions. The overall message is to share a healthy and nutritious recipe with her audience.

17842792398687283.summary: The video is a Telugu-language cooking tutorial from creator 'iSmart Aishwarya Kitchen vlogs' demonstrating how to make 'Amla Laddu' (Indian gooseberry sweet balls). A woman in a yellow outfit prepares the mixture in a kitchen setting. She dry-roasts sesame seeds and grated coconut, then roasts chopped cashews, almonds, pistachios, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, and watermelon seeds in ghee, followed by chopped dates and raisins. Separately, she sautés grated fresh amla (gooseberry) in ghee, adds the roasted sesame-coconut powder, then melts palm jaggery into the mixture until thick. She combines the roasted nuts/seeds and spices (cardamom, dry ginger powder), mixes everything, cools slightly, and rolls into round laddus. Finished laddus are displayed on a brass plate lined with banana leaf. Throughout, on-screen text in English ('Cleanse, glow, and stay strong your daily health boost!') and Telugu promotes the laddu as a daily health booster for immunity, digestion, hair growth, skin glow, blood sugar control, and energy, claiming it treats 100 ailments. The tone is instructional and promotional, typical of Indian home-remedy food content.

17941160655031825.summary: This video is a step-by-step tutorial on how to make black sesame tea balls. It begins with the creator introducing the final product. She then proceeds to demonstrate each step of the recipe: first, she roasts two cups of organic black sesame seeds on a low heat until they become fragrant. Next, she blends the roasted seeds into a fine powder using a Vitamix blender. After transferring the powder to a bowl, she slowly incorporates two tablespoons of organic maple syrup to bind the mixture. Finally, she rolls the mixture into small, round balls. Throughout the video, she explains the health benefits of black sesame seeds, noting their content of protein, healthy fats, fiber, vitamins, minerals like calcium and zinc, and antioxidants. She also mentions that in traditional Chinese medicine, these seeds are believed to support liver and kidney health, which are organs linked to youthful hair, bones, and skin. The video concludes by showing her storing the finished tea balls in her freezer for convenience. The creator's friendly and informative tone, combined with the clear visuals, creates an engaging and trustworthy recipe guide.

17990461754755464.summary: This is a home cooking video demonstrating how to make '7 Seed's Laddo' labeled as No Sugar, No Flour, Kid's Friendly. The creator, identified as Sanskriti Singh (@maafoodtales), shows the finished dark round laddoos in containers, then walks through the process step-by-step. Seven types of seeds — pumpkin, melon, sunflower, poppy, sesame, flax, and chia — are dry-roasted together in a pan, ground into a coarse powder, and set aside. Peanuts and makhana (fox nuts) are separately roasted and ground. In a pan with ghee, chopped dates are cooked down into a paste. All the powders are combined in a large bowl with melted ghee and the date paste, mixed by hand until bindable, and rolled into balls. The Hindi voiceover explains the seasonal relevance during cold weather, emphasizes the seeds are sugar-free and good for children, and gives the ingredient amounts. The video ends with a child's voice interrupting, matching the caption's prompt not to miss the end. The overall tone is warm, educational, and family-oriented, focused on healthy traditional snacking.

18098277635313772.summary: The video is a short, user-generated content piece that serves as a recipe for 'white choc macadamia black sesame cookies'. The dough is then shaped into balls and placed on a baking sheet. The video concludes with the finished cookies, which are shown with a final layer of flaky sea salt. The creator then tastes one of the cookies, suggesting they are delicious. The entire video is accompanied by calm, instrumental music, creating a relaxing and enjoyable viewing experience.

17851746975645117.summary: This is a cooking tutorial video from creator Samayal with Sharon demonstrating how to make Vellarikai Thogayal, a South Indian cucumber chutney. The video shows a step-by-step process: roasting peanuts, coriander seeds, chana dal, urad dal, cumin, dried red chilies, green chilies, and sesame seeds in oil, then separately frying garlic, sliced cucumber, and red onion with turmeric and salt. The roasted spice mixture is ground in a black stone mortar, the cooked cucumber-onion is added and pounded together, then finished with chopped raw onion, cilantro, and a tempering of curry leaves in hot oil. The final thick, reddish-orange paste is mixed by hand and shown being served with white rice. The audio features a female narrator in Tamil explaining each ingredient and step enthusiastically. The tone is instructional, warm, and appetizing, aimed at home cooks looking for an easy vegetarian recipe.

17890831248435401.summary: This social media video presents a recipe for healthy protein balls in a concise and visually appealing manner. It opens with a trendy 'POV' meme-style text overlay that humorously captures the dilemma of wanting to indulge in dessert while also wanting to maintain a healthy lifestyle. The video then quickly transitions to a step-by-step visual guide, showing the ingredients being combined in a food processor and the final product being rolled in a mix of black and white sesame seeds. The creator, a woman in a modern kitchen, presents the finished product with a smile, and the video concludes with her tasting it. The entire process is set to an upbeat, generic electronic music track. The humor of the video lies in the ironic use of audio; it starts with a sound effect ('womp womp') that is commonly associated with failure, but is used here to frame a successful and positive outcome, creating a playful and relatable experience for the viewer.

18346641058226724.summary: The video is a short, self-recorded clip that begins with a close-up of a glass jar filled with greenish-brown, round food balls called 'laddoos'. The creator, a woman with long brown hair, appears and presents the laddoos, claiming they have been more effective for her hair than any hair serum she has ever tried. She then proceeds to demonstrate the recipe, showing the ingredients: black sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, walnuts, dates, moringa powder, and ghee. The video shows the process of dry-roasting the seeds and nuts, blending them, and mixing them with the other ingredients to form the final laddoo. The creator concludes by encouraging viewers to save the recipe, try making the laddoos themselves, and come back to share their results. The overall narrative is a personal testimonial that combines a recipe demonstration with a health tip, aiming to promote a simple, homemade solution for hair health.

18177453313377140.summary: The video is a recipe demonstration for eight different summer drinks that are free from refined sugar. The preparation process is shown in close-up shots, highlighting the ingredients and the pouring action. The video concludes with the speaker enjoying one of the purple drinks, showcasing the final product.

18111887320579379.summary: This video is a concise cooking tutorial demonstrating how to prepare a nutritious amaranth porridge. The narrator explains that this bowl offers more protein and fiber than an equivalent bowl of oats and promotes feelings of fullness. The video then transitions to the preparation process. It shows the ingredients being combined in a stainless steel pot: water, milk, cloves, amaranth, and cacao powder. The mixture is stirred and cooked until it reaches the desired consistency. Finally, more milk is added for creaminess, followed by honey for sweetness. The video concludes by showcasing the finished porridge, emphasizing its appealing texture and nutritional benefits.

17937782274177803.summary: This video is a short, engaging recipe reel for a healthy amaranth porridge. The creator, a woman in a brown crop top and jeans, presents the recipe in a friendly and informative manner. The video begins with a title card for 'Iron in Disguise,' a series that focuses on nutritious food. The creator explains that the amaranth porridge is an excellent source of iron, a nutrient that many women lack. She then demonstrates the recipe, starting with blending amaranth, dates, and water in a food processor. The mixture is cooked in a pot, and the video shows the preparation of a vibrant raspberry and blood orange compote. The final dish is presented in a light blue bowl, topped with the compote and pistachios. The creator encourages viewers to follow her for more recipes that are both delicious and beneficial for their health.

18103535647910442.summary: This video is a short, engaging recipe demonstration for a healthy amaranth porridge. The creator begins by introducing the main ingredient, amaranth, and highlights its nutritional benefits, such as being a complete plant protein and a rich source of iron. The video then proceeds to show the step-by-step process of making the porridge. It starts with blending the amaranth with milk, then cooking the mixture in a saucepan on a stove. The creator also shows how to make a quick blueberry compote to serve alongside the porridge. The video concludes with the finished dish being presented and eaten. Throughout the video, text overlays reinforce the health benefits and steps of the recipe. The overall narrative is informative and promotes healthy eating habits.

18124516798599873.summary: This video presents a recipe for 'No Sugar Sweet Potato Kheer'. It begins by showcasing the finished dessert in a white bowl, garnished with almonds and rose petals.
